# Decisions — v9 (Hybrid-AND, TLS authentication via two certificates, phase 1 local)

## 1. T1, reconnaissance: facts A, B, E and F confirmed in the current code; fact D does not reproduce in the official v8 data (clarified afterward, see note); fact C is deferred to Decision 2 (direct reading of the SAD)

**Fact A, confirmed.** `mock-service-os/mock_mtls/hybridVerification.go`,
`hybridVerifyPeerCertificateFunc()`/`verifyHybridClientCert()`: the
ML-DSA-65 signature verified in Hybrid-v8 is only the CA's signature
over the CLIENT certificate's preTBS (proof that the CA signed that
content, never proof of possession of the ML-DSA key performed by the
party connecting). The actual proof of possession during the TLS
handshake is RSA only (`CertificateVerify`). The SERVER certificate
never undergoes an equivalent check on the client side.

**Fact B, confirmed on both points.** `thesis/scripts/tls_kem_proxy/
main.go:212`: `InsecureSkipVerify: true` in the `upstreamTLSConfig`, for
the three v8 profiles, varying only the curve. `mock-service-os/certs/main.go`:
all certificate generation uses `ExtKeyUsageClientAuth`, including the
certificates used as the SERVER certificate (`mtls_pqc`,
`mtls_hybrid`); no occurrence of `ServerAuth` in the entire file.

**Fact D, investigated, clarified by Luciano (see his message).**
I recalculated from the official data of the 720 runs
(`consolidated_combined.json`) and confirmed that `term_handshake_pcap`
matches `term_handshake` (gateway) exactly across the three profiles, 0%
difference -- that is, the current pcap extractor (`pcap_utils.py`,
`extract_clean_handshake_bytes()`), even after the fix from Decision
85 of v8, does NOT exclude the first HTTP request in practice, because
its phase 3 consumes the entire segment in the same direction without
being able to distinguish, without a keylog, where the TLS 1.3
`Finished` ends (both come out as an encrypted 0x17 record on the
wire). Luciano confirmed that the values 4.945/22.373/18.783 B came from
a recalculation he did outside this repository, using a TCP segment
boundary heuristic (first client->server segment starting with 0x17
after the client's flight), valid in ~97-99.7% of connections but it is
an ESTIMATE, not official data. The official figure remains the
gateway's (5.179/22.607/19.017 B). Adjustment recorded for T6(d):
byte counting INSIDE the process (net.Conn summing bytes in both
directions, closing the count when `tls.Conn.Handshake()` returns, at
both the client proxy and the gateway), giving the exact boundary
without depending on pcap; keylog + full pcap remain as an independent
cross-validation.

**Fact E, confirmed, and explains fact D.** Without SSLKEYLOGFILE, no
handshake message after the ServerHello is distinguishable in the pcap,
by construction of TLS 1.3 (everything encrypted as the same external
record type). Snaplen 256 confirmed in `campaign_run.py`
(`TCPDUMP_SNAPLEN_BYTES`).

**Fact F, confirmed, already honestly documented in the current v8
final report.** Handshake residue above expectation: Section 6 of
`Consolidated_Metrics_Report_FINAL.md`, "not attributed," investigated
with no isolated cause identified with confidence. Residue of ~14% of
T_flow in the reference cell (240.1/260.3/253.9 ms, Classical/PQC/Hybrid):
same section, with the Hybrid's "HTTP calls" phase being the largest of
the three (410.7 ms), "partly residual, not fully attributed." Item
T6(f) of this plan attacks that point directly (per-call server time).

**Luciano's decisions D1-D6 and the AND mechanism specification**: no
contradiction with the current code. No patch or `dual.go` file exists
in this repository yet -- confirmed by search, nothing to reconcile, T3
implements it from scratch per the specification received.

**Scope confirmed for the upcoming tasks, with no blocker:** `certs/
main.go` (1.333 lines, generic functions reused by name) will need a
new function for the Hybrid-AND (two independent chains) in T4;
`mock_mtls/main.go` currently has a fixed `ClientAuth`
(`VerifyClientCertIfGiven`) for all profiles, which will become
profile-dependent in T5 (`RequireAndVerifyClientCert` only for
Hybrid-AND, D3). There is no Go installed locally in this environment,
but Docker (29.9.1) is available and working, with no blocker for T2.

No action on AWS, no terraform touched, no commit prior to this one.

## 3. T2, reproducible Go toolchain: go1.27.3 chosen and justified, build from official source succeeded, crypto/tls suite 100% green (214 PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 SKIP)

**Version chosen: go1.27.3** (not go1.27rc2, which v8 used, nor plain
go1.27.0). Three reasons, in order of weight:
1. rc2 is a release candidate, never promoted to stable -- v9 begins a
   more sensitive mechanism (forking `crypto/tls` itself), with no
   reason to start from a pre-release base when the final release
   exists.
2. go1.27.3 (released 2026-10-19, confirmed via search) includes a
   security fix in `crypto/x509` that rc2 does not have -- relevant
   because the AND mechanism depends directly on that package's chain
   verification.
3. It is the same version that Luciano's external reference patch has
   already been validated against, outside this repository -- it
   eliminates version drift between that validation and the
   reconstruction done here.

**Commit of the `go1.27.3` tag**, resolved via `git ls-remote --tags
https://go.googlesource.com/go go1.27.3` in this session:
`2aae1000ea1d4b28923b96db28acf4e3b99d6aff`. The `Dockerfile`
(`thesis/results/v9/toolchain/Dockerfile`) fails the build if the clone
resolves to a different commit.

**Base images, pinned by digest** (`docker pull`, resolved in this
session): `golang:1.27.3-alpine@sha256:
d200d2dd76b03a99b52651fd1325aff7dcd35422c35c01bac56571b0507f3deb`
(used only as the bootstrap compiler) and `alpine:3.24@sha256:
be2656061b536c1883c4034790e21d0a09c5aaaf51968b89368a3c0371ea2c9a`
(builder image).

**Pipeline**: clones `go.googlesource.com/go` fresh at tag `go1.27.3`
(does not reuse the bootstrap image's `/usr/local/go/src`, so that the
commit actually compiled is verifiable against the public tag); applies
`patches/and.patch` via `git apply` if the file is not empty (empty at
this stage -- no fork code exists yet, on purpose, this is the proof
that the pipeline works before T3 writes the real patch); runs
`./make.bash`; runs the `crypto/tls` package's test suite, unmodified.

**Real bug found and fixed in this session's own Dockerfile, before the
final result:** the first version did `go test | tee
file; echo "exit_code=$?"` -- `$?` after a pipe captures `tee`'s exit
code, not `go test`'s, so a failing test would NOT fail the build.
Fixed to `bash -o pipefail -c "go test |
tee file"`, which propagates `go test`'s actual exit code.
Necessary before T3, where real test failures need to be detected.

**Result, full `crypto/tls` suite, unmodified, against the freshly
compiled go1.27.3 toolchain:** `ok crypto/tls 48.969s` -- **214
PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 SKIP**. The container had real network access during
the build/test, so this result does not distinguish "the suite has no
test that needs internet" from "it needed it and the network was
available" -- recorded as an observation, not as a claim of
network-isolated testing.

Committed artifacts: `thesis/results/v9/toolchain/Dockerfile`,
`README.md`, `patches/and.patch` (empty, T3 placeholder),
`build_metadata.json`, `crypto_tls_test_summary.txt`.

## 4. Scope added by Luciano after the Fact C/T2 report (SAD, Section 3.4): stack divergence, TLS 1.3 limitation, interoperability matrix

**a) Declared stack divergence.** The SAD (Section 3.4, "EXPERIMENTAL
VALIDATION", PDF 31/printed 30) envisions the experimental environment
with "reference implementations of MLKEM and MLDSA made available by NIST...
integrated with open-source cryptographic libraries with support for
hybrid operations, namely OpenSSL and liboqs". v9 (like the entire
v1-v8 series before it) uses Go 1.27.3 with native ML-DSA-65 and
ML-KEM-1024 from the stdlib's own `crypto/tls`/`crypto/x509`/`crypto/mldsa`,
without OpenSSL or liboqs. Justification recorded: (1) this is the SAME
stack the whole project has already used for PQC/Hybrid since v6
(Tier 1) -- switching to OpenSSL+liboqs now would invalidate
comparability with v6-v8; (2) the AND mechanism requires forking
`crypto/tls` itself (ClientHello, CertificateRequest, Certificate
message, dual `CertificateVerify`) -- this is only feasible with access
to the TLS stack's source code, which Go's stdlib offers directly and
OpenSSL (a C library, binary API) would not offer without an
equivalent, more costly fork of OpenSSL itself; (3) Go 1.27 already has
native, tested ML-DSA-65/ML-KEM-1024 (confirmed in T2), eliminating the
external liboqs dependency that the SAD anticipated when it was written
(before these APIs existed in Go's stdlib). A real divergence from what
the SAD proposed, recorded here, not hidden.

**b) Declared limitation: TLS 1.3 only, not TLS 1.2/1.3.** The SAD
cites OPIN's data channel as "TLS 1.2/1.3" (PDF 12/printed 11). The AND
mechanism, per the specification received from Luciano itself, only
works over TLS 1.3 (the `signature_algorithms`/`CertificateRequest`
extended with code 0xFE65 and the dual `CertificateVerify` design have
no defined equivalent in TLS 1.2, and the specification's "known gaps"
list this explicitly: "no explicit TLS 1.2 rejection -- usage is TLS 1.3
minimum"). Recorded as an explicit limitation of the Hybrid-AND measured
in v9: it covers only the TLS 1.3 subset of what the SAD describes for
the OPIN channel, not the TLS 1.2 that the SAD also allows.

**c) Interoperability matrix -- checking what already exists before
implementing.** I searched `Consolidated_Metrics_Report_FINAL.md` and
v8's `DECISIONS.md` for any cross-profile interoperability measurement
(one profile's client against another profile's server). The only
existing finding is **PQC against a generic OpenSSL client**
(`thesis/results/v8/artifacts/pqc/openssl_interop_diagnosis.md`,
Section 2 of the final report) -- a configuration diagnosis (missing
the `-sigalgs` flag), not a matrix among the project's OWN profiles. v8
never tested Classical-client against PQC-server, or any other cross
combination: by design, the client (`tls_kem_proxy`) and the server
(`mock_mtls`) always use the SAME `CRYPTO_PROFILE` in every official
run. **Confirmed to Luciano: no cross-profile interoperability matrix
exists in any v8 data or report** -- this is genuinely new scope for
v9, implemented in T3/T4 as a local functional test (it does not enter
the official performance results), covering Classical, PQC, Hybrid-v8,
Hybrid-AND-non-strict, and Hybrid-AND-strict, per client x server pair,
with success/failure, reason, `DualAuthenticated` (indicates downgrade)
and the "effective AND protection: yes/no" column.

## 5. Strict mode and backward compatibility

**Strict is a per-pair policy, not a global protocol.** The mechanism
(client offers 0xFE65 alongside the classical schemes; server chooses
the dual pair if it has a PQ chain available) supports both
`Dual.Require=true` (strict) and `Dual.Require=false` (non-strict) --
T3's patch keeps both configurations, with no automatic fallback built
INTO the officially measured Hybrid-AND profile (which always runs
strict, per D3). The experiment measures only that profile, where every
participant is Hybrid-AND, so strict mode does not distort the official
metric -- it would only show up if the experiment tested a mixed pair,
which the interoperability matrix (Decision 4c) does deliberately,
outside the official performance results.

**Proposed transition model, aligned with the SAD (Section 3.2 and 3.4,
via Decision 2):** non-strict for a pair not yet migrated (the
connection is marked as lacking AND protection, via
`DualAuthenticated=false`); strict for a migrated pair; until strict
becomes the ecosystem's general rule. Logic similar to HSTS (trust on
first use / enforce once confirmed). **The trusted source for "this
pair has already migrated" (for example, a field in the OPIN
Participant Directory) is NOT implemented in v9** -- recorded here as
future work and a dependency on OPIN's own governance, without claiming
that the real Directory already has that field today (it does not, per
what the SAD describes).

**A classical participant against a strict server is refused by
design** -- which is exactly what the impostor test (below) and the
interoperability matrix demonstrate. The operational alternative (a
separate, non-strict endpoint to accept classical participants during
the transition) amounts to non-strict AT THAT SPECIFIC endpoint, and
must be described as such, never as "the strict server accepting
classical."

**Impostor test (evidence of why strict mode is mandatory) -- result in
Decision 6 (T3).**

**What was implemented**, in `thesis/results/v9/toolchain/patches/and.patch` (SHA-256
`cc61d6dec9c774b358d48ff528e8d46bd178ccb71d78e01fbd22bef324fffb95`):

- Changes across 6 existing files, 529 lines in total (outside

  (+17, offering the dual code in the ClientHello, forbidding

  selection on the server, `CertificateRequest` with the dual code,

- `dual_test.go` (718 lines, new): 18 tests -- the 15 items from the
  original request (counting by semicolon), 3 of them with two
  scenarios each, giving the 18 scenarios covered (see Decision 7, item
  3, and Luciano's confirmation in Decision 8: "15 items, 18 scenarios"
  is the correct count, "17" discarded). Exact names of the 3 requested

  `TestDualQuantumAdversaryHoldingOnlyRSAKey`,
  `TestSingleChainRSAAdversaryStillAuthenticates`,
  `TestDualNonStrictAllowsDowngrade`.

**Patch-size decision, asked and confirmed by Luciano.**
529 lines outside `dual.go`/tests exceeds the ~400 he marked as an
explicit stopping point. I asked before proceeding; he confirmed
"proceed as is" -- the excess comes from needing the complete logic on
both sides (client sends and verifies, server sends and verifies), with
real security validation (independent chains, SAN, no short-circuit),
not from loose or needlessly duplicated code.

**Impostor test, the two results side by side (the direct evidence of
why strict mode is mandatory):**

| Test | Adversary | Verifying pair | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TestDualQuantumAdversaryHoldingOnlyRSAKey` | Holds the legitimate pair's RSA key, does NOT have the ML-DSA key (presents the legitimate public PQ certificate, but signs with a different ML-DSA key, for lack of the real one) | Strict AND server (`Dual.Require=true`) | **Rejected** -- classical ok, post-quantum fake, server refuses the pair |
| `TestSingleChainRSAAdversaryStillAuthenticates` | The SAME adversary (RSA key only, single chain, nothing post-quantum) | Plain classical server, mTLS without `Dual` (Hybrid-v8 format: ML-DSA only as the CA's signature, never verified during the handshake) | **Authenticates normally** -- there is no PQ key-possession proof to fail, because none is ever requested |

This table demonstrates exactly the gap that motivated v9 (fact A from
Decision 1): the same adversary, with the same stolen key, is refused
by AND and accepted by Hybrid-v8.

**Real bug found and fixed in T2's own `Dockerfile`, before the final
result.** The first attempt to apply the real patch
(`cd src && git apply /tmp/and.patch && cd ..`) reported success (exit
0) but "Skipped" (`Skipped patch`) every file, applying nothing --
`git apply` resolves the patch's paths against the ROOT of the cloned
git repository, not against the shell's current directory, and the
patch was generated with paths relative to `crypto/tls` (`a/common.go`),
not to `src/crypto/tls` (the clone's real root). Fixed with
`git apply --directory=src/crypto/tls`, the option that prefixes each
patch path -- confirmed in an isolated diagnostic container before
touching the real Dockerfile.

**Two other real bugs found and fixed during the implementation itself,
not in the Dockerfile:**
1. `net.Pipe()` in the tests caused a transport deadlock whenever the
   client aborted reading midway through the server's first flight
   (exactly the case for the negative tests) -- replaced with
   `localPipe(t)` (real TCP over loopback, the same mechanism the
   `crypto/tls` suite itself already uses for complete handshakes).
2. Go's own unmodified `getClientCertificate()` filters the client's
   classical certificate by the same list of signature algorithms the
   server announced in the `CertificateRequest` -- in strict mode that
   list is just `0xFE65`, which matches no real classical algorithm,
   causing the client to send no certificate at all even though one is
   available. Fixed by using a common classical algorithm list solely
   for certificate SELECTION, not for choosing the signature scheme
   (which remains the dual code).

**Final result, full `crypto/tls` suite (original + the 18 new tests),
against the go1.27.3 toolchain rebuilt from the real patch, via T2's
complete pipeline (clone -> verify commit ->
`git apply` -> `make.bash` -> test):** `ok crypto/tls 55.306s` --
**232 PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 SKIP** (214 from the original suite, unchanged, +
18 new). Wire-size measurement (`TestDualWireSizeMeasurement`,
real data from this run): classical-only Certificate message 814 B vs.
dual (classical+ML-DSA-65) 6.355 B (+680.7%); classical-only
CertificateVerify signature field 256 B vs. dual 3.567 B (+1.293,4%);
standalone PQ chain 5.533 B.

Updated artifacts: `thesis/results/v9/toolchain/Dockerfile`,
`README.md`, `build_metadata.json`, `crypto_tls_test_summary.txt`,
`patches/and.patch` (now with the real content, no longer empty).

## 7. Response to the 6 points requested after the T3 report: full impostor pair, SKIPs explained, exact count of the 23 tests, pipeline hardened against the git-apply bug, session resumption and HelloRetryRequest tested, per-file documentation

**1. Impostor pair, single classical chain, strict vs. non-strict, side
by side.** The previous report compared the adversary (RSA key only)
against a strict AND server and against a plain classical server (with
no `Dual` at all) -- useful for the interoperability matrix, but not
the exact pair requested. Two new tests were added, with the SAME
client configuration (single classical chain, no `Dual`) in both:

| Test | Server | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `TestDualImpostorSingleChainVsStrict` | Strict AND (`Dual.Require=true`) | **Rejected** |
| `TestDualImpostorSingleChainVsNonStrict` | Non-strict AND (`Dual.Require=false`) | **Accepted**, `DualAuthenticated=false` confirmed in the test (`cs.DualAuthenticated` checked explicitly, not just the absence of an error) |

The tests `TestDualStrictServerVsLegacyClient` and
`TestDualNonStrictAllowsDowngrade` (from the previous round) already
covered these same two result transitions, but under different
thematic names, without it being explicit that it is the SAME client in
both cases -- the two new tests make this comparison self-contained and
named for the exact pair requested.

**4. Pipeline hardened against the `git apply` bug.** The patch-apply
step now counts how many files `and.patch` ITSELF touches
(`grep -c '^diff --git' /tmp/and.patch`, not a fixed number in the
Dockerfile -- stays correct if the patch changes) and compares that
against how many files `git status --porcelain` actually finds changed
in `src/crypto/tls` after `git apply`. A mismatch = explicit `exit 1`,
with a message naming the original bug. Validated in an isolated
diagnostic container, outside the real pipeline: deliberately
reintroducing the old invocation (`cd src && git apply
... && cd ..`, without `--directory`), the check now reports "and.patch
touches 9 files; git status reports 0 changed" and correctly identifies
the mismatch -- confirmed that this specific bug can no longer pass
silently.

**5. Patch gaps: tested or recorded.**

a) **Session resumption -- decided and tested, not left as an open
gap.** TLS 1.3 resumption skips Certificate/
CertificateVerify entirely, so a resumed connection would inherit the
original connection's dual authentication WITHOUT reverifying either
chain -- undermining exactly the guarantee that `Require=true` exists
to make absolute. Decision: strict connections NEVER issue a session
ticket (`shouldSendSessionTickets`, `handshake_server_tls13.go`) --
there is nothing to resume. Tested in
`TestDualStrictModeDisablesSessionTickets`
(two consecutive connections with the same `ClientSessionCache`; the
second never resumes). Non-strict connections keep issuing tickets as
before, but a resumed connection NEVER reports `DualAuthenticated=true`
(this field is never restored from the session state, unlike
`PeerCertificates`/`VerifiedChains`, which Go itself already restores
with no change from me) -- tested directly in
`TestDualResumedSessionDoesNotCarryDualAuthentication` (confirms
`DidResume=true` AND `DualAuthenticated=false` on the same resumed
connection, not merely assumed).

b) **HelloRetryRequest with the hybrid group -- tested, passes.**
`TestDualHandshakeAcrossHelloRetryRequest` forces a genuine group
retry: `curvePreferences()` (`common.go`) always orders the allowed
groups in a fixed global order (hybrids before classical ones,
`curvePreferenceOrder()` in `defaults.go`), ignoring the order given in
`Config.CurvePreferences` -- so simply placing the hybrid group first
in the client's list does not force a retry (it would already be first
anyway). The real way to force it: client allows
`X25519MLKEM768` (sorts first in the fixed list, receives the initial
key share) AND `SecP384r1MLKEM1024` (only declared, no initial key
share); server accepts only `SecP384r1MLKEM1024`; the client's initial
key share is unusable, the server responds with a HelloRetryRequest
specifically asking for `SecP384r1MLKEM1024`, and the dual handshake
completes correctly after that -- confirmed (`cs.HelloRetryRequest`,
`cs.DualAuthenticated`, `cs.CurveID` all checked in the test).

c) **Recorded as a gap still open, with no code change**
(in `dual.go`'s header, updated): the client's
`VerifyConnection`/`VerifyPeerCertificate` callbacks still see only the
classical chain (`c.peerCertificates`), exactly as in stock Go, and run
BEFORE the PQ chain's validation; no support for
`CompressedCertificate` (RFC 8879) or Exported Authenticators (RFC
9261); no `RelatedCertificate` (RFC 9440); the mechanism is TLS 1.3
only, with no explicit rejection of the dual code under TLS 1.2 (it is
simply never offered or accepted below 1.3, with the same practical
effect).

**6. Documentation: 543 lines vs. ~400 expected, per-file table,
the three fixes.**

The total rose from 529 to **543 lines outside `dual.go`/tests**
(item 5a's session-ticket guard added 14 lines to
`handshake_server_tls13.go`). Luciano's decision to proceed as is
(Decision 6) remains valid -- the increase is for the same reason
(real security logic, not loose code).

| File | Lines | What it does |
|---|---:|---|
| `common.go` | +30 | `Dual *DualConfig` field in `Config`; `Dual.clone()` in `Config.Clone()`; 3 new fields in `ConnectionState` (`DualAuthenticated`, `DualPeerCertificates`, `DualVerifiedChains`) |
| `conn.go` | +10 | 3 internal fields in `Conn` (mirroring those in `ConnectionState`); population in `connectionStateLocked` |
| `handshake_client.go` | +17 | Offering the dual code `0xFE65` in the `ClientHello` (it alone in strict mode); forbidding `InsecureSkipVerify` with `Dual` configured |
| `handshake_client_tls13.go` | +172 | Client: independently validates the server's PQ chain; verifies the dual `CertificateVerify` (both signatures, no short-circuit); when a certificate is requested (mTLS), selects the classical certificate via a common classical algorithm list (not the strict server's dual-only list) and sends both certificates + dual signature when the server requests it |
| `handshake_messages.go` | +157 | Serialization/parsing of the Certificate message with the 3-zero-byte delimiter; rejects a first, last, or repeated delimiter; behavior identical to the original parser when there is no delimiter |
| `handshake_server_tls13.go` | +152 | Server: chooses the dual certificate when the client offers the code and a PQ chain is configured; `Require` closes the handshake if the client does not offer it; `CertificateRequest` also offers the dual code for mTLS; verifies the client's pair (PQ chain + SAN identity) and the dual `CertificateVerify`; suppresses the session ticket in strict mode |
| `tls_test.go` | +5 | Registers the `Dual` field in `TestCloneNonFuncFields` (an existing test, not modified by this patch, but one that requires every new `Config` field to be accounted for) |

**The three real bugs found during implementation, summarized:**
1. `git apply` resolves paths against the cloned git repository's
root, not against the shell's current directory -- it reported success
while skipping every file. Fixed with `--directory=src/crypto/tls`;
hardened in item 4 above to never again pass silently.
2. `net.Pipe()` in the tests causes a transport deadlock whenever the
client aborts reading midway through the server's first flight (the
case for every negative test) -- replaced with `localPipe(t)` (real
TCP over loopback, the same mechanism the `crypto/tls` suite itself
already uses for complete handshakes).
3. Go's own unmodified `getClientCertificate()` filters the client's
classical certificate by the same signature algorithm list the server
announced -- in strict mode that list is just `0xFE65`, which matches
no real classical algorithm, causing the client to send no certificate
at all even though one is available. Fixed by using a common classical
algorithm list solely for certificate SELECTION, not for choosing the
signature scheme (which remains the dual code).

## 8. Response to 3 points requested after the previous round's report: 15/17/18 reconciliation (see Decision 7, item 3, already corrected above), HelloRetryRequest with explicit initial and final group, and recording of per-profile group restriction for T5/T6

**1. Count 15 vs. 17 vs. 18.** See the correction made directly in
Decision 7, item 3 (rewritten, not duplicated here): counting by
semicolon, the original request has 15 top-level items, of which 3
(items 6, 12, and 14) name TWO scenarios each within the same item,
totaling **18 concrete scenarios** -- not 15, nor 17.
T3's 18 tests cover these 18 scenarios one by one (table in Decision
7). If "17" intended to treat one of the three duplicated items as a
single combined test, I need Luciano to say which one -- as
implemented, all three were treated as pairs, giving 18.

**2. HelloRetryRequest -- initial and final group, made explicit.**
`TestDualHandshakeAcrossHelloRetryRequest` (`dual_test.go`) already
correctly forced and verified the retry in the previous round (the
test passed), but did not make the two groups visible in the test's
own log -- fixed. The test now names the two roles explicitly
(`initialShareGroup`, `retryTargetGroup`) and logs explicitly via
`t.Logf`:

- **First ClientHello**: key share sent for `X25519MLKEM768`
  (this group sorts first in `curvePreferenceOrder()`, so it receives
  the client's initial key share, even though it is listed after
  `SecP384r1MLKEM1024` in `Config.CurvePreferences`).
- **HelloRetryRequest**: the server (which only accepts
  `SecP384r1MLKEM1024`) cannot use that initial key share, and responds
  by specifically requesting `SecP384r1MLKEM1024` -- a group the client
  had already declared support for, just without an initial key share.
- **Negotiated final group**: `SecP384r1MLKEM1024`, confirmed via
  `ConnectionState.CurveID` on BOTH sides (client and server,
  `cs.CurveID`/`ss.CurveID`), not just one side -- and via
  `ConnectionState.HelloRetryRequest=true` on both sides too,
  confirming that the retry actually happened (not a direct negotiation
  by coincidence).

**Finding while strengthening the test, not a patch bug:** the first
strengthened version checked `DualAuthenticated` on BOTH sides, but the
original test only configured the SERVER's dual identity (no mTLS) --
and `ss.DualAuthenticated` (server) correctly came out `false`, because
the server never requested or verified any client certificate, dual or
otherwise. Not a bug: `DualAuthenticated` describes whether THIS side
verified the OTHER side's pair, not a symmetric flag for the whole
connection. Fixed by raising the test to full mutual mTLS (like
`TestDualStrictFullMTLS`), where both ends do authenticate each other
-- only then should both sides report `true`, and they do.

Real result, full suite after this change: `ok crypto/tls`,
`TestDualHandshakeAcrossHelloRetryRequest` passes (mutual mTLS, group
retry included), real log from the run:
`first ClientHello key share: X25519MLKEM768; server's only accepted
group (HelloRetryRequest target): SecP384r1MLKEM1024; negotiated group
after retry: client=SecP384r1MLKEM1024 server=SecP384r1MLKEM1024`.

**3. Per-profile KEX group restriction, recorded for T5/T6
(not implemented now -- it concerns the real campaign code, outside
the scope of T3/the `crypto/tls` fork).** Confirmed in `curvePreferences()`
(`common.go`, Decision 7 item 5b): the order given in
`Config.CurvePreferences` is ignored; only which groups are ALLOWED
matters, priority is always `curvePreferenceOrder()`'s fixed global
order. Direct consequence for the real campaign (T5/T6, not for this
patch's unit tests): **each profile needs to restrict
`CurvePreferences` to EXACTLY one group**, with no extras, or the group
actually negotiated may not be the one the profile intends to measure:
- Classical: `CurveP384` only.
- PQC: `MLKEM1024` only.
- Hybrid and Hybrid-AND: `SecP384r1MLKEM1024` only.

This is already exactly what `mock_mtls/main.go` does today in v8
(confirmed in T1, Decision 1 of this folder: `serverCurvePreferences`
fixed to a single entry per profile, no multiple lists) -- the
requirement here is to NOT regress this in T5/T6 when integrating AND
(never introduce `X25519MLKEM768` or any other extra group into the
REAL client/gateway configurations, even though an isolated unit test,
like the HelloRetryRequest one above, needs an extra group on purpose
solely to force the retry in the lab).

**Recorded as a mandatory T5/T6 requirement (implementation pending,
not part of this Decision):** every measured run must read
`ConnectionState.CurveID` right after the handshake and **explicitly
fail the run** (not merely log a warning) if the negotiated group is
not exactly the one expected for that profile -- the same "fail
explicitly, never pass silently" logic already applied to the
pipeline's own `git apply` (Decision 7, item 4), now extended to the
KEX group of every real measured connection.

**Finding while strengthening the HelloRetryRequest test with both
sides checked (not just the client): not a patch bug.** The first
strengthened version (item 2 above) checked `DualAuthenticated` on both
sides, but the original test only configured the SERVER's dual
identity, with no mTLS -- `ss.DualAuthenticated` (server) correctly
came out `false`, because the server never requested or verified any
client certificate. `DualAuthenticated` describes whether THIS side
verified the OTHER side's pair, not a symmetric flag for the whole
connection -- correct behavior, not a bug. Fixed by raising the test to
full mutual mTLS (like `TestDualStrictFullMTLS`), where both ends do
authenticate each other; only then do both sides report `true`,
confirmed.

## 9. T4, new certificates: Classical and Hybrid-v8 on RSA-2048, Hybrid-AND with two independent chains (RSA-2048 + ML-DSA-65, same SAN identity), PQC reused unchanged from v8 -- all validated by Go's standard verifier, no InsecureSkipVerify

**Scope decision, not asked beforehand, recorded here for Luciano to
confirm or correct:** T4's original request cites
`certs/main.go` (the REAL production certificate generator,
`mock-service-os/certs/main.go`, used by the already published and
tagged v7/v8). I chose **NOT to touch that file** and to build a new,
isolated generator at `thesis/results/v9/certs/` -- under the same
principle already applied to all of v9 ("additive, never overwrites
the official v8"): any edit to `certs/main.go` would risk affecting,
even by accident, the RSA-4096 certificates that v8 already measures
and publishes. The actual integration with the gateway/client (deciding
whether this new generator ends up living inside `certs/main.go` or
stays separate) is left for T5, which is explicitly about integration.
If Luciano wanted `certs/main.go` edited already, I am flagging this
here before any wiring happens in T5.

**What was generated, and where:**
`thesis/results/v9/certs/main.go` (a self-contained Go program, standard
library only -- without `github.com/google/uuid`/`go-oidc`, which the
real generator uses only for JWKS/extra Subject fields, outside T4's
scope) generates and validates the 4 profiles, writing each certificate
and key to `thesis/results/v9/certs/certs/`:

| Profile | Chain(s) | Files |
|---|---|---|
| Classical | 1 RSA-2048 CA -> server leaf + client leaf, RSA-2048 | `classico_ca`, `classico_server`, `classico_client` |
| Hybrid-v8 | 1 RSA-2048 CA (primary) + 1 ML-DSA-65 CA (signs only the AltSignatureValue) -> RSA-2048 leaves with the 3 hybrid X.509 extensions (Bindel et al. 2019), same mechanism as v8, now RSA-2048 instead of RSA-4096 | `hibrido_v8_ca` (RSA), `hibrido_v8_ca_mldsa` (alt), `hibrido_v8_server`, `hibrido_v8_client` |
| Hybrid-AND | 2 FULLY independent chains: 1 RSA-2048 CA -> RSA-2048 leaves; 1 ML-DSA-65 CA (genuinely self-signed) -> ML-DSA-65 leaves. Same SAN identity on both, different end keys, no CA shared with Hybrid-v8 | `hibrido_and_rsa_ca/server/client`, `hibrido_and_mldsa_ca/server/client` |
| PQC | Reused from v8 **with no change whatsoever** -- a read-only copy (only the `.crt` files, no keys) of `mock-service-os/certs/{root_ca_pqc,issuer_ca_pqc,mtls_pqc,client_one_pqc}.crt` into `thesis/results/v9/certs/v8_pqc/`, loaded and revalidated, never regenerated | (no new file; read-only copies in `v8_pqc/`) |

**SAN used**: server leaves carry `mtls` (the literal SNI that
`thesis/scripts/tls_kem_proxy` dials by default today) plus the same
hostname list `mock-service-os/certs/main.go` already uses
(`auth.local`, `matls-auth.local`, `api.local`, `matls-api.local`,
`directory`, `directory.local`, `keystore`) and the IPs
`127.0.0.1`/`::1`; client leaves carry a stable identity of their own,
`opin-client-one`, the same across both Hybrid-AND chains (a
requirement of the mechanism).

**EKU**: every server certificate with `ExtKeyUsageServerAuth`, every
client certificate with `ExtKeyUsageClientAuth` -- confirmed by the
validation itself below (which fails if the EKU does not match), not
merely by what the template requests.

**Validation, all chains, with Go's `x509.Certificate.Verify()`,
`InsecureSkipVerify` used nowhere** (that flag belongs to
`crypto/tls`, at the connection level -- it doesn't even exist in an
isolated x509 call like this one, which by itself already eliminates
the most common way for a validation to "pass" without checking
anything for real):

```
=== Classico (RSA-2048) ===
OK   Classico/server: verified (root trusted, EKU=serverAuth, DNSName="mtls")
OK   Classico/client: verified (root trusted, EKU=clientAuth, DNSName="")

=== Hibrido-v8 (RSA-2048 + assinatura dupla X.509 ML-DSA-65) ===
OK   Hibrido-v8/server (RSA half): verified (EKU=serverAuth, DNSName="mtls")
OK   Hibrido-v8/client (RSA half): verified (EKU=clientAuth, DNSName="")
OK   Hibrido-v8/server: AltSignatureValue (ML-DSA-65 half) independently re-verified
OK   Hibrido-v8/client: AltSignatureValue (ML-DSA-65 half) independently re-verified

=== Hibrido-AND (duas cadeias independentes) ===
OK   Hibrido-AND/server (cadeia RSA): verified (EKU=serverAuth, DNSName="mtls")
OK   Hibrido-AND/client (cadeia RSA): verified (EKU=clientAuth, DNSName="")
OK   Hibrido-AND/server (cadeia ML-DSA-65): verified (EKU=serverAuth, DNSName="mtls")
OK   Hibrido-AND/client (cadeia ML-DSA-65): verified (EKU=clientAuth, DNSName="")
OK   Hibrido-AND/server: as duas cadeias declaram a MESMA identidade SAN
OK   Hibrido-AND/client: as duas cadeias declaram a MESMA identidade SAN

=== PQC (reaproveitado da v8, sem mudanca) ===
OK   PQC/server (v8, inalterado, EKU real=ClientAuth): verified (EKU=clientAuth)
OK   PQC/client (v8, inalterado): verified (EKU=clientAuth)
```

Full real output in `thesis/results/v9/certs/validation_report.txt`.

## 10. Response to the 5 points requested before T5: PQC reissued with the correct EKU, size comparability explained, per-handshake table, parametrizable SAN, confirmation on committed keys

**1. PQC reissued, no longer reused from v8.** The real
`mtls_pqc.crt` certificate is NO LONGER used as v9's PQC profile --
confirmed that v9's client verifies the server in every profile, with
no `InsecureSkipVerify`, and Go would refuse that file (EKU=ClientAuth
only). Generated from scratch: `pqc_ca` (self-signed ML-DSA-65 CA) ->
`pqc_server` (EKU=ServerAuth) and `pqc_client` (EKU=ClientAuth), using
the SAME `generateMLDSACA`/`generateMLDSALeaf` functions already used
for Hybrid-AND's ML-DSA-65 chain (same template, not a separate copy).

**EKU confirmed, leaf by leaf, every profile, no exception**
(real output from this round):

| Profile | Leaf | EKU |
|---|---|---|
| Classical | server | `serverAuth` |
| Classical | client | `clientAuth` |
| Hybrid-v8 | server | `serverAuth` |
| Hybrid-v8 | client | `clientAuth` |
| Hybrid-AND | server (RSA) | `serverAuth` |
| Hybrid-AND | client (RSA) | `clientAuth` |
| Hybrid-AND | server (ML-DSA-65) | `serverAuth` |
| Hybrid-AND | client (ML-DSA-65) | `clientAuth` |
| PQC (v9) | server | `serverAuth` |
| PQC (v9) | client | `clientAuth` |

All 10 leaves validated with `x509.Certificate.Verify()`, the required
EKU matching expectations, `DNSName="mtls"` on the server ones (a real
hostname check, not an empty one).

**2. Size comparability, explained and fixed.** The original question
(why v8's PQC totals 23.490 B against ~16.7 KB for Hybrid-AND's
ML-DSA-65 side) was comparing chains of DIFFERENT formats:
real v8 has 2 CA levels (`root_ca_pqc` -> `issuer_ca_pqc` ->
leaf, 4 certificates) and 3 extra DN fields on each leaf
(`organizationID`, `LDAP-UID`, `X500-UID`); Hybrid-AND (and now the
reissued PQC) has 1 level (CA signs the leaf directly, 3
certificates) and a DN with only `CommonName`. PQC was reissued with
the SAME template as Hybrid-AND (request made, fulfilled) -- now the
two ML-DSA-65 chains are directly comparable, and the remaining
difference is minimal, just variable-length ASN.1 encoding (serial
number, timestamps):

| | PQC (v9) | Hybrid-AND (ML-DSA-65) |
|---|---:|---:|
| CA | 5.468 B | 5.496 B |
| server | 5.619 B | 5.647 B |
| client | 5.506 B | 5.534 B |

**Recorded for the equivalence checklist (T8) and here:** v9's PQC
(16.593 B total) is structurally DIFFERENT from v8's real PQC
(23.490 B) -- not because of ML-DSA-65 (public key and signature have
a FIXED size, identical in both), but because of 1 fewer CA level and
3 fewer DN fields. This is a deliberate divergence of this phase (T4,
simplification for local comparability), not an error -- if v9's real
campaign (T5/T8) needs the same 2-level format v8 used (for example, to
compare OPINsize per term directly with v8), this needs to be decided
explicitly before the official collection, recorded here as a pending
item.

**3. Per-handshake table -- what actually travels on the wire**
(leaf/leaves + intermediates, WITHOUT the root -- the root never
travels on the network, it only needs to be in each side's local trust
pool):

| Profile | Chain sent by the server | Bytes | Chain sent by the client | Bytes |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| Classical | leaf only | 900 | leaf only | 787 |
| Hybrid-v8 | 1 leaf (with the 3 hybrid X.509 extensions) | 6.242 | 1 leaf (idem) | 6.131 |
| Hybrid-AND | RSA leaf + ML-DSA-65 leaf (both, per the mechanism) | 6.561 | RSA leaf + ML-DSA-65 leaf | 6.335 |
| PQC (v9) | leaf only | 5.619 | leaf only | 5.506 |

No profile in this round uses its own intermediate (all are 1
level); if a real profile ever uses 2 levels (as v8 did for PQC), the
intermediate adds to this same table as well -- the formula is "every
leaf between the final leaf and the root, root excluded."

**4. SAN as a parameter, no longer fixed in code.** `main.go` now

## 13. Two adjustments requested before T6: session tickets turned off on all FOUR profiles (not just Hybrid-AND), and an explanation of why the full flow (44 HTTP / 6 mTLS / 28 JWT / 4 jwks / 4 CA) did not run in T5

**1. TICKETS, on all four profiles.** `gateway/main.go` and
`proxy/main.go` gained an explicit `ticketsDisabled` parameter
(`TICKETS_DISABLED` on the gateway, `-tickets-disabled` on the proxy,
default `true` on both) that sets `tls.Config.SessionTicketsDisabled`
-- previously set only on Hybrid-AND's `Dual`, now on EVERY
`tls.Config` that `buildServerTLSConfig`/`buildClientTLSConfig`
produce.

**What v8 (and v7, same code) actually did -- confirmed, not
assumed:** `grep -rn SessionTicket mock-service-os/mock_mtls/*.go
thesis/scripts/tls_kem_proxy/*.go` returns no occurrence at all --
no `tls.Config` in v7/v8 ever sets `SessionTicketsDisabled`,
so tickets stay ON (Go's zero-value default) in ALL three
v8 profiles, always. And the ticket bytes DID enter the gateway's
counter: `thesis/results/v8/DECISIONS.md`, Decision 78, had already
tracked this byte for byte via a real capture (tcpdump) of a real
Hybrid connection -- `mtlsHandshakeBytes` contained the `ClientHello`
+ the server's complete flight + **2.162 B consistent with a
`NewSessionTicket`** + the client's flight + the start of the first
HTTP request, all summed because `connStateHandshakeLogger` reads the
cumulative counter at `ConnState -> StateActive`, which only fires
after ALL of that traffic has already passed through the connection.
Decision 79 (same file) records that Luciano decided **NOT to fix**
this measurement limit in v8, to maintain comparability with v7
(which carries the same artifact as always, same code). In other
words: v7/v8's historical `mtlsHandshakeBytes` figures include
ticket(s) plus a chunk of the first request -- a deliberately "dirty"
number for historical-comparability reasons, not an unknown bug.

**Why v9 diverges from this, deliberately, recorded here for T8's
equivalence checklist:** v9 is not trying to reproduce v7/v8's
historical numbers byte for byte -- it is comparing Hybrid-AND against
v9's own other 3 profiles. If tickets stayed on for 3 profiles and
never for Hybrid-AND (the only profile whose own protocol logic
structurally prevents them, see T6 below), the comparison would be
biased in Hybrid-AND's favor for a reason that has nothing to do with
the AND mechanism itself. Turning them off on all four levels the
playing field. **Explicit divergence of v9 from v7/v8:** v9 measures
the handshake WITHOUT tickets by default; v7/v8 always measured WITH
tickets (and with the ticket partially contaminating the counter).
The two numbers are not directly comparable to each other for this
additional reason (added to the certificate non-comparability already
recorded in Decision 11) -- only among v9's 4 profiles, among
themselves.

**Quantification of the effect, requested for T6 (diagnostic mode,
tickets turned back on just to measure):** done, see Decision 14
below -- it includes a new, unforeseen structural finding: Hybrid-AND
NEVER issues a ticket, regardless of this parameter, for a different
reason (a design decision from T3 itself, not from this adjustment).

**2. FULL LOCAL FLOW -- why it did not run in T5, what is missing, how
v8 runs it, feasibility.**

**Why T5 did not run the full flow:** T5 was designed and approved
(Decision 12) with a deliberately restricted scope -- to prove that the
TLS MECHANISM (handshake, mutual verification, single group, the AND
gate) works across the 4 profiles, without rebuilding OPIN's business
logic. The T5/T6 harness (`thesis/results/v9/integration/{gateway,proxy}`)
is a deliberately reduced fork: the gateway's HTTP handler is a single
fixed endpoint that returns `{profile, curve, dualAuthenticated,
tlsVersion}` -- there is no reverse proxy to auth/api, no SSA signing,
no token introspection, no `/jwks`/`/root-ca.pem`/
`/issuer-ca.pem` serving real content, and the proxy makes ONE manual
HTTP call per run, not a persistent tunnel that the real `opin_flow.py`
could use.

**How v8 actually runs the full flow (`mock-service-os/
docker-compose.yml` + `insurance-server-lambdas/docker-compose.yml`),
service by service:**
- `mtls` (the real gateway, `mock_mtls`) -- reverse proxy to auth/api,
  serves `/root-ca.pem`/`/issuer-ca.pem`/`/jwks`, signs the SSA.
  Exposes `matls-auth.local`/`auth.local`/`api.local`/`matls-api.local`/
  `directory` as network aliases.
- `auth` (`mock_as`, Node.js, oidc-provider) -- issues the JWTs, makes
  the `InsurerAdapter.getConsent()` reentrant call back to the
  gateway via SNI `matls-api.local`.
- `mongo1`/`mongo_seed` -- the oidc-provider's state (sessions,
  clients, grants).
- `localstack` -- emulates SSM Parameter Store and S3 LOCALLY (a local
  Docker container, never touches real AWS -- not violating the "no
  AWS" rule), serves the SSA's private key (`SSA_JWK_URL`) and the
  config parameters `auth`/`mtls` read at boot.
- `insurance-server-lambdas` (a separate stack, `API_GATEWAY_URI`) --
  the RS/insurer-side API that the gateway proxies to via
  `api.local`/`matls-api.local`.
- `thesis/scripts/opin_flow.py` + `thesis/scripts/tls_kem_proxy` (relay
  mode, not stub) -- the real client: `tls_kem_proxy` terminates a
  local TLS (throwaway, self-signed) on one side and opens ONE real
  mTLS connection per connection on the other, passing raw bytes
  through -- this is what lets Python talk to a gateway that requires
  ML-KEM groups Python's OpenSSL cannot negotiate.

**What is concretely missing to run v9's 4 profiles (including
Hybrid-AND) end to end locally, with the same counts (44/6/
28/4/4):**
1. Give the gateway fork (`thesis/results/v9/integration/
   gateway`) back the business layer T5 removed for scope: reverse
   proxy to auth/api, SSA signing (needs the `jwx` dependency back),
   `/jwks`/`/root-ca.pem`/`/issuer-ca.pem`,
   token introspection -- OR point these handlers to the real `mock_as`/
   `insurance-server-lambdas` (neither needs a change, both are
   agnostic to the TLS profile).
2. Extend the proxy fork with a persistent RELAY MODE (like the real
   `tls_kem_proxy` has, which T5 removed for scope -- see
   Decision 12), including the 4th profile (hibrido-and) that the real
   `tls_kem_proxy` does not have.
3. Bring up `auth`/`mongo1`/`mongo_seed`/`localstack`/
   `insurance-server-lambdas` alongside it (no change to any of
   them -- they are agnostic to the TLS mechanism, they only speak
   plain HTTP to the gateway).
4. Point `opin_flow.py` at this gateway/proxy instead of the real ones
   (there is precedent: the `REMOTE_GATEWAY_HOST` flag designed in
   v8's AWS experiment plan solves exactly this kind of redirection,
   reusable here).
5. Confirm the counts (44 HTTP / 6 mTLS / 28 JWT / 4 jwks / 4 CA)
   via the SAME instrumentation T6 already built (Decision 14),
   now measuring the full flow, not an isolated connection.

**Feasibility: YES, no fundamental technical obstacle found.**
None of the missing components depends on external network, real AWS,
or anything that does not already exist in this repository today -- it
is integration engineering (items 1-4 above), not research or new
design. Outside the already-approved scope of T5 (Decision 12) and of
this instrumentation round (T6); recorded here as a **mandatory T7
criterion**, as requested, before any AWS pilot.

Same rules: no action on AWS, no commit before the scanner, report in
chat.

## 14. T6, instrumentation: decrypted keylog+pcap cross-checked against in-process counting at the exact Handshake() boundary, CPU microbenchmarks, tickets quantified (structural finding: Hybrid-AND in STRICT MODE never issues a ticket -- non-strict mode not tested, would issue one normally), initcwnd/RTT analysis for distant routes

**Architecture, to avoid a bind mount (does not work in this
environment -- Decision 11):** `thesis/results/v9/integration/measure/`
builds ONE container holding gateway, proxy, tcpdump, AND tshark
together; gateway and proxy talk over loopback (127.0.0.1) INSIDE
that same container, writing the TLS keylog to the same local
filesystem that tshark reads afterward -- no file crosses a container
boundary, no bind mount anywhere. `measure.sh` orchestrates: tcpdump in
the background -> gateway in the background -> proxy in the
foreground (one connection) -> stop the capture -> decrypt with tshark
using the keylog -> print everything. `thesis/results/v9/integration/bench/`
is a separate container, no network, CPU only.

**Byte counting at the exact `Handshake()` boundary:** `gateway/
main.go` and `proxy/main.go` dropped T5's `http.Server`/`http.Client`
(which hide the call to `Handshake()` inside `net/http` itself) in
favor of an explicit `Accept()`/`tls.Server()`/`tls.Client()` loop: a
`countingConn` wrapper beneath `tls.Conn` takes a snapshot of the
counters immediately before and after the call to
`Handshake()`, and a second window ("post-handshake") covers exactly
what is written/read between `Handshake()`'s return and the manual
HTTP response this harness writes by hand (never `net/http` -- see
`serveOneResponse`'s comment). This replaces, for v9, the heuristic
estimate 4.945/22.373/18.783 that Luciano identified as not
reproducible from the repository's code -- the numbers below ARE
reproducible, by running `bash thesis/results/v9/integration/run_t6.sh`.

**Cross-validation, confirmed across the 4 profiles:** the number the
process counts (`handshakeBytesIn`/`handshakeBytesOut`) matches, byte
for byte, the sum of the TLS records tshark decrypts via the keylog
(for example, Classical: ClientHello 341B + server flight
(ServerHello+EncryptedExtensions+CertificateRequest+Certificate+
CertificateVerify+Finished) 1.640B + client flight
(Certificate+CertificateVerify+Finished) 1,172B = exactly the
`handshakeBytesOut=1640`/`handshakeBytesIn=1513` -- `341+1172=1513` --
that the gateway recorded). The pcap's raw byte sum for the whole
capture (independent of decryption) also matches handshake + the
post-handshake window summed together, across the 4 profiles. Three
independent sources (the in-process counter, decrypted tshark, the
pcap's raw sum) agree exactly -- no estimate, three measurements.

**Result per profile, normal mode (tickets off, N=1 run each --
proof of instrumentation, not yet a statistical campaign; repeating
with a larger N is pilot/T7 work):**

| Profile | Negotiated group | DualAuthenticated | Server flight (B) | Client flight (B) | Post-handshake in/out (B) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Classical | CurveP384 | false (n/a) | 1.640 | 1.513 | 71 / 203 |
| PQC | MLKEM1024 | false (n/a) | 10.878 | 10.728 | 71 / 198 |
| Hybrid-v8 | SecP384r1MLKEM1024 | false (n/a; the client cert's X.509 gate passed) | 8.552 | 8.397 | 71 / 215 |
| Hybrid-AND | SecP384r1MLKEM1024 | **true**, confirmed on both sides | 12.177 | 11.902 | 71 / 215 |

All 4: negotiated group matches expectations exactly, `status=200`
on the single HTTP request, no failure.

**Tickets, diagnostic mode (turned back on just to measure; a
technical finding along the way -- recorded because it changed the
test's design):** the first attempt, with `SessionTicketsDisabled=false`
on both sides, measured a ZERO delta on every profile -- a bug in the
instrumentation ITSELF, not in the mechanism: this toolchain's
`handshake_client.go` (line ~376) only makes the client announce
`psk_key_exchange_modes` (the signal the server's
`shouldSendSessionTickets()` requires, RFC 8446 4.2.9) when
`Config.ClientSessionCache` is NOT nil -- the harness never set this.
Fixed (`proxy/main.go`, `buildClientTLSConfig`): when
`ticketsDisabled=false`, it sets `ClientSessionCache =
tls.NewLRUClientSessionCache(4)`. After the fix:

| Profile | Server flight WITHOUT ticket (B) | Server flight WITH ticket (B) | Ticket overhead (B) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Classical | 1.640 | 3.331 | **1.691** |
| PQC | 10.878 | 22.007 | **11.129** |
| Hybrid-v8 | 8.552 | 15.591 | **7.039** |
| Hybrid-AND | 12.177 | 12.177 | **0** |

Confirmed symmetrically on the client side: the SAME number of bytes
shows up in the proxy's post-handshake window (e.g., Classical
203->1.894, delta 1.691) instead of in the handshake window --
because the CLIENT's `Handshake()` returns before opportunistically
reading the `NewSessionTicket` the server has already written
(confirmed by reading `handshake_server_tls13.go`: the server sends
the ticket SYNCHRONOUSLY, inside its own `Handshake()`, right after
processing the client's `Certificate`/`CertificateVerify` -- but the
client does not need to finish READING that ticket to consider its
own handshake complete). In other words: the same ticket can fall on
one side or the other of the boundary depending on WHO measures and
WHEN -- which is exactly why the original request (measuring both
windows, on both sides) was not redundant.

**Structural finding, CORRECTED after Luciano's review -- the
original wording ("never issues a ticket, in any mode") was imprecise
and contradicted what T3 itself had already documented (non-strict
mode issues a ticket normally). Reconciled here, by reading the code
again instead of relying on memory:** the ticket suppression in
`dual.go`'s `shouldSendSessionTickets()` is gated ONLY by
`Dual.Require`:

```go
if hs.c.config.Dual != nil && hs.c.config.Dual.Require {
    return false
}
```

In other words: with **`Dual.Require = true` (strict mode)**, no
ticket is ever issued -- confirmed, this part of the original wording
was correct. With **`Dual.Require = false` (non-strict mode)**, this
`if` is never entered, and the ticket is issued normally, subject to
the same RFC 8446 gate as the other 3 profiles
(`ClientSessionCache`/`pskModeDHE`) -- exactly as T3 had already
recorded ("non-strict connections keep issuing tickets as before",
`dual.go`/Decision 6's comment). **"In any mode" was wrong** -- it
should have been "in strict mode." The T5/T6 harness only tests
`Dual.Require = true` for Hybrid-AND (and the mechanism's
specification requires this -- Decision 5, strict mode is the only one
that makes sense for v9 to prove the dual proof-of-possession
guarantee), which is why both tests (normal and diagnostic) gave the
same result: it is not that non-strict mode is also immune, it is that
it was never exercised here.

**Correction to the conclusion:** Hybrid-AND is immune to the
inflation artifact **specifically in strict mode**
(`Dual.Require=true`), the only mode v9 uses and measures -- the
reason is the same: resuming a session via PSK would skip the ENTIRE
Certificate/CertificateVerify exchange that proves possession of both
keys, which would nullify the mechanism's central guarantee, so the
patch disables tickets unconditionally in this mode. In non-strict
mode (not used by v9), Hybrid-AND would behave like the other 3
profiles: vulnerable to the same artifact if an operator turned
tickets back on. v9's other 3 profiles (and v7/v8's 3) remain
vulnerable to the artifact regardless of mode, because they have no
notion of `Dual` at all. This also explains why the ticket size scales
with the profile (1.691B Classical -> 7.039B Hybrid-v8 ->
11.129B PQC): Go's ticket embeds the peer's verified certificate
chain, so that a resumed session still has
`ConnectionState.PeerCertificates` populated without needing to
re-send the certificates -- so a client with a large certificate
(PQC, Hybrid-v8) produces a proportionally large ticket.

**Per-stage times at the gateway, an additional finding about the
measurement boundary's limit (transparency, does not invalidate the
table above):** `gateway/main.go` gained `requestDurationUs` (time
for just the HTTP-response-serving stage, separate from
`handshakeDurationUs`). While measuring this, a second form of the
SAME kind of artifact v8's Decision 78 had already documented (bytes
from a later stage entering an earlier stage's count) showed up --
just at a different layer: with the client sending its HTTP request
with NO delay right after its own `Handshake()` returns, the server's
`Read()` that consumes the handshake's last message (the client's
`Finished`) occasionally already finds, in the socket buffer, the
HTTP request bytes that arrived stuck right behind it (loopback,
near-zero latency) -- and counts them as "handshake"
(`handshakeBytesIn` rose from 1.513 to 1.584 in that round, exactly
the 71 B of the request that "leaked" to the inside of the boundary;
`postHandshakeBytesIn` correspondingly dropped to 0). **This does NOT
invalidate the table published above** -- that round was obtained
with a 100ms pause before sending (originally introduced for the
ticket diagnostic, still active when that table was generated) and
confirmed TRIPLY (process counter = decrypted tshark = pcap raw sum,
all three agreeing exactly) -- but it does confirm that the
measurement boundary, even at the `Handshake()` level, is not immune
to this effect when the peer sends data immediately, with no pause at
all. **Recorded for T7:** the real campaign must keep cross-checking
the process counter against pcap/tshark per run (already part of this
pipeline), not rely solely on the counter when the real latency
between the handshake and the first request is very low (e.g., a 0ms
scenario).

Measured times, same round (normal mode, without the diagnostic
pause, hence without the ticket bias): `requestDurationUs` --
Classical 30us, PQC 63us, Hybrid-v8 43us, Hybrid-AND 115us (the stage
of serving ONE minimal HTTP response, not yet comparable to v7/v8's
real `opin_processing_ms`, which serves larger JSON payloads --
Hybrid-AND is expected to tend to be the slowest here too in the real
campaign, for having two chains to consider in the ConnState checks,
not because of this specific number).

**CPU microbenchmarks per operation (4 primitives, N=2000 each,
except RSA/ML-DSA-65 keygen N=100 for being much slower;
`thesis/results/v9/integration/bench`, keys generated on the spot,
same type/parameter as the real profiles -- the specific key does not
affect CPU cost):**

| Operation | ns/op | ops/s |
|---|---|---|
| RSA-2048 keygen | 61.518.062 | 16 |
| RSA-2048 sign (PSS-SHA256) | 830.087 | 1.205 |
| RSA-2048 verify (PSS-SHA256) | 27.887 | 35.859 |
| ML-DSA-65 keygen | 270.874 | 3.692 |
| ML-DSA-65 sign | 537.322 | 1.861 |
| ML-DSA-65 verify | 152.369 | 6.563 |
| ECDH P-384 keygen | 112.387 | 8.898 |
| ECDH P-384 compute (KEX) | 550.225 | 1.817 |
| ML-KEM-1024 keygen | 112.890 | 8.858 |
| ML-KEM-1024 encapsulate | 77.896 | 12.838 |
| ML-KEM-1024 decapsulate | 126.740 | 7.890 |

KEX cost per profile, summing the operations the handshake actually
performs: Classical = 1x keygen + 1x ECDH P-384 compute (~663 us);
PQC = 1x keygen + 1x encapsulate + 1x decapsulate ML-KEM-1024 (~317
us); Hybrid/Hybrid-AND = sum of the two lines above, since the hybrid
group's combiner concatenates both secrets (~980 us).
Sign/verify cost per profile: Classical uses RSA-2048 (1
sign + 1 verify on the certificate pair = ~858 us); PQC/Hybrid-AND
(ML-DSA-65 chain) use ML-DSA-65 (1 sign + 1 verify = ~690 us, FASTER
than RSA-2048 despite the larger certificate); Hybrid-v8 sums RSA
(primary signature) + ML-DSA-65 (X.509 alt signature, verified only
during chain validation, not as a network operation). Hybrid-AND pays
the full RSA cost AND the full ML-DSA-65 cost, structurally IN
PARALLEL (two independent chains) -- CPU cost is the sum of both, not
a hybrid of the two.

**initcwnd / extra-RTT analysis for distant routes (desk calculation,
local Phase 1 -- there is no real AWS route yet to measure; uses the
REAL sizes measured above, not T4's certificate table):**
formula: `extra RTTs = max(0, ceil(flight_bytes / cwnd_bytes) - 1)`,
`cwnd_bytes = initcwnd_segments x MSS`, MSS=1460B (standard Ethernet).

| Profile | Server flight (B) | initcwnd=10 (14,600B, current Linux default) | initcwnd=3 (4,380B, pre-2011 legacy) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Classical | 1.640 | 0 extra RTT | 0 extra RTT |
| PQC | 10.878 | 0 extra RTT | **2 extra RTTs** |
| Hybrid-v8 | 8.552 | 0 extra RTT | **1 extra RTT** |
| Hybrid-AND | 12.177 | 0 extra RTT | **2 extra RTTs** |

**Conclusion:** with the `initcwnd=10` that is the default on any
reasonably current Linux kernel (since 2011, RFC 6928) -- what is
expected of any modern EC2 instance --, NONE of the 4 profiles needs
an extra RTT due to an initial congestion-window limit, at ANY of the
latency tiers already used in this thesis (14/30/140/225/320ms) --
Hybrid-AND's extra cost (nearly 2x Hybrid-v8, from carrying two
complete chains) still fits within the first flight at any RTT. Only
under a legacy `initcwnd` (3 segments, pre-2011) would PQC and
Hybrid-AND pay extra RTTs -- **recorded for T7: empirically confirm
the pilot EC2 instances' real `initcwnd` before assuming 0 extra
RTTs**, not decided here for lack of a real route to measure. This
analysis does not cover packet loss/retransmission (a real-route-
dependent phenomenon, not reproducible on local loopback).

**Artifacts:** `thesis/results/v9/integration/gateway/main.go` and
`proxy/main.go` rewritten (counting at the `Handshake()` boundary,
keylog, parametrized tickets); `measure/{Dockerfile,measure.sh,
.gitignore-covered certs}`; `bench/{main.go,go.mod,Dockerfile}`;
`run_t6.sh` (replaces `run_t5.sh` as the reference script --
`run_t5.sh` still works, kept for compatibility, but `run_t6.sh` is
what now proves both the integration and the instrumentation). No
key, no certificate, no pcap or keylog committed -- everything
generated and discarded on every run (`t6_out/` and `measure/certs/`
gitignored).

Same rules: no action on AWS, no commit before the scanner, report in
chat.

## 15. Clarifications requested after T6: per-TLS-message table (4 profiles), per-stage times, the initcwnd implication for v8's residue

**Point 1 (tickets)** reconciled directly in Decision 14 above
(corrected text, not a new section): the immunity applies only in
strict mode (`Dual.Require=true`), the only one v9 uses.

**Point 2: size per TLS message, per profile, per direction,
measured in the same round (normal, tickets off).**
`measure.sh` gained a second tshark query
(`-Y tls.handshake -e tls.handshake.type -e tls.handshake.length`),
decrypted via the same keylog -- the size of each message = 4 bytes
of handshake header + the declared length (`tls.handshake.length`).
Confirmed against the isolated ClientHello (the only number with no
grouping ambiguity): Classical 332+4=336, real frame 341 (336 +
5B of TLS record header -- a single record, no CCS, no AEAD tag,
because the ClientHello is never encrypted). The others already
arrive encrypted; the number below is the size of the MESSAGE inside
the record, not the entire encrypted record.

| Message | Classical | PQC | Hybrid-v8 | Hybrid-AND |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ClientHello | 336 | 1.779 | 1.876 | 1.858 |
| ServerHello | 187 | 1.658 | 1.755 | 1.755 |
| EncryptedExtensions | 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 |
| CertificateRequest | 109 | 104 | 111 | 98 |
| Certificate (server) | 913 | 5.632 | 6.255 | 6.582 |
| CertificateVerify (server) | 264 | 3.317 | 264 | 3.575 |
| Finished (server) | 36 | 36 | 36 | 36 |
| Certificate (client) | 800 | 5.519 | 6.144 | 6.356 |
| CertificateVerify (client) | 264 | 3.317 | 264 | 3.575 |
| Finished (client) | 36 | 36 | 36 | 36 |
| **Sum, client->server direction** (client's CH+Cert+CV+Fin) | 1.436 | 10.651 | 8.320 | 11.825 |
| **Sum, server->client direction** (server's SH+EE+CR+Cert+CV+Fin) | 1.519 | 10.757 | 8.431 | 12.056 |
| **Total measured at the Handshake() boundary, already excluding the 1st HTTP request -- client->server** | **1.513** | **10.728** | **8.397** | **11.902** |
| **Total measured at the Handshake() boundary, already excluding the 1st HTTP request -- server->client** | **1.640** | **10.878** | **8.552** | **12.177** |
| Record-layer overhead (measured - sum of messages) | 77 / 121 | 77 / 121 | 77 / 121 | 77 / 121 |

The record-layer overhead (5B TLS 1.3 record headers + 1 inner type
byte + 16B AEAD tag per encrypted record, plus the compatibility
ChangeCipherSpec record) comes out to **exactly
77B in the client->server direction and 121B in the server->client
direction, across the 4 profiles, with no exception** -- this makes
sense: the NUMBER of messages per flight is identical across the 4
profiles (always 1 ClientHello; always the server's
SH+EE+CR+Cert+CV+Fin; always the client's Cert+CV+Fin), only the
CONTENT varies, and the record overhead depends on how many records
exist, not on each one's size. This consistency is itself an
additional confirmation (a fourth, beyond the three already reported
in Decision 14) that the measurement is correct across all 4 profiles
equally, not just by coincidence in one of them.

**Point 3: gateway times per stage, per profile (same round,
normal mode, without the diagnostic-pause bias).**

| Profile | `handshakeDurationUs` | `requestDurationUs` |
|---|---|---|
| Classical | 4.752 | 30 |
| PQC | 2.813 | 63 |
| Hybrid-v8 | 5.402 | 43 |
| Hybrid-AND | 8.734 | 115 |

N=1 per profile -- proof that the instrumentation measures the
correct stage (handshake isolated from the request, no contamination
by the ticket diagnostic pause, see Decision 14), not yet a
statistical campaign (that is a larger-N, pilot/T7 undertaking).
Hybrid-AND is slower than the other 3 both in the handshake (more
bytes to generate/verify: two complete chains) and in the
response-serving stage (more `ConnState` work considering two
certificate sets) -- expected direction, exact magnitude only with
more samples.

**Point 4: what initcwnd=10 implies for v8's unattributed residue
(handshake time above expectation that the thesis had not yet
explained), and which component measured by T6 might explain it.**

With `initcwnd=10` covering the entire flight of any of the 4
profiles in ONE window (Decision 14), the hypothesis that the residue
came from an extra RTT due to a congestion-window overflow is
**ruled out for the latency tiers already used in this thesis
(14-320ms)** -- no flight, not even Hybrid-AND's (12.177B), comes
close to the 14,600B limit. This shifts the explanation to two
components that T6 now measures for the first time, separately, and
that v7/v8 never isolated:

1. **Session-ticket generation/transmission cost.** v7/v8 always ran
   with tickets ON (Decision 13) -- every handshake paid the cost of
   ENCRYPTING and sending a ticket that embeds the peer's certificate
   chain (Decision 14), **1.691 to 11.129B extra, depending on the
   profile**, never accounted for as a separate line in any previous
   report. This cost (AEAD encryption of a blob of a few KB, plus the
   corresponding network write) is a direct candidate for part of the
   residue -- especially in the PQC/Hybrid profiles, where the ticket
   is larger because the client's certificate is larger.
2. **CPU cost of the primitives themselves (signing, verifying, KEX),
   now measured in isolation by `bench`** (Decision 14): this had
   never been isolated as a fraction of total handshake time in
   v7/v8 -- it was implicitly inside the total time, never decomposed.

**Not decided here, recorded for T7/the pilot:** confirming whether
the sum (ticket cost, when on + measured CPU cost) actually accounts
for v8's historical residue would require reprocessing v8's raw data
(outside this round's scope, which is v9's local Phase 1) -- what this
round delivers is the TWO missing pieces for that reckoning, not the
reckoning closed.

Same rules: no action on AWS, no commit before the scanner, report in
chat.

## 16. T7, DRAFT acceptance criteria before the pilot -- for Luciano's review, not executed, no tag created

**Status of this draft: a proposal, not approved.** None of these
criteria is to be taken as closed merely for being listed here --
each one receives its own status (CLOSED, with the evidence that
closes it; or PENDING, with what is missing). The `v9-prereg` tag only
goes out after Luciano's explicit approval of this draft, and only
after ALL the criteria below are CLOSED (or explicitly waived by him).

**(a) Full local flow, with v8's counts, zero errors.**
Criterion: the 4 profiles (Classical, PQC, Hybrid-v8, Hybrid-AND) run
locally against the real stack (`mock_as`, `insurance-server-lambdas`,
`localstack`, `mongo`, unmodified), producing exactly 44

## 17. T6b, full local flow: the 4 profiles ran end to end against the real stack (mock_as and insurance-server-lambdas untouched), 44 HTTP calls and 0 errors across all 4, with three real bugs found and fixed along the way; mTLS connection-count divergence reported, not forced to match

**Risk verified before writing any business code:**
`client_one` uses `token_endpoint_auth_method: "private_key_jwt"`
(`init_clients.json`) -- the client assertion's signature is verified
by the AS against a REGISTERED JWKS (`mongo_seed`), a credential
ENTIRELY SEPARATE from the mTLS certificate carrying the connection.
Confirmed by reading `thesis/scripts/opin_flow.py`'s
`load_client_signing_key()` and `mock-service-os/mock_as/mongo-seed/
start.sh`: both already fall back to the real classical setup
(`client_one.jwks`/`client_one_pub.jwks`, RSA-4096, PS256) for
ANY profile that is not literally `"pqc"` or `"hybrid"` --
`"hibrido-and"` falls into this fallback for free, with no need for
any change in `mongo_seed` or in `opin_flow.py`'s signing. This
confirmed that no change would be needed in `mock_as` or
`insurance-server-lambdas` -- the mTLS mechanism swap (v9) is
completely orthogonal to client authentication at the token endpoint
(which uses a different key, a different protocol).

**Real empirical baseline, BEFORE any change, against the 100%
original stack:** the real `mtls` restarted (`docker compose up
mtls`), the original `opin_flow.py` run with no modification --
`run_insurance_flow('classic')` + `run_person_flow('classic')`:
**20 + 24 = 44 HTTP calls, 0 errors.** This confirms exactly the
number already established (`v8/DECISIONS.md`, Decisions 89/9064/10719)
and serves as a control: any divergence that appears later is from MY
harness, not from the real stack.

**Architecture (see `thesis/results/v9/integration/`):**
- `gateway/business.go` + `business_server.go` (new): gives
  `mock_mtls/main.go`'s business layer (reverse proxy to
  `auth:3000`/`mockapi:8080`, token introspection,
  `/root-ca.pem`/`/issuer-ca.pem`) back to v9's fork, WITHOUT SSA
  (confirmed by directly reading `opin_flow.py`: neither flow calls

  pre-registered, it does not go through DCR) and without

- `proxy/relay.go` (new): persistent relay mode (the counterpart of

  ephemeral self-signed certificate (same mechanism as the real

  covering the 4 profiles including Hybrid-AND, which the real
  `tls_kem_proxy` does not have). Enabled by `-listen`.
- `thesis/scripts/opin_flow.py` (EDITED -- the only production file

**Integration with the real stack:** the real `mtls` container was
stopped (`docker stop`, never removed); a `v9-mtls` container (my
image, `business` mode) joined the SAME
`insurance-server-lambdas_default` network with the SAME network

matls-auth.local auth.local matls-api.local api.local directory`) --
`auth`/`mockapi`/`mongodb`/`psql`/`localstack` stayed up, unchanged,

(`docker run -v`, confirmed working normally in this environment with

correct that earlier understanding).

**Three real bugs found and fixed along the way, each found by
actually running it, not foreseen statically:**

1. **DNS round-robin between the real `mtls` and the new `v9-mtls`.**
   An intermittent error ("certificate is valid for ..., not mtls") on
   the first attempt -- cause: the REAL `mtls` container was still
   running (I had restarted it to measure the baseline and forgot to
   stop it), and both (the real `mtls` + `v9-mtls`) had the `mtls`
   alias registered on the same network at the same time -- Docker's
   embedded DNS alternated between the two. Fixed by stopping the real
   `mtls` before continuing.

2. **`internalCallerConfig` with `ClientCAs` fixed to `ca.crt`,
   diverging from the original.** Under `pqc`, the
   `InsurerAdapter.getConsent()` reentrant call (via SNI
   `matls-api.local`) failed with
   `certificate signed by unknown authority` -- `setup_ssm.sh`
   publishes `op_pqc.crt` (signed by `root_ca_pqc`, NOT by `ca.crt`)
   as the AS's transport certificate under that profile. The ORIGINAL
   `mock_mtls/main.go` does not have this problem because its
   `internalCallerConfig := *cfg` INHERITS the `ClientCAs` from the
   main config (which `caCertPool()` already expands to trust
   `root_ca_pqc.crt` under `CRYPTO_PROFILE=pqc`) -- I had fixed a
   separate pool, with only `ca.crt`, diverging on this detail. Fixed:
   the pool now also trusts `root_ca_pqc.crt` when the profile is
   `pqc` (`business_server.go`'s `attachInternalCallerCarveOut`).

3. **`VerifyPeerCertificate` unintentionally inherited in the
   carve-out.** Under `hybrid`, the same reentrant call failed with
   `ML-DSA-65 alt signature verification failed` -- Hybrid-v8's AND
   X.509 gate (which verifies the alternative signature against v9's
   OWN ML-DSA CA, `hibrido_v8_ca_mldsa.crt`) was being inherited by
   `internalCfg` via `cfg.Clone()`, but `op_hybrid.crt` (the AS's real
   certificate under that profile) has its alternative signature made
   by the REAL production ML-DSA CA, a completely different key. The
   internal caller was never meant to be part of v9's own
   profile-specific identity scheme. Fixed: an explicit `internalCfg.
   VerifyPeerCertificate = nil` in the carve-out.

**Final result, the 4 profiles, `auth`/`mongo_seed`/`mockapi` recreated
with the matching `CRYPTO_PROFILE` before each test (classic/pqc/
hybrid; hibrido-and runs with the backend set to classic, on purpose --
see below), `insurance-server-lambdas` and `mock_as` never edited:**

| Profile | HTTP calls (insurance+person) | Errors | Group (client connections) | DualAuthenticated |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Classical | 20+24=44 | 0 | CurveP384, 7/7 | n/a (false, expected) |
| PQC | 20+24=44 | 0 | MLKEM1024, 7/7 | n/a (false, expected) |
| Hybrid-v8 | 20+24=44 | 0 | SecP384r1MLKEM1024, 7/7 | n/a (false, expected -- X.509 gate confirmed passing in the logs) |
| Hybrid-AND | 20+24=44 | 0 | SecP384r1MLKEM1024, 7/7 | **true, 7/7 client connections** |

All 44 calls returned success (no Python exception, no
`raise_for_status()` triggering) across the 4 profiles. On ALL client
connections (SNI `mtls`) of the 4 profiles, the negotiated group
matched the profile's expectation exactly; in Hybrid-AND specifically,
`DualAuthenticated
= true` in 100% of those connections (confirmed by the gateway's own
log, not inferred).

**Why the backend stays on `classic` for Hybrid-AND:** the AND
mechanism is entirely a transport-layer matter (dual proof of
possession in the TLS handshake) -- it changes nothing about how the
AS signs JWTs or how the RS signs responses. Leaving `auth`/`mockapi`
on `classic` for this profile is a deliberate choice, not an omission:
there is no (and should be no) "CRYPTO_PROFILE=hibrido-and" in the
real `mock_as`/`insurance-server-lambdas`, because nothing there needs
to know the AND mechanism is in use.

`InsurerAdapter.getConsent()` firing once per consent authorization).

**JWTs (28) and /jwks (4): extracted and confirmed in Decision 18**,
