**2. KEYLOG_PATH and the Go gateway.**

**(a) Off across every timed window, proven with a test.**
A real finding this round (not a hypothesis): Decision 52's first
version turned `KEYLOG_PATH` on in EVERY `start_block` -- that is, on
EVERY timed run, not just during `dedicated_capture`. This would have
introduced extra I/O per handshake (writing the session key to disk)
across all 60 real runs, never present before this round -- a real
MEASUREMENT effect, not merely theoretical.
**Fixed:** `_launch_gateway(profile, keylog=False)` (a new method,
factored out of `start_block`) is the ONLY place that decides the
flag -- `start_block` always calls it with `keylog=False` (never
turns it on); ONLY `dedicated_capture` calls it with `keylog=True`,
restarting the SAME container ONLY when it is about to capture.
Guarantee: the environment variable (`-e KEYLOG_PATH=...`), set only
on the second call to `_launch_gateway`, never the first. New tests
(`test_orchestrator.py`):
`test_start_block_nunca_liga_keylog_path` (green), `test_run_execution_
nunca_menciona_keylog` (green), `test_dedicated_capture_liga_keylog_
so_na_propria_reinicializacao` (confirms both calls exist and
differ), `test_mutante_keylog_sempre_ligado_e_pego` (a mutant that
reproduces THIS round's ORIGINAL bug -- confirming the tests above
genuinely depend on the fix).

**(b) The gateway's restart happens outside any timed window, never
altering already-measured data.** Structural, not just by
convention: `run_pilot` runs the ENTIRE block loop (the 60 runs +
each block's `stop_block`) first; ONLY AFTER THAT, in a SEPARATE
loop (`if not skip_dedicated_captures: for profile... dedicated_
capture(...)`), do the dedicated captures run. `dedicated_capture`
now calls `self.start_block(profile, route)` (rebuilding the correct
backend/proxy/signer for THIS capture's PROFILE -- a real finding:
without this, the gateway that would be running at this point would
be the LAST block in the grid's, not necessarily the right profile)
and only THEN `_launch_gateway(..., keylog=True)`. Both restarts
happen inside this second loop, which only begins after ALL 60 runs'
data has already been written to disk (`piloto_calls.
json`/`criterio6_execucoes.json`) -- restarting the container after
that can NEVER alter already-persisted data. `dedicated_capture`
ends with `self.stop_block(...)`, symmetric cleanup.

**(c) Gateway binary hash/identity -- there is NO pre-registered hash
to compare against, but there IS a pre-registered MECHANISM to
guarantee integrity, and it remains correct.** Searched across the
whole frozen `v9-prereg`: no literal hash of any `gateway` build was
ever recorded at any earlier point -- there is no "old hash" to
compare against a "new" one. What DOES EXIST, pre-registered (the
PKI/binary/collection delivery section): **"Binary delivery:
the same path -- the operator `scp`s the `gateway`/`proxy` (plus the
`.sha256`) to the control instance, the control instance `scp`s it
to each destination instance... each instance runs `sha256sum -c`
before using it."** This mechanism ALWAYS recomputes the hash from
the binary that will actually be used (never reuses an old value) --
my `KEYLOG_PATH` fix changes the compiled binary (any source change
does), and the pre-registered mechanism correctly captures this by
construction, with no extra action needed from me. **Honest, separate
finding:** the current `SSHExecutor`
(`orchestrator.py`) NEVER implemented this `scp`+
`sha256sum -c` mechanism for the gateway -- it assumes a Docker image
already built on the instance (`docker run ... mockopin-v9-gateway`),
with no hash verification at all. A PRE-EXISTING gap (not caused by
this round), recorded here for completeness, not fixed now (it
requires deciding BETWEEN the pre-registered binary+sha256 mechanism
OR formalizing the build-by-Docker-image as the real method -- a
design decision, not an implementation bug, outside this round's
scope).

**5. handshakeBytesIn deviation (+22/+28B) -- cause isolated, not just
assumed.**

Captured again, now looking at EACH message individually (not just
the aggregate) against `evaluate_criteria.py`'s REAL baselines
(`HANDSHAKE_MESSAGE_BASELINE`/`CLIENTHELLO_BASELINE`), for the
Hybrid-v8 profile:

| Message (client) | Observed (raw) | Baseline (raw) | Deviation |
|---|---|---|---|
| ClientHello | **1900** | **1872** | **+28B** |
| Certificate_client | 6140 | 6140 | 0 |
| CertificateVerify_client | 260 | 260 | 0 |
| Finished_client | 32 | 32 | 0 |

**The deviation is 100% concentrated in the ClientHello -- every
other message matched EXACTLY, 0B of difference.** The cause is
isolated in the code, not assumed:
`thesis/results/v9/integration/negtest/main.go`'s
`baseConfig()` (used to trigger the connection for this local
validation, via `-scenario matrix`) sets
`MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS12` for ALL profiles generically --
while `proxy/main.go`'s
`singleChainClientConfig()` (the pilot's REAL client) receives
`minVersion` PER PROFILE, and `hibrido-v8`/`pqc` are called with
`tls.VersionTLS13` explicitly (only `classico` uses `TLS12`). A
`ClientHello` that declares TLS 1.2 support HAS to announce the
legacy cipher-suite list and additional signature_algorithms valid
for 1.2 -- exactly what inflates the `ClientHello` by ~22-28B,
varying per profile according to that extra list's exact content.
**It is not a NewSessionTicket (that is post-handshake, never counted
in `handshakeBytesIn/Out`, which closes the snapshot right after
`Handshake()` returns) nor TLS 1.3 record-layer overhead (confirmed
record by record: each AEAD record has 17B of overhead -- 1B
content-type + 16B tag -- IDENTICAL on both sides, already baked into
both numbers, never the cause of the DIFFERENCE between them).**

**Conclusion: this deviation is an artifact of the VALIDATION METHOD
(negtest used as the connection trigger for this local capture),
never a property of the pilot's real client**
(`opin_flow.py`/proxy, which correctly pins `MinVersion` per profile)
-- it should not appear in a measurement made with the real client.

**Pre-registered tolerance for `handshakeBytesIn/Out` -- does NOT
EXIST, explicitly stated.** What the pre-registration defines
(Decision 20/29/30) is tolerance for criterion 1 (sizes PER
MESSAGE, via tshark): today, **0B for the ClientHello, ±4B for
Certificate, 0B for the rest** -- but that measures a DIFFERENT
quantity (each decrypted message's `tls.handshake.length` field),
not the aggregate `handshakeBytesIn/Out` counter the gateway itself
logs (RAW bytes on the TCP connection, including record/AEAD
overhead). No tolerance was pre-registered for this second number
specifically.

**Proposal, not applied retroactively:** adopt the SAME 0B tolerance
criterion_1 already uses for the ClientHello (the only message where
some deviation historically appeared), propagated to the aggregate --
that is, `handshakeBytesIn/Out` measured with the pilot's REAL client
should match EXACTLY (0B) against the historical values
(8.397/8.552, 11.902/12.177), since every individual message is
already required to be within 0B/±4B and the aggregate is just their
sum plus the fixed protocol overhead (identical across runs).
Proposal recorded here for Luciano to decide -- NOT applied to any
existing criterion this round, and the real measurement (when done
with the real client, not negtest) needs to be redone before
declaring this tolerance met or not.

**1. Gateway binary verification in the real SSHExecutor -- implemented.**

A mechanism ALREADY PRE-REGISTERED (`v9-prereg`, "Binary delivery"
section: "the operator `scp`s the `gateway`/`proxy`... each instance
runs
`sha256sum -c` before using it"), never implemented before this
round (an honest gap from Decision 53, item 2c) -- now implemented in
`SSHExecutor`:

- `_local_gateway_binary_info()`: extracts `/gateway` from the
  already-built local Docker image (`docker create`+`docker cp`, the
  same pattern as `certs/Makefile`), genuinely computes the sha256,
  runs `go version -m` via `mockopin-v9-toolchain` (static reading,
  never executing the binary) and reads the `/build_metadata.json`
  the toolchain ITSELF already records (`go_tag`, `go_commit`, the
  AND patch's hash) -- confirmed by genuinely running it this
  session: `go1.27.3`, path
  `mockopin-v9-gateway`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 GOARCH=amd64 GOOS=linux`.
- `_verify_gateway_binary(profile, route)`: `scp`s the binary to the
  server, writes the `.sha256` remotely, runs `sha256sum -c` THERE
  -- raises `RuntimeError` BEFORE `_launch_gateway` runs if it
  diverges.
- `_verify_running_gateway_binary(verification)`: closes the full
  loop -- after the container comes up, it checks that the binary
  INSIDE it (`docker exec ... sha256sum /gateway`) matches the SAME
  hash verified in transit (otherwise the transit verification would
  prove little, the Docker image could have been built from a
  different binary).
- `start_block` calls both, in this order, BEFORE any run.
  `dedicated_capture` re-checks the container (not the transit, which
  does not change) after restarting with `KEYLOG_PATH`.
- Each block's manifest (`run_pilot`/`run_smoke_gate`) gains
  `gateway_binary_verifications`: one entry per block, with the
  sha256, `go_version_m`, `go_build_version`, toolchain metadata, and
  both verification results (transit + running container).

6 client-facing connections per run = **120 samples per profile,

| Profile | N samples | min (in/out) | max (in/out) | deviation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Classical | 120 | 1.513 / 1.640 | 1.513 / 1.640 | **0B** |

**Zero variation across ALL 480 samples, on all 4 profiles.** The
local environment (Docker containers on the same host) is fully
deterministic for this measure.

**Possible variation sources, separated by where they CAN differ on AWS:**

| Source | Can it differ on AWS? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Certificate SAN (real private IP/EIP vs. loopback) | **YES** | Already measured and compensated (Decision 28/29): -14B (single-leaf-certificate profiles) or -28B (Hybrid-AND, 2 leaves) -- a FIXED, known difference, not random |
| Certificate's ASN.1 serial number (1-byte padding if the most significant byte has the high bit set) | **YES, but limited** | Varies per certificate BUILD (`make certs`), never per run -- ±2B per leaf, ±4B for Hybrid-AND (2 leaves); this is ALREADY the basis of criterion 1's `CERTIFICATE_TOLERANCE_B=4B` |
| SNI ("mtls", fixed) | **NO** | Confirmed by Decision 30: byte-for-byte identical regardless of the real target -- never depends on the destination's IP/DNS |
| Session tickets (`TICKETS_DISABLED`) | **NO, if the config is the same** | Always `true` in every launch of this project -- if it ever diverged, it would add `NewSessionTicket` to handshakeBytesOut (never tested here because it has always been off) |
| Client's minimum TLS version (`MinVersion`) | **NO, if the binary is the same** | The EXACT cause of the deviation closed in item 2 -- controlled by item 1's binary verification |
| TLS 1.3 random fields (32B Random, key_share) | **NO** | FIXED size by specification -- only the CONTENT is random, never the length |

**Proposed tolerance** (for Luciano's approval, NOT applied to any
existing criterion this round): **0B for `handshakeBytesOut`
on the 3 single-certificate profiles, ±4B for Hybrid-AND's
`handshakeBytesIn` (2 leaf certificates, doubling the serial-number
margin) --
and, when measured in an environment with a SAN different from
loopback (the real AWS), add the FIXED, already-measured offset
(-14B/-28B) to the baseline before applying this same tolerance,
never treating this offset as "unknown variance."** Justification:
480 real local samples gave 0B of variation; the ONE legitimate
variation source that remains (the serial number) is the same one
criterion 1 already tolerates for individual messages. Proposal
recorded, not applied -- it needs Luciano's approval before it holds
for any criterion.

**2. SAN and the Certificate gate -- a viable technique, validated against the real BASELINE.**

Finding: `make certs SERVER_IPS="<real IP>,::1"` (keeping the COMMA
and the
`::1`, only swapping the IPv4's VALUE) preserves the SAME SAN entry
count/type as the baseline (`127.0.0.1,::1`) -- an IPv4 entry always
takes 4 bytes, an IPv6 one always 16 bytes in ASN.1 DER, REGARDLESS
of the value. Confirmed by running `make certs` 20 times (10
private-style IPs, 10 public-EIP-style, a different value on each
build), measuring each certificate's real DER against
`BASELINE_CERT_DER_SIZES`:

```
all_zero: True, n_builds: 20, n_rows: 80, nonzero rows: 0
```

**80/80 combinations (20 builds x 4 profiles), ZERO delta against the
BASELINE -- not just against its own prediction -- in both
directions.**

**Alternative attempted and discarded:** DNS-name padding (adding a
calculated-length name to compensate for the `::1` that would be
removed). Tested with 15, 17, and 18 characters -- deviations of
-2B, +1B, and +3B respectively (per server leaf; doubled on
Hybrid-AND) -- it does NOT scale linearly with the name's length
(a boundary effect in the extension-length's ASN.1 encoding, never
calibrated to exactly 0B in 3 attempts). The IP+`::1` technique is
simpler, exact by construction (does not depend on calibrating any
length) and provenly 0B -- preferred, with no reservations.

**No Amendment needed** -- the technique is viable (confirmed, not
the opposite) and changes no code in this project, only the
`SERVER_IPS` VALUE passed to `make certs` on the pilot's day (an
operational choice, documented in `PILOT_READINESS.md`, section d).

## 62. Real finding during Phase A's real execution (a real apply, 5 instances up) -- `deliver_campaign_key` was writing the key with CRLF (Windows line breaks), rejected by the real destination ssh/scp ("invalid format"); fixed to write in binary, with no newline translation at all

Nothing outside the authorized scope. Branch `v9/fase1-local`, commit
and push (Luciano's rule 5 -- every fix gets a Decision + commit).

**Finding, live, at Step 4 of the real rehearsal (checking Docker
readiness on the 4 hosts via a relay through the control instance):**
the 4 SSH attempts from the control instance to the real hosts failed
with `Load key "/home/ec2-user/
.ssh/campaign_key": invalid format` / `Permission denied`. The key
had ALREADY been delivered successfully in Step 3 (`deliver_campaign_key`,
with no error reported) -- the problem was the file's CONTENT, not
the delivery itself.

**Root cause:** `Path.write_text(pem, encoding="utf-8")`, in TEXT
mode, on Windows Python, translates every `\n` to the OS's default
newline (`\r\n`) before writing -- an SSH key with CRLF in the middle
is invalid for the real OpenSSH key parser (confirmed live, not
assumed). It never showed up in the tests because the tests stub the
entire `cli._run` -- none of them writes the real file and then tries
to use it with a real `ssh`/`scp`.

**Fixed:** `deliver_campaign_key` now normalizes (`\r\n` -> `\n`, in
case any came from some pipe beforehand) and writes with
`Path.write_bytes` (binary, never `write_text`) -- exact bytes, no
newline translation possible. 2 new tests
(`test_deliver_campaign_key_grava_bytes_sem_cr`, confirms `b"\r\n"`
is absent from the file captured before `TemporaryDirectory` removes
it).

**Retry 1/3 for this problem** (Luciano's rule 3) -- re-running
Step 3 (key delivery) and Step 4 (Docker readiness) again, with
the fix.

**Tests:** 142/142 (140 before + 2 new), all passing.

scripts/pki_relay.py` (fix), `thesis/results/v9/campaign/tests/
test_pki_relay.py` (2 new tests), `thesis/results/v9/DECISIONS.md`
(this Decision).

## 63. Second real finding in the same real Phase A -- `deliver_images.py` used `sh -c "docker save ... > <windows-path>"`, which corrupts the redirection with a backslash path; fixed to `docker save -o <path>` (pure argv, no shell in between)

Branch `v9/fase1-local`, commit and push. Retry 2/3 for the same
"Windows path problem" (same family as Decision 62's finding, but in
a different file/command -- counted as a new problem for rule 3, not
a repeat of the same one).

**Finding, live, at Step 7 (`deliver_images.py`):** `docker save`
returned `returncode=0` (success) but the `.tar` never existed at the
expected path -- a `FileNotFoundError` on the `tar_path.stat()` call
right afterward. Cause: `cli._run(["sh", "-c", f"docker save
{image} > {tar_path}"])` with `tar_path` a WINDOWS path
(`C:\Users\...\gateway.tar`) interpolated INSIDE a shell string --
the backslashes break the redirection parsing for the real `sh`
(git-bash), which accepts the command (exit 0) but never writes to
the right place.

**Fixed:** `docker save` has its OWN `-o <file>` flag -- switched to
`cli._run(["docker", "save", "-o", str(tar_path),
docker_image])`, pure argv (a list), no shell interpreting the path.
Also added an explicit check
(`tar_path.is_file()`) after `docker save` -- never again trusting

## 64. Third real finding, same CRLF family (Decisions 62/63), found via a preventive audit after the second one -- deliver_images.py was writing the .sha256 and gateway_binary_info.json with write_text (Windows), corrupting the real sha256sum -c verification on the control instance

Branch `v9/fase1-local`, commit and push. Retry 3/3 for the
"Windows path/encoding problem" (rule 3 -- on the 3rd, if it
persists, the rule says to tear down and stop; I decided to audit the
ENTIRE rest of the package for this pattern BEFORE spending this 3rd
attempt, so as not to hit it again at a 4th, unchecked spot).

**Finding, live, resuming Step 7 after Decision 63's fix:**
`docker save -o` now correctly created the `.tar`, but `sha256sum -c`

directory`. The same root cause as Decisions 62/63 -- `sha_path.
write_text(f"{sha256}  {tar_path.name}\n")` writes `\r\n` on
Windows; the `\r` sticks to the file NAME when the real (Linux)
`sha256sum` parses the line on the control instance.

**Preventive audit (before spending the 3rd/last retry):**
`grep -rn "write_text(" thesis/results/v9/campaign/scripts/*.py` --
9 occurrences. Classified:
- `cli.py` (`_LocalShellShim`): only manual LOCAL validation, never
  exercised by the real pilot (`orchestrator.py --mode ssh` never
  turns the shim on) -- no risk here.
- `collect_artifacts.py` (`.pull-verified`): written on the
  OPERATOR, only its EXISTENCE is checked afterward (`cleanup.py`),
  never its content -- no risk.
- `orchestrator.py` (manifest/logs/criterio6/captures): written
  INSIDE the `orchestrator.py` process, which runs on the CONTROL
  instance (Linux, Decision 59) -- `write_text` there never
  translates to CRLF (only Windows does that) -- no risk.
- `deliver_images.py` (`.sha256`, `gateway_binary_info.json`): BOTH
  written on the OPERATOR (Windows) and then READ by a real Linux
  process (`sha256sum`/`json.loads` on the control instance) --
  **real risk, both fixed**.

**Fixed:** both `write_text` calls in `deliver_images.py` swapped for
`write_bytes` with an explicit `\n`, the same pattern as Decisions
62/63.

(`test_deliver_images_sha_path_nunca_tem_cr`/`test_deliver_images_
gateway_info_json_nunca_tem_cr`) -- 144/144 (142 before + 2 new),

## 66. Real finding at Step 9 (--exercise-start-stop) -- `_tcp_preflight` always failed on the FIRST block of any route, because it checked port 443 before the gateway existed; fixed to distinguish "connection refused" (network OK, the app just hasn't come up yet -- expected) from a real timeout (the only case that still fails)

Branch `v9/fase1-local`, commit and push.

**Finding, live, resuming Step 9:** `_tcp_preflight` aborted with
"client could not reach ...:443" -- real output: `bash: connect:
Connection refused`. Investigating: the real v8 had `mtls` as a
PERSISTENT docker-compose service (never recreated by
`switch_crypto_profile.py`), so port 443 was always up when
`preflight_tcp.py` (the original) ran. v9's `_launch_
gateway` does `docker rm -f`+`docker run` on every profile switch --
`_tcp_preflight`, being deliberately the FIRST step of
`start_block`, runs BEFORE the gateway has ever come up on the first
block of any route (or in an isolated exercise like `--exercise-
start-stop`) -- "connection refused" is exactly what is expected at
that moment, never a symptom of a wrong Security Group.

**Distinction that was missing:** "connection refused" (a fast RST)
PROVES the packet reached the server's kernel and was rejected only
because nothing is listening yet -- POSITIVE evidence the Security
Group let the traffic through. Only a genuine TIMEOUT (no response,
packet silently dropped) is real evidence of a wrong SG/VPC.

**Fixed:** the remote command now distinguishes the 3 cases (the
real `timeout`'s `$?`: `0`=OK, `124`=TIMEOUT, anything else=REFUSED)
-- `ok = outcome in ("OK", "REFUSED")`, only `TIMEOUT` aborts.
`tcp_preflight_results` gains an `outcome` field (besides `ok`), so
the audit shows which of the 3 genuinely happened.

**Tests:** `test_tcp_preflight_aborta_se_timeout_de_verdade`
(renamed/fixed -- simulates an explicit TIMEOUT, no longer a generic
"FAIL") + `test_tcp_preflight_passa_com_connection_refused` (new --
proves REFUSED passes and lets the entire block proceed) -- 145
in total (144 before + 1 new).

**Commit and push** (`v9/fase1-local`): `thesis/results/v9/campaign/
scripts/orchestrator.py` (`_tcp_preflight` fixed),
`thesis/results/v9/campaign/tests/test_orchestrator.py` (2 tests),
`thesis/results/v9/DECISIONS.md` (this Decision).

## 68. Amendment -- the delivery verification mechanism switched from Image ID to content (tar sha256 + RootFS.Layers + Config subset + the binary's sha256 inside the container), confirmed stable across Docker versions by a local test with docker:25-dind; no pre-registered criterion nor what is measured changes

Branch `v9/fase1-local`, commit and push. Luciano's decision, a
direct response to Decision 67's finding: "nothing else is decided,
proceed this way"
+ a detailed instruction for item 1 of the prompt.

**Reason.** Decision 67 stopped the real Phase A because the
gateway's Image ID
(`.Id`), after `docker load` on the real server, diverged from the
one pinned in PINS.json -- even with the binary inside the container
byte-identical to the pin. The root cause (the operator's Docker
29.9.1 vs. the real server's 25.0.16) is structural: any real EC2
instance tends to run an older Docker (a distribution package) than
the operator's, so the Image ID-based fail-closed mechanism
pre-registered in Decision 55 would never survive a real execution,
on any future attempt.

**Local investigation, without AWS, before any change.** I brought
up a `docker:25-dind` (resolving to Docker 25.0.5, the same version
family as the real AMI, 25.0.16) alongside the operator's Docker
(29.9.1). For each of the 4 pinned images, I did a `docker load` of
the SAME `.tar` on both daemons and compared `docker image inspect`:

- `.RootFS.Layers` (the content-addressable layer digest list):
  IDENTICAL across both versions, across the 4 images.
- `.Config` (the Entrypoint/Cmd/Env/ExposedPorts subset): IDENTICAL
  across both versions, across the 4 images.
- `.Id` (the final Image ID): DIVERGES between the two versions,
  exactly reproducing what was seen live on the real server (Decision
  67).
- For gateway/proxy: the sha256 of the binary INSIDE the container
  loaded on DinD matched exactly the one pinned in PINS.json in both
  cases.
- `docker save` of the same local image id (never rebuilt), two
  independent invocations: the same file sha256 both times (proving
  the `.tar` itself is reproducible, not just the binary inside it).

Conclusion: layers and config ARE stable across Docker versions for a
byte-identical `.tar`; only the Image ID is not. The first branch of
Luciano's item 1 applies (pin by `.tar` sha256 + RootFS.Layers +
Config subset; the Image ID drops to informational).

**New mechanism, in this order (every abort occurs BEFORE any real
execution on the image):**
1. The sha256 of the freshly built local `.tar` checks against the
   pinned `tar_sha256` (`deliver_images.py`, 1st hop,
   operator->control) -- if the local image was rebuilt, it aborts
   here, never getting to scp.
2. The sha256 of the `.tar` staged on the control instance checks
   against the same `tar_sha256` (`orchestrator._deliver_image`,
   before the 2nd hop).
3. After `docker load` on the host (server/client), `RootFS.Layers`
   checks against the pinned `rootfs_layers`.
4. `Config` (Entrypoint/Cmd/Env/ExposedPorts) checks against the
   pinned `config_subset`.
5. For gateway/proxy (which have their own Go binary): the sha256 of
   the binary INSIDE the container loaded on the host (never of the
   isolated `.tar`) checks against the pinned `binary_sha256` -- the
   same content guarantee Decision 55 already required, just now
   verified after the real `docker load` on the host, not only on the
   `.tar`.

The Image ID (`.Id`) continues to be read and recorded in PINS.json,
but **only as an informational field** -- never compared, never a
reason to abort.

**PINS.json diff (schema, per image; 4 images, the same change on
all):**
```
- "image_id": "sha256:...",                    # the only identity field, fail-closed
+ "tar_sha256": "<the .tar's sha256>",          # NEW -- fail-closed, 2 hops
+ "rootfs_layers": ["sha256:...", ...],         # NEW -- fail-closed, after docker load on the host
+ "config_subset": {                             # NEW -- fail-closed, after docker load on the host
+     "Entrypoint": [...], "Cmd": ..., "Env": [...], "ExposedPorts": ...
+ },
+ "image_id": "sha256:...",                     # KEPT, now informational only
+ "image_id_note": "Informational only -- NEVER verified (Decision 68, see _image_identity_note)."
```
Plus a new top-level field, `_image_identity_note`,
explaining the finding and the new verification order. The gateway
re-pinned in Decision 61 already had `binary_sha256`/`binary_path_in_image`
unchanged -- this Amendment only adds the 3 content fields above,
never touching the already-pinned binary/certificates/sha256.

**Explicit statement (Luciano's rule 6/7e):** this Amendment alters
ONLY the mechanism that verifies the delivered image is the expected
one (an infrastructure integrity check). None of the 7 pre-registered
criteria nor their thresholds changes; no measurement (latency,
bytes, any pilot metric) depends on the Image ID or starts depending
on any of the new fields -- they only decide whether the run CAN
begin, never what is measured during it. No binary, certificate, or
runtime configuration was altered or rebuilt for this Decision.

**Code:** `orchestrator._deliver_image` rewritten (reads `tar_sha256`/
`rootfs_layers`/`config_subset`/`binary_path_in_image`/
`binary_sha256` from PINS.json; aborts on the `.tar`'s sha256 BEFORE
any scp; after `docker load`, checks layers/config/binary and only
then decides `ok`). `deliver_images.py` gains the same `tar_sha256`
check on the 1st hop. `preflight.check_capture_prerequisites`/
`run_capture_preflight` swap the `measure` image's Image ID check for
`RootFS.Layers`+`Config` subset.

**Tests (mutants requested by Luciano, all new or rewritten):** a
tampered local tar fails BEFORE any scp; a tampered layer fails; a
tampered config fails; a binary tampered inside the container fails
(only the image with the swapped binary, the others pass); the
correct case passes with `layers_ok=config_ok=binary_ok=true`
across the 3 images with verifiable binary/content. 151/151 after
this round (145 before + 6 new/rewritten, minus 1 obsolete Image ID
test removed).

**Documentation:** `PILOT_READINESS.md` (the pins section rewritten +
a new "Image ID -- Decision 68" subsection) and `INFRA_REHEARSAL.md`
(Steps 7 and 9 updated, expected output shows the new fields) updated
to reflect the new mechanism.

PINS.json`, `thesis/results/v9/campaign/scripts/orchestrator.py`,
`thesis/results/v9/campaign/scripts/deliver_images.py`,
`thesis/results/v9/campaign/scripts/preflight.py`,
`thesis/results/v9/campaign/tests/test_orchestrator.py`,

## 70. Real finding, live, resuming the real Phase A (a new fleet, Step 9) -- `_launch_gateway` unconditionally used `--network insurance-server-lambdas_default` (only exists in LOCAL validation via the shim), getting the container stuck in "Created" (never "Up") on a real EC2 server; neither `docker run -d` nor the "listening on" wait loop checked the exit code, so the real error only appeared 2 steps later, with no clue to the cause

Branch `v9/fase1-local`, commit and push. A real resumption of Phase
A (item 3 of Luciano's earlier prompt), a new fleet (`terraform apply
-var="self_terminate_hours=1"`, 28 resources, 5 instances, 3
regions) -- account confirmed clean (12 `describe-*` calls, 3
regions, all empty) before the apply.

**Finding, live, at Step 9 (`--exercise-start-stop`):**
`_verify_running_gateway_binary` aborted with `"Error response from
daemon: container ... is not running"`. Investigated via `docker ps -a`
on the real server (2nd hop, through the control instance): the
`v9-mtls` container was in `Created` status (never `Up`) --
`docker run -d` never actually started the container.

**Root cause:** `_launch_gateway` always used `--network
insurance-server-lambdas_default` + 6 `--network-alias` (meant for
internal Docker DNS resolution by OTHER containers of the local
`insurance-server-lambdas` stack, which only comes up when
`local_shim_bridge_
join=True`). On a real EC2 server (`local_shim_bridge_join=False`,
the case for every real remote pilot), this network NEVER exists --
`docker run` failed (network not found), but neither this call nor
the `"listening on"` wait loop below it (`cli.run_ssh(...)`
with no `.returncode` check) caught the error -- the problem only
showed up 2 steps later, in `_verify_running_gateway_binary`, with no
clue to the real cause. This same gap had already been honestly
recorded in `start_block`'s docstring since Decision 49
("For a real remote pilot, this script needs a v9-aware version...
this does NOT exist yet") -- a known, deferred gap, which only
manifested for real on this resumption.

**Why this is a safe fix, never a STOP:** the real client
(`_server_gateway_ip`) always dials the HOST's IP on port 443, never
a Docker alias -- the network/aliases never had any effect on what is
measured (bytes/latency of the real TLS handshake), they only decided
whether OTHER local containers (auth/mockapi, which do not even exist
in the remote pilot) could resolve "mtls" via Docker DNS. Swapping
this for the remote case's only real requirement (publishing the port
on the host) does not touch PINS.json, the pinned binary/certificate,
nor any of the 7 pre-registered criteria.

**Fixed, in `orchestrator.py._launch_gateway`:** `network_flags`
is now conditional on `local_shim_bridge_join` -- `True` keeps the
old network/aliases (local validation, where other compose containers
need to resolve the alias); `False` (the real remote case) now uses
`-p 443:443`. `docker run -d` now has its `.returncode` checked,
aborting immediately with the real output if it fails. The
"listening on" wait loop now also checks whether it found it
("FOUND" in stdout) before proceeding -- if it never finds it within
30s, it aborts with the container's real status (`docker ps -a`) in
the message, instead of letting the error show up 2 steps later with
no context.

**Tests:** 2 new (`test_launch_gateway_aborta_se_docker_run_falha`,
`test_launch_gateway_aborta_se_container_nunca_fica_pronto`) + the 2
existing `_launch_gateway` tests (real remote case / local
validation) gained new assertions checking the correct
`network_flags` in each mode. 156 tests in total.

**Validated live, resuming Step 9 on the SAME real fleet** (after
redeploying the fixed `orchestrator.py` to the control instance via

gateway comes up, logs "listening on", `_verify_running_gateway_binary`
confirms `running_container_sha256_ok: true`.

./../../certs/generated: No such file or directory`.

relative to the script itself (`$(dirname "$0")/../../...`) that
`orchestrator._launch_gateway.real_certs_mount` had BEFORE Decision
58 -- it only makes sense when the script runs inside the real
repository (the operator's laptop). The copy `deliver_source.py`
delivers to the CONTROL instance (`CONTROL_FILES`) never has
`certs/generated` alongside it (`CLIENT_ONLY_FILES` only delivers
that to the CLIENT) -- and even if it did, the
`-v $CERTS_DIR:/certs:ro` mount needs to exist on the HOST that
actually runs `docker run` (client/server, via `on_client`/
`on_gateway`), never on the control instance, which only triggers the
command via SSH. The same bug class, exactly the same reasoning
already fixed in `_launch_gateway` (Decision 58) -- except this shell
script had never received the same treatment.

**Why this is a safe fix, never a STOP:** the certificate mount's
path alters no pinned binary/certificate nor any of the 7
pre-registered criteria -- the SAME certificates (delivered by

(the real client/server) instead of a place that never existed (the

**Infrastructure note (not a code bug, recorded here for
transparency):** before managing to redeliver and retest this fix

L0) became simultaneously unreachable on ports 22 AND 443 from the
operator's machine, for ~8 straight minutes (multiple attempts,

configuration problem: `aws ec2 describe-
instance-status` confirmed all 3 instances with `instance: ok` and

(HTTPS) kept working perfectly the whole time; the control instance's
Security Group confirmed unchanged and correct (rule 22/tcp exactly
for the operator's CIDR, same as the apply's); the IP
The operator's public IP confirmed unchanged; port 22 to a
non-AWS host (github.com) worked normally at the same instant.
Conclusion: a transient network-route problem between the operator's
machine and specifically these 3 instances (`sa-east-1` region),

available as an alternative (`ssm:DescribeInstanceInformation` denied

../../terraform --release-eips --force`, `all_clean: true`,

## 75. Amendment -- the real SAN (SERVER_IPS="<real EIP>,::1") dropped for the pilot, never applied; checked by content that the certificates delivered (certs/generated, mock-service-os/certs) are the same ones already embedded in the pinned images

Luciano's decision, in response to the real Phase A resumption's
report: the real-SAN technique (PILOT_READINESS.md, section d/j-6) is
dropped for the pilot -- no image rebuild, no `make
certs`. The pilot uses the certificates exactly as they are, embedded
in the pinned images. Before proceeding, a content-based proof
(never assumed) was required that the certificates REALLY delivered
to the instances this round (certs/generated, mock-
service-os/certs) are the same ones embedded -- a read-only
investigation, with no rebuild, no AWS call.

**(a) certs/generated (disk) == the certificates embedded in the
pinned images.** Extracted the 16 files (`.crt`, 5 per profile + the
CA for each) from inside `mockopin-v9-gateway:pinned` (`docker run
--entrypoint cat`) and compared by sha256 against
`thesis/results/v9/certs/generated/`: 16/16 identical byte for byte.
`mockopin-v9-proxy:latest` confirmed with the same 5 server
certificates as the gateway (identical sha256). No file rebuilt for
this check.

**(b) mock-service-os/certs -- internal consistency.** Nothing in
this directory is embedded in any image by design
(`business_server.go`: REAL_CERTS_DIR is always MOUNTED, never
copied into an image) -- the possible check here is chain
consistency, not comparison against a baked-in value. `ca.crt`
is the single trust anchor; `root_ca.crt`, `issuer_ca.crt`,
`op.crt`, `mtls.crt`, `client_one.crt`, `client_two.crt` verify
OK against `ca.crt` (`openssl verify -CAfile ca.crt`). The directory
unchanged since 2026-09-29, predating this entire campaign.

**(c) why the real SAN was never necessary.** The SAN of every
embedded server certificate is `DNS:mtls, IP Address:127.0.0.1, IP
Address:0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1` -- loopback, never the real EIP; the "<IP>"
in Luciano's phrasing is always this generic placeholder, never the
pilot's public IP. `negtest/main.go.baseConfig()` fixes `ServerName:
"mtls"` -- the client's hostname verification always checks against
this fixed label (present in every certificate's SAN), never against
the dialed IP. This is why Step 10 (Decisions 72/73/74) closed with a
0B delta on a real network without the SAN containing the EIP:
neither the hostname check nor the byte parity (Decision 56: the
SAN's IPv4 VALUE never affects the DER size) depends on it.
Rebuilding the image to change the SAN would never have had any
effect on either of the two mechanisms that actually matter --
proposal correctly dropped.

**Why this is an Amendment, never a STOP:** no file was altered by
this investigation (only reading/comparing); no pre-registered
criterion changes; the pilot keeps using exactly the certificates
that were already there, with no mechanism change.

**Tests:** none new (a read-only investigation, not code).

**Commit and push** (`v9/fase1-local`): `thesis/results/v9/DECISIONS.md`
(this Decision).

## 76. The smoke gate (run_smoke_gate) never breaks on the control instance again: the bytes diagnostic switched to the stdlib, certs/generated delivered to the control instance, any exception in the diagnostic only marks needs_decision

Luciano's decision, item 2 of the same request: `run_smoke_gate` runs
from the CONTROL instance (Decision 59 -- SSHExecutor only genuinely
works from there) and the bytes diagnostic
(`_bytes_diagnostic_for_profile` -> `ec.expected_handshake_bytes` ->
`ec._cert_der_size`) had, until now, depended on two assumptions
never true there: the `cryptography` library installed, and
`certs/generated` present on disk. Without both, the diagnostic
(only that, never the official gate) would break the entire smoke
gate with `ModuleNotFoundError`/`FileNotFoundError` before even
reaching the criteria that actually decide.

**Fixed, two independent points:**

1. `evaluate_criteria.py._cert_der_size` switched from
   `cryptography.x509.load_pem_x509_certificate(...).public_bytes
   (Encoding.DER)` to `ssl.PEM_cert_to_DER_cert(pem_text)` (stdlib
   -- a PEM is just the DER in base64, decoding never re-serializes,
   same size byte for byte; the test
   `test_bytes_diagnostic_zero_desvio_com_certs_reais_e_log_real`,
   which already exercised this entire path with real certs, keeps
   passing unchanged, proving the equivalence).
2. `deliver_source.py.CONTROL_FILES` gains
   `thesis/results/v9/certs/generated` (the same directory
   convention `CLIENT_ONLY_FILES` already used for the clients) --
   the control instance now receives the real certificates before
   any smoke gate runs.
3. `orchestrator.py.run_smoke_gate`: the loop that builds
   `bytes_diagnostic_rows` now wraps each call to
   `_bytes_diagnostic_for_profile` in a try/except -- any
   exception (residual, in case items 1/2 above are not enough for
   some unforeseen reason) produces `{"ok": False, "note": "<exception>"}`
   for that profile, which automatically marks
   `bytes_diagnostic_needs_decision = True` via the already-existing
   formula (`any(not r["ok"] ...)`) -- never propagating and
   breaking the function. `smoke_ok` continues to be computed ONLY
   from `total_execucoes`/`failures`/`capture_proof_ok` (unchanged
   formula) -- the diagnostic never enters this reckoning, with or
   without an exception.

**Why this is a safe fix:** no pre-registered criterion changes; the
bytes diagnostic has always been just that, a diagnostic (Decision
55, item 3) -- never criterion 1's official gate.

**Tests, including Luciano's explicit request ("an error in the
diagnostic pauses and does not alter smoke_ok; the correct
diagnostic with a 0 delta passes"):**
`test_bytes_diagnostic_excecao_pausa_mas_nunca_quebra_o_smoke_gate`
(new) -- forces `_bytes_diagnostic_for_profile` to raise a
`FileNotFoundError` for the `pqc` profile, checks that `run_smoke_gate`
NEVER propagates it (if it did, the test would not even reach the
asserts), that that profile's row ends up `ok: False` with the
exception in `note`, that `bytes_diagnostic_needs_decision` ends up
`True`, and that `smoke_ok` remains `True` (official criteria
intact). The pre-existing tests `test_bytes_diagnostic_zero_desvio_com_certs_reais_e
_log_real`/`test_porta_de_fumaca_sinaliza_decisao_pendente_sem_
bloquear_smoke_ok_quando_desvio_detectado` keep covering the correct
path (a 0 delta passes; a detected deviation with no exception also
only pauses, never breaks). `test_control_files_inclui_certs_
generated` + `test_deliver_to_control_tarball_inclui_certs_
generated` (new) cover item 2. 161 tests in total (158 + 3
new: 1 in test_orchestrator.py, 2 in test_deliver_source.py).

**Commit and push** (`v9/fase1-local`): `thesis/results/v9/integration/
evaluate_criteria.py`, `thesis/results/v9/campaign/scripts/
{orchestrator.py,deliver_source.py}`,
`thesis/results/v9/campaign/tests/{test_orchestrator.py,
test_deliver_source.py}`, `thesis/results/v9/DECISIONS.md` (this
Decision).

## 77. A pre-check of the operator's public IP against the SSH ingress rule (check_operator_ip.py) -- added after Decision 72's real 8-minute block, root cause never retroactively confirmable

Luciano's decision, item 5 of the same request: investigate whether
the real 8-minute block (ports 22/443, Decision 72, "infrastructure
note") could be explained by a change in the operator's public IP
NOT reflected in the control instance's SSH ingress rule
(`module.control.aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule.ssh["operator"]`,
`terraform/main.tf:131`, `ssh_ingress_cidrs =
{"operator": var.operator_ip_cidr}` -- a DIFFERENT rule from
control->server/clients, which uses the control instance's EIP and
was already correct by design).

**Investigated, honestly as far as possible:** the rule covers ONLY
port 22 (there is no rule giving the operator direct access to port
443 on any instance -- any unreachability of 443 observed from the
operator would never be evidence of a dropped rule, but of a port
that was NEVER opened to it by design). The IP is captured once per
`terraform
apply` (the `TF_VAR_operator_ip_cidr` environment variable, never
persisted to a file) and never checked again afterward -- the
scratch script that generated this value (`env.sh`) always
recalculates it on the spot, never recording the historical value
that was in force at the incident's exact moment. Honest conclusion:
it is not possible to reconstruct, retroactively, what the
operator's IP was at the moment of the real block -- the mechanism
(a single capture, never rechecked) is
plausible, but was NEVER proven to be that specific incident's root
cause.

**Why the pre-check is added anyway:** cheap insurance, independent
of proving that specific cause -- an 8-minute block cost an entire
fleet (teardown+reapply). Rechecking the IP before each phase costs
one HTTP call and, in the rare case of a change, a `terraform apply
-target` scoped to ONE resource.

**Implemented:** `check_operator_ip.py` (new,
`thesis/results/v9/campaign/scripts/`), run by the OPERATOR (never
by the control instance) before each phase that depends on SSH
working.
`ensure_operator_ip_current(tf_dir)`: reads the current IP
(`curl https://checkip.amazonaws.com`, via `cli._run`, the same
testing boundary as the whole package), reads the `cidr_ipv4`
recorded today in the state (`terraform show -json`, via
`cli.run_terraform`, locating
`module.control.aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule.ssh["operator"]`
in the `child_modules` tree); if they match, it does nothing
(`{"changed": False}`); if they differ, it reapplies ONLY that rule
(`terraform apply -auto-approve
-target='module.control.aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule.ssh
["operator"]' -var="operator_ip_cidr=<new>/32"`, never a full fleet
apply) and fails loudly (`RuntimeError`) if the reapply itself
fails -- never proceeding with a phase under a possibly stale rule.

**Tests (new, `test_check_operator_ip.py`, cli._run/cli.run_
terraform stubbed, no real call):** reading the current IP
(success/loud failure if curl fails); reading the state's cidr
(success/loud failure if `terraform show` fails or the resource does
not exist in the state); `ensure_operator_ip_current` does not
reapply when the IP matches (checks no `apply` call is triggered);
reapplies when the IP differs (checks the exact `-target`/`-var` in
the real command); fails loudly if the reapply fails. 8 new tests.

**169 tests in total** (161 from Decision 76 + 8 here -- the final
number confirmed by running the whole suite after this Decision).

**Commit and push** (`v9/fase1-local`): `thesis/results/v9/campaign/
scripts/check_operator_ip.py`,
`thesis/results/v9/campaign/tests/test_check_operator_ip.py`,
`thesis/results/v9/DECISIONS.md` (this Decision).

## 78. collect_artifacts.py rewritten for run_pilot's real FLAT structure -- the previous version assumed a per-profile directory that never genuinely existed

Luciano's decision, item 3 of the same request: the earlier
resumption's code research (before Decision 75) had already found
that `collect_artifacts.py` expected a structure
`<remote_base_dir>/<profile>/` + a per-profile `<profile>.sha256`,
but `orchestrator.py.run_pilot` ALWAYS wrote to a single FLAT
directory (`piloto_combined.log`, `piloto_calls.json`, `criterio6_
execucoes.json`, `manifest.json`, `criterio1_capturas/*.log`, all
together, never split by profile) -- this function would never have
worked against the pilot's real output, only against the old tests'
own wrong premise.

**Fixed:** `collect_block()` (per profile) removed; `collect_
pilot_data(control_ip, key_path, remote_dir, local_dir)` (new)
regenerates the sha256 manifest on the control instance over the
ENTIRE DIRECTORY (`find . -type f | xargs sha256sum`, the same call
as always, just without the `/<profile>` suffix), pulls everything
with a single `scp -r` step, and re-checks the manifest locally --
EXACTLY the same guarantee as always (no change to the verification
logic itself, only to what it points at). CLI: `--remote-dir` (was
`--remote-base-dir`
+ `--profiles`) -- the same `--out` already passed to `orchestrator.py

## 81. Real finding, live, running the real Phase B (Step 10, the first time run_smoke_gate runs against a real fleet) -- capture_ready_check() always failed on a new fleet, for lacking an image it itself never delivered

Branch `v9/fase1-local`. A real apply (`self_terminate_hours=4`, 28
resources), Steps 0-9 of `PILOT_RUNBOOK.md` all green (a new fleet,
the operator's IP checked by Decision 77 live for the first time --
`{"ok": true, "changed": false}`; 4 images delivered and sha256
checked; `certs/generated` confirmed reaching the control instance
for the first time, Decision 76). Step 10 (the smoke gate) ran and
FAILED **before any run**:

```
"capture_preflight": {"go": false, "checks": [{"host": "<servidor>",
  "missing": ["imagem docker mockopin-v9-measure ausente (entregue
  por docker save/load, Decisao 55 item 2 -- nunca docker build na
  instancia)"]}]}
```

**Root cause:** `preflight.run_capture_preflight` (called by
`SSHExecutor.capture_ready_check()`, Decision 53/4c) only READS
whether `mockopin-v9-measure` already exists on the server (`docker
image inspect`) -- it never delivers it. `dedicated_capture()`
(Decision 55, item 2) delivers this image, but only LAZILY, the
first time IT runs -- and `dedicated_capture` only runs AFTER the
smoke gate passes (inside `run_smoke_gate` itself, in the 4
`smoke_capture_proof`). On a new fleet, nothing had ever delivered
`measure` before this point --
`capture_ready_check()` always failed, for lacking an image it
itself never tries to deliver. Never caught before because
`run_smoke_gate`/`capture_ready_check` had NEVER run against a real
fleet in this history -- `INFRA_REHEARSAL.md` only exercises
`--exercise-start-stop`/`rehearsal_handshake.sh`, neither of which
touches capture.

**Why this is a safe fix, never a STOP (this authorization's rule
7(a) does not apply -- this is a code bug, never a pre-registered
criterion failing with already-correct code):**
`_deliver_image` is idempotent (sha256 checked at both hops,
Decision 68) and is exactly the same mechanism `dedicated_capture`
already uses for this SAME image -- it only moves the delivery up to
the preflight moment instead of waiting for first real use. No
pre-registered criterion changes, no measurement is affected.

**Fixed:** `SSHExecutor.capture_ready_check()` now calls
`self._deliver_image("measure", self._server_ip())` BEFORE running
`preflight.run_capture_preflight(...)` -- the preflight becomes
self-sufficient (guaranteeing what it checks), no longer merely
passive.

**Tests (new):**
`test_capture_ready_check_entrega_measure_antes_de_rodar_o_probe`
(checks the exact ORDER: delivery before the probe, with the right
host) +
`test_mutante_capture_ready_check_nunca_entrega_measure_e_pego`
(a mutant that reverts to the old behavior, confirming the real test
depended on the delivery). 175 tests in total (173 + 2).

**Commit and push** (`v9/fase1-local`): `thesis/results/v9/campaign/
scripts/orchestrator.py`,
`thesis/results/v9/campaign/tests/test_orchestrator.py`,
`thesis/results/v9/DECISIONS.md` (this Decision).

Redelivering `orchestrator.py` to the control instance (same fleet,
no reapplying) and repeating Step 10.

## 82. Real STOP in Phase B, Step 10 (resumption) -- the gateway's business layer (HTTP_MODE=business) never had, anywhere in this v9 package, a delivery path for the real AS/API backend to any instance -- every real run that requires JWKS fails with unresolved DNS

**Result of the reapplied Step 10 (after Decision 81's fix):** the
capture preflight passed; the 12 runs began; the readiness probe
(`readiness_probe`, which triggers the COMPLETE real flow via
`campaign_client_runner.py`/`opin_flow.py` -- JWKS, AS, RS, never
just the mTLS handshake) failed for `hibrido-v8`/`L0` on both internal
attempts of `latency_automation.run_once_timed_with_retry`:

```
RuntimeError: readiness_probe hibrido-v8/L0: execucao de settling falhou:
settling_hibrido-v8_L0 failed on both attempts -- stopping (not retrying
further; this is no longer the known rare race, treat as a new failure).
Last error: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
```

**Root cause, confirmed by reading the gateway's real log on the
server (never assumed):**

```
2026/11/08 19:31:00 http: proxy error: dial tcp: lookup auth on 172.31.0.2:53: no such host
2026/11/08 19:31:00 INFO access log ... host=auth.local request=/jwks method=GET status=502 ...
```

The mTLS handshake itself always passes ("connection OK", 3x in the
first few seconds) -- what fails is the BUSINESS layer
(`HTTP_MODE=business`, `business.go`, reinstated by Decision 17 "to
run the real 44-HTTP-call flow end to end"): every call to
`auth.local/*` is a real reverse proxy to
`AUTH_URI` (default `http://auth:3000`, `business.go` line 40) --
"auth" is a hostname that ONLY exists as a Docker network alias in
LOCAL validation (`insurance-server-lambdas_default`, the same
network Decision 70 had already identified as exclusive to local
validation). On a real EC2 instance, "auth" never resolves (the
VPC's DNS resolver returns NXDOMAIN) -- NO call requiring JWKS (or
`api.local`/`matls-api.local`, proxying to `API_GATEWAY_URI`)
would ever work on a real run, not just this one.

**Why this was never caught before:** `INFRA_REHEARSAL.md`
(`--exercise-start-stop`) never calls `readiness_probe`/
`run_execution` -- only `start_block`/`stop_block`. `rehearsal_
handshake.sh` (Step 10 of that procedure) tests ONLY the mTLS
handshake (negtest), never the business HTTP flow. This Phase B Step
10 (the smoke gate, which calls `run_pilot`->`readiness_probe`->
`campaign_client_runner.py`->`opin_flow.py`, the REAL business flow)
is, confirmed by searching this entire project's history, THE FIRST
TIME any real business HTTP call runs against a genuine EC2
instance.

**Confirmed, by reading `thesis/results/v8/campaign/scripts/
deliver_images.sh`:** v8 had ALREADY solved this EXACT problem for
its own campaign -- delivering 4 SERVER images
(`insurance-server-lambdas-mtls`,
`insurance-server-lambdas-auth`, `raidiam-insurance-lambdas` [the
API],
`insurance-server-lambdas-mongo_seed`) to each real server, via the
SAME 2-hop relay. v9 never ported this mechanism -- `PINS.json`/
`deliver_images.py` only deliver gateway/proxy/pqc-signer/measure,
never auth/mockapi/mongo_seed. These images also do NOT exist
locally today (`docker images` does not list any `insurance-server-
lambdas-*`) -- they would need to be (re)built (`docker-compose build`
inside `mock-service-os/`) before any delivery.

**Why this is a STOP, never a fix-and-retry (this authorization's
rule 6/7(e)):** this is not a 1-2-line bug like Decisions 70-74/81 --
it requires: (1) (re)building 3-4 entire Docker images never built
this round; (2) a NEW delivery mechanism
(`deliver_images.py`/`PINS.json` never knew about them);
(3) orchestrating this backend's containers on the server alongside
the gateway (`_launch_gateway`/`start_block` today bring up nothing
beyond gateway/proxy/pqc-signer); (4) deciding the correct
`AUTH_URI`/`API_GATEWAY_
URI` for this new arrangement. Any of these changes directly alters
what runs during a real measurement --
exactly the "doubt about whether the fix alters what is measured"
rule 7(e) asks to be handled with a stop, never with an attempt
within the same session.

**Action taken, following rule 6 (fleet never idle):** no new attempt
within this fleet -- immediate teardown (`emergency_
stop.py` dry mode confirmed the expected 5 instances/5 EIPs/3
SGs/4 key pairs; `cleanup.py --tf-dir ../../terraform --profile mockopin-pqc
--release-eips --force` reported `"all_clean": true`, zero drift);
an independent final verification (12 `describe-*` calls, 3 regions)
confirmed empty.

**Decisions pending from Luciano (none taken on my own):**
1. Port v8's auth/mockapi/mongo_seed backend to v9 (rebuild
   the images, a new delivery mechanism, a new orchestration step
   on the server) -- the most complete path, but the most time-costly.
2. Decide whether v9's pilot can/should measure only the mTLS layer
   (without the complete business flow) -- this would require
   changing `opin_flow.py`/
   `campaign_client_runner.py` to skip JWKS/AS/RS in this mode, which
   changes what is measured (criteria 4/6 depend on the complete
   flow, 40/44 HTTP calls) -- probably unfeasible without
   re-registering criteria.
3. Some third option Luciano prefers (e.g., a minimal AS/API stub,
   simpler than porting all of v8, if he judges this does not
   relevantly alter what is measured).

**Tests:** none new (an infrastructure/architecture finding, never a
code bug fixable with this package's existing tests -- no Python
function needs to change until Luciano decides the path).

**Cost of this attempt:** a fleet alive for approximately 25-30
minutes (real apply ~19:1x UTC, teardown confirmed ~19:3x UTC) --
well within the US$5 cap, adding to Phase A's spend (~US$0.55).

**Commit and push** (`v9/fase1-local`): `thesis/results/v9/DECISIONS.md`
(this Decision), evidence in `thesis/results/v9/piloto/
ensaio_fase_b_real/`.

## 84. DEPENDENCY_MAP.md (item 2) + local validation in a CLEAN environment (item 3) -- a real finding in the validation itself, fixed before touching AWS again

**Item 2:** `thesis/results/v9/campaign/DEPENDENCY_MAP.md` (new) --
a complete hostname/port/volume/env/file/image table for the
gateway, proxy, pqc-signer, and the business backend (Decision 83),
stating where each one resolves and who provides it on a real AWS.
Conclusion: no listed dependency is "local only" -- the last one that
was (AUTH_URI/API_GATEWAY_URI) was fixed by Decision 83 itself.

**Item 3: local validation in a CLEAN environment, a real finding.**
Tested WITHOUT depending on this machine's development environment:
an ISOLATED directory (`/tmp/v9_clean_validation/`) with ONLY what
`deliver_source.py` actually delivers (`SERVER_ONLY_FILES` +
`mock-service-os/certs`), no build source present, a compose project
with its OWN name (`-p v9cleantest`, never the default name that
would collide with this machine's development containers).

**Real finding, live, within the validation itself:** the 1st
attempt, with `-p v9cleantest` but WITHOUT retagging the pre-built
images to the name this project expected (`v9cleantest-auth`/`v9cleantest-
mongo_seed`), made `docker compose up` try to BUILD (never reusing
the already-loaded pinned image) -- `additional privileges
requested: pass "--allow=fs.read=..\mock-service-os"`, because the
build context (`mock_as/`) never exists in the isolated directory.
**This proves, live, why the real mechanism (with no `-p`, Decision
83) works:** on the real server, `docker load` preserves the EXACT
name (`insurance-server-lambdas-auth:latest`) and `docker compose`

## 86. Real finding, live, running Phase B again (Step 8) -- scp's fixed timeout (140s) never designed for the backend images, overflowed delivering localstack.tar (1.8GB)

Branch `v9/fase1-local`. A new fleet applied (31 resources, `self_
terminate_hours=4`), Steps 0-7 all green (the operator's IP
checked, the key delivered, Docker ready across the 5 instances,
`deliver_
source.py` confirmed Decisions 83/85's new files arriving correctly,
`dedicated_criteria.py`/`orchestrator.py` confirmed genuinely
importing on the control instance -- see the note below). Step 8
(`deliver_images.py`, now with 10 images -- the original 4 + the 6
from the backend) failed while delivering `localstack.tar` (1.8GB):

```
subprocess.TimeoutExpired: Command [... 'scp' ... 'localstack.tar' ...]
timed out after 140 seconds
```

**Root cause:** `cli.run_scp`'s timeout (`connect_timeout=20` default
-> a total process timeout of 140s) was measured and calibrated only
against the 4 original images (~140MB total, Decision 59/68) -- never
designed for the 6 backend images (Decision 83), some ~1.8GB. The
real bandwidth was GOOD (`psql.tar`, 642MB, completed within the same
140s limit BEFORE `localstack.tar` -- >4.5MB/s measured live) -- the
problem was never the network, it was the fixed timeout never
scaling with the file's real size.

**Fixed:** `deliver_images.py` gains `_scp_timeout_for_bytes`
(new) -- computes the `connect_timeout` (which `cli.run_scp` already
uses as the basis for the total process timeout) PROPORTIONAL to the
`.tar`'s real size, with a conservative floor of 24Mbps (well below
the real observed bandwidth, never the old fixed value). Passed
explicitly in the main tar's `cli.run_scp` call (never for the
`.sha256`, which is tiny).

**Why this is a safe fix, never a STOP:** it touches no
identity/content verification (sha256/layers/config remain exactly
as Decision 68 defined) -- it only gives the real scp enough time to
finish before the process thinks it is stuck. No pre-registered
criterion changes.

**Tests (new):** `test_scp_timeout_for_bytes_escala_com_tamanho_
real` (+ a mutant reverting to the fixed value, caught) +
`test_deliver_images_
usa_timeout_proporcional_no_scp_do_tar` (checks the exact
`ConnectTimeout=N` in the real scp argv). 202 tests in total (199 + 3).

**State of the control instance at the moment of the finding (never
needed manual cleanup -- scp overwrites the destination):**
`gateway`/`proxy`/`pqc-
signer`/`measure`/`psql` already delivered and verified (sha256 OK);
`localstack.tar` partial (470MB of ~1.8GB) -- will be overwritten by
redelivery. Control instance disk with 28GB free, a huge margin.

scripts/deliver_images.py`,
`thesis/results/v9/campaign/tests/test_deliver_images.py`,
`thesis/results/v9/DECISIONS.md` (this Decision).

Redelivering the remaining images (same fleet, no reapplying).

## 87. Real finding, live, running Phase B again (Step 10) -- stock images (psql/localstack/mongodb) should never go through the by-name save/load mechanism

Branch `v9/fase1-local`. After Decision 86's finding (fixed, the
remaining images delivered, sha256_ok:true for all 5), Step 10 (the
smoke gate) failed again, now inside `start_block`:

```
RuntimeError: _deliver_image(psql, <servidor>): identidade nao
confere (layers_ok=False, config_ok=False, binary_ok=True) --
abortando ANTES de qualquer execucao
```

**Investigated live, never assumed:** reproduced locally on a CLEAN
`docker:25-dind` (a new container, never used before): `docker
save postgres@sha256:ca0bd...` (a reference ONLY by digest, never
tagged by name) + `docker load` on the dind -> `docker images
--digests` shows `<none> <none> <none>` -- NO nameable reference
survives save/load, only a loose Image ID ("Loaded image
ID: sha256:..."). `docker image inspect postgres@sha256:...` on the
dind returns `Error response from daemon: No such image` -- exactly
the `actual_layers=None`/`config=None` (the command failed, never a
genuine content mismatch) that produces `layers_ok=False,
config_ok=False` without breaking the process.

**Root cause:** `psql`/`localstack`/`mongodb` (Decision 83) are
STOCK images, referenced in PINS.json ONLY by digest
(`postgres@sha256:...` etc, to match exactly what
`docker-compose.yml` already fixes) -- but the by-NAME delivery/
verification mechanism (`_deliver_image`, Decision 68) requires a
nameable reference surviving `docker load`, which NEVER happens for a
digest-only image, confirmed live above.

**Fix -- never retag and force it, reconsidered the design (simpler,
more correct):** `psql`/`localstack`/`mongodb` EXIT
the 2-hop mechanism entirely -- removed from `PINS.json`
(they never needed a pin of their OWN: the exact digest is already
fixed INSIDE `docker-compose.yml`, the correct source of truth) and
from `deliver_images.py.BACKEND_IMAGE_KEYS` (now only `auth`/`mongo_seed`/
`mockapi` -- EXACTLY the 3 CUSTOM images Luciano explicitly requested,
"extra server images (auth, mockapi,
mongo_seed)"). `docker compose up` itself already resolves the 3
STOCK ones correctly -- a direct pull from the public registry (the
egress SG open, confirmed in `main.tf`), the same exact digest
compose.yml already fixes, deterministic content either way (pull
or load). No pinned CUSTOM image was touched -- `auth`/`mongo_
seed`/`mockapi` were already delivered and verified (sha256_ok: true)
on the same fleet, never needing redelivery.

**Side finding, fixed in the same step:** this very fix's own edit
(a Python script writing PINS.json in text mode on Windows)
reintroduced CRLF into the file -- immediately caught by
`test_no_crlf_sweep.py` (Decision 69) before any commit, fixed by
writing in binary.

**Why this is a safe fix, never a STOP:** it simplifies the design
(3 images delivered via 2 hops, no longer 6), touches no CUSTOM
image's content verification, and the pin for the 3 STOCK ones still
exists -- just in the right place (`docker-compose.
yml`, where it always was, never duplicated in PINS.json). No
pre-registered criterion changes.

**Tests:** the entire suite runs unchanged (`test_orchestrator.py`
computes `BACKEND_IMAGE_KEYS` dynamically, never hardcoded -- the
tests automatically adapt to the smaller list). 202 tests in
total (unchanged).

{orchestrator.py,deliver_images.py}`,

## 89. Real finding, live, running Phase B again (Step 10, the backend comes up end to end for the first time) -- setup_ssm.sh lost its executable bit on the remote path, only on Windows

Branch `v9/fase1-local`. With Decision 88 fixed, Step 10 advanced
MUCH further -- the 4 backend images came up, `localstack` was
successfully skipped by compose (confirming Decision 87 live), but
`auth` never came up: `Container insurance-server-lambdas-localstack-1
Error dependency localstack failed to start: dependency failed to
start: container insurance-server-lambdas-localstack-1 is
unhealthy`.

**Investigated live, never assumed:** `docker logs insurance-
server-lambdas-localstack-1` on the real server shows the exact
cause:

```
PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied:
'/etc/localstack/init/ready.d/init-aws.sh'
```

**Root cause:** this path is `mock-service-os/setup_ssm.sh`
MOUNTED (`docker-compose.yml`, the `localstack` service) --
`localstack` executes this script DIRECTLY via `subprocess.call`
(never `sh script.
sh`), requiring the file's own executable bit. `git ls-files -s`
confirms git tracks this file as `100755` (executable) -- but
`deliver_source.py.build_tarball` uses `tar.add(src,
arcname=rel)` with NO filter, which uses the LOCAL file's `os.stat()`
(Windows, where the operator runs) for the tar's Unix mode -- and
Windows NEVER preserves the 755 bit git tracks at checkout. The
tarball delivered to the server always had this script WITHOUT the
+x, even though it came from a repository where it was always marked
executable.

**Why this was never caught before:** no other `.sh` delivered via
this path needs its own +x bit -- `rehearsal_handshake.sh` is always
invoked as `bash rehearsal_handshake.sh` (the bit never matters,
`bash` reads the content regardless of execute permission).
`setup_ssm.sh` is the FIRST `.sh` file delivered via this path that
needs to be executable on its own (`localstack` calls it directly)
-- and it only started being delivered this same round (Decision
83/85, `SERVER_ONLY_FILES`).

**Fixed:** `deliver_source.py.build_tarball` gains `_fix_
permissions_filter` (new, passed as `filter=` to `tar.add()`)
-- forces 0o755 for any `.sh` and directories, 0o644 for the rest,
NEVER trusting what the local OS (Windows) reported.

**Why this is a safe fix, never a STOP:** it touches no file
content, only the Unix permission in the tar -- making the delivery
CORRECT (what git always intended), never a behavior change beyond
fixing a transport bug.

**Tests (new, with a mutant):** `test_build_tarball_forca_bit_
executavel_em_arquivos_sh` + `test_build_tarball_arquivo_nao_sh_
fica_so_leitura` + `test_mutante_tarball_sem_filtro_de_permissao_e_
pego` (deliberately zeroes the local +x, confirming that WITHOUT the
filter the tar loses the bit, and that the real `build_tarball`
always forces it). 205 tests in total (202 + 3).

**Commit and push** (`v9/fase1-local`): `thesis/results/v9/campaign/
scripts/deliver_source.py`,
`thesis/results/v9/campaign/tests/test_deliver_source.py`,
`thesis/results/v9/DECISIONS.md` (this Decision).

Redelivering `deliver_source.py` (Step 6, server+clients -- the
fixed `setup_ssm.sh` only arrives this way) and repeating Step 10.

## 90. Real STOP in Phase B, Step 10 -- the business backend comes up end to end for the FIRST time (12/12 runs, 0 failures), but the capture proof fails across the 4 profiles -- a real finding over a real network, never before exercised, rule 7(e) applied

**Result, after Decisions 81/87/88/89 (real findings, all fixed
live, each validated): Step 10 advanced further than on ANY previous
attempt this round.** `smoke_capture_proof` confirms, by reading the
real `manifest.json` directly from the control instance (the SSH
connection got stuck without closing after the command finished --
the SAME "empty heredoc" symptom already recorded earlier in this
session, never a problem with the pilot ITSELF -- the real result
was read directly from the file on the control instance, never
assumed):

- `capture_preflight.go: true`
- **12/12 smoke-gate runs, ZERO failures** (`smoke_
  failures: []`) -- the FIRST time in this package's history that
  the real business backend (auth/mockapi/mongo_seed + psql/
  localstack/mongodb) comes up, genuinely serves JWKS/token, and
  sustains 12 real runs via `campaign_client_runner.py`/`opin_flow.py`
  with no failure at all -- **the complete delivery requested in
  Luciano's item 1 is proven, live, on a real AWS.**
- `bytes_diagnostic_needs_decision: false` (the diagnostic, Decision
  76, never the official gate -- passed clean).
- `capture_proof_ok: false` -- the 4 MECHANISM-PROOF tests
  (Decision 53, item 4b -- 1 dedicated capture per profile, never
  one of criterion 1's 12 official ones) failed, all 4 with
  `ok: false`.

**Investigated live, never assumed:** the 4 capture logs
(`smoke_capture_proof/*.log`, archived here) show REAL decryption
working -- "size PER MESSAGE" with concrete, plausible values, never
empty nor corrupted. The cause of `ok: false` is that EACH log
contains the SAME message group REPEATED 6 times (always with the
SAME bytes on every repetition -- never values diverging from each
other), with the "server CertificateVerify+Finished" group (tshark
types 15,20) appearing on a line SEPARATE from the
"ServerHello+EncryptedExtensions+CertificateRequest+
Certificate" group (types 2,8,13,11) --
`_message_sizes_for_profile` (evaluate_criteria.py) only assigns
15/20 as "from the server" when they appear ON THE SAME line as
2+11; when tshark reports them in SEPARATE frames (due to different
TCP fragmentation/coalescing on a real network vs. local), these two
fields are never filled, and the criterion fails for a missing
field, never for a wrong byte.

**Why this is a STOP, never a fix-and-retry:** this classification
(`_message_sizes_for_profile`) is the SAME function that decides the
OFFICIAL criterion 1 (the pre-registration's most cited criterion)
-- never just the smoke gate's mechanism proof. This is the FIRST
TIME, in this entire project's history, that this classification
runs against a REAL network capture (every previous validation was
local/loopback, where TCP coalescing is always different). Fixing
this classification logic, under time pressure, on a live fleet,
WITHOUT fully understanding whether frame grouping varies per run
(network timing/jitter) or is deterministic for the real environment
-- is exactly the "doubt about whether the fix alters what is
measured" this authorization's rule 7(e) asks to be handled with a
stop, never with an attempt within the same session. Unlike
Decisions 81/87/88/89 (infrastructure/transport/transcription bugs,
always with a single, obviously-safe-to-fix root cause), this
finding touches the MEASUREMENT MECHANISM itself.

**Decision taken:** STOP here. The business backend (this round's
central request) is proven working end to end -- this is a real,
significant result, not a defeat. The tshark message classification
under a real network needs Luciano's decision before any change: it
touches the official criterion 1.

**Action taken, following rule 6 (fleet never idle):** `emergency_
stop.py` dry mode confirmed the expected 5 instances/5 EIPs/3
SGs/4 key pairs; `cleanup.py --tf-dir ../../terraform --profile mockopin-pqc
--release-eips --force` reported `"all_clean": true`, zero drift;
an independent final verification (12 `describe-*` calls, 3 regions)
confirmed empty.

**Decisions pending from Luciano:**
1. Does `_message_sizes_for_profile`'s per-line classification need
   to group by TIME WINDOW (not just by exact line), or does tshark
   need an option forcing TLS record reassembly before analysis
   (`-o tls.desegment_ssl_records: TRUE`, possibly already on by
   default -- needs confirming), or is this an expected/tolerable
   behavior that just needs a fallback in the classification (sum
   15/20 from ANY line in the block, not just the one with 2+11)?
2. The 6 repeated groups per capture -- are they 6 genuinely real
   connections (why 6, if each capture should have only 1 settling
   run?) or is it the SAME handshake being reported in multiple
   windows by tshark? It needs deeper investigation (perhaps with
   the raw pcap, not just the already-extracted text) before any
   fix.
3. Given the business backend is already proven (item 1 complete),
   Luciano decides whether he wants: (a) to investigate/fix the
   classification before any new real-pilot attempt, or (b) to
   accept running the full pilot even with the smoke gate's
   mechanism proof failing (never recommended -- the same
   classification decides the official criterion 1), or (c) another
   approach.

**Tests:** none new (a measurement finding under a real network,
never testable locally the same way -- it would need an equivalent
real capture, which only exists in this archived evidence).

**Cost of this attempt:** a fleet alive for approximately 1h25
(apply ~20:32 UTC, teardown ~21:53 UTC) -- the LARGEST window of a
single attempt this round, but still well within the US$5 cap

## 91. Amendment -- a PARSING bug in criterion 1's measurement mechanism (NEVER a change to the criterion, the thresholds, or the baselines), response to Decision 90's 3 pending decisions

**Item 1 of Luciano's request -- confirmed by data, without AWS, before any fix:**

1. **Cause of the fragmentation:** `_message_sizes_for_profile`
   classified each message by the CO-OCCURRENCE of types on the same
   tshark line ("server" = a line with ServerHello(2) AND
   Certificate(11) together), never by WHO ACTUALLY SENT the
   message. Under a real network, the server's flight sometimes
   arrives in TWO separate socket writes (CertificateVerify+Finished
   on a line with no 2/11) -- the same TLS mechanism as always, just
   with a different packet grouping than loopback (real RTT/
   congestion window, never present in loopback). The old heuristic
   simply never tested this possibility.
2. **The "6 repeated groups" per capture hypothesis:** CONFIRMED, and
   it is not a new assumption -- it is an invariant OF THIS PROJECT,
   documented in `thesis/scripts/opin_flow.py`
   (`get_local_leg_cert_paths`, a v7 decision from 2026-09-14): a
   complete business-flow run (`opin_flow.py`) opens exactly 6 real
   client-facing mTLS connections per run
   ("restores exactly 6 'upstream handshake complete' lines per
   full flow", confirmed against v7 data from 2026-09-12). The 6
   repeated groups, byte for byte identical, in Decision 90's real
   logs (`smoke_capture_proof_*.log`, 1 `dedicated_capture` =
   1 complete `campaign_client_runner.py` run) ARE these 6
   connections -- never the same handshake reported in different
   windows by tshark.
   - **Honest limitation:** this attempt's RAW .pcap was never
     pulled from the ephemeral host to the operator before Decision
     90's teardown -- only the "size PER MESSAGE" section (text
     ALREADY derived by `dedicated_capture` itself) survived,
     archived now in `piloto/tentativas/ensaio_fase_b_real_v2/`
     (`conta_como_
     dado: false`, Luciano's request). It was not possible to count
     `tcp.
     stream` in this specific attempt's raw pcap because it never
     existed locally -- item 2's confirmation above comes from the
     project's CODE (a primary source, never an assumption) and,
     below, from a NEW, local capture with a real raw pcap. Fixed
     from here on: the next real attempt also archives the raw pcap
     (see item 4).

**Item 2 of Luciano's request -- fixing `_message_sizes_for_profile`, constraints (a)-(f):**

- **(a) Thresholds/baselines untouched:** `CERTIFICATE_BASELINE`,
  `CLIENTHELLO_BASELINE`, `HANDSHAKE_MESSAGE_BASELINE` and the
  tolerances (0B/±4B/0B) -- not a single line changed.
- **(b) TLS messages reassembled per connection:** a new function
  `_message_sizes_stream_aware` (evaluate_criteria.py) classifies

  per-type dict, fragmentation stops mattering.
  `dedicated_capture` (orchestrator.py)
