## 93. Amendment -- `CERTIFICATE_BASELINE` recalibrated by DERIVATION from the real DER (Luciano's option 2), full investigation before any correction: Decision 75 had already reverted the Decision 28/29 premise and `CERTIFICATE_BASELINE` was never rechecked against that reversal

**Investigation, without AWS, item 1 of the request (five parts, none assumed):**

**(a) Real DER of each embedded certificate vs `BASELINE_CERT_DER_SIZES`.**
Measured directly (`ssl.PEM_cert_to_DER_cert`) against `certs/generated/`
(confirmed by sha256 == the same one embedded in `mockopin-v9-gateway:
pinned`, Decision 92): classico out=900/in=787; pqc out=5619/in=5506;
hibrido-v8 out=6242/in=6131; hibrido-and out=914+5647/in=801+5534 --
**all four match `BASELINE_CERT_DER_SIZES` EXACTLY, with no
divergence.** That table was never the problem.

**(b) History via `git log -S` + `DECISIONS.md`.** `BASELINE_CERT_
DER_SIZES` was introduced in `8a14254b` (Decision 55) with the SAME
900/5619/6242/914+5647 as today -- never changed since. `CERTIFICATE_
BASELINE` changed exactly once, in `107f592c` (Decisions 28/29): the
diff literally shows the REMOVED comment reading "Baseline
recalculated: 913-12=901, 5632-12=5620, 6255-12=6243, 6582-12=6570" --
in other words, **913/5632/6255/6582 (the SAME values that the real
AWS measurement, Decision 92, found) were already Decision 28's
starting point**, which SUBTRACTED an arithmetic estimate of -12B
(later corrected to -14B/-28B measured in Decision 29) assuming the
pilot would swap the loopback SAN for one with two real IPs
(private+EIP). Decision 75 (resumed in this same extended session)
investigated this EXACT premise and explicitly knocked it down: "the
real-SAN technique... is ruled out for the pilot -- no image rebuild";
confirmed by sha256 that the embedded certificate is the loopback one
(127.0.0.1,::1); and concluded "why this is an Amendment, never a
STOP: no pre-registered criterion changes" -- but never rechecked
`CERTIFICATE_BASELINE` against that reversal. The number stayed
anchored to a SAN swap that Decision 75 itself proved never happens.

**(c) Sum of per-message baselines vs `BASELINE_HANDSHAKE_BYTES`,
residual, single inconsistent entry.** For each profile/direction:
`out_sum = ServerHello+EncryptedExtensions+CertificateRequest+
Certificate+CertificateVerify_server+Finished_server`; `in_sum =
ClientHello+Certificate_client+CertificateVerify_client+Finished_
client`. **Before the correction** (899/5618/6241/6554): `out`
residual = 135/135/135/149 (NOT constant -- hibrido-and diverges from
the other 3 by exactly the extra Certificate leaf) and `in` residual =
77/77/77/77 (already constant, the client side never had a problem).
**After the correction** (913/5632/6255/6582): `out` residual =
121/121/121/121 (constant across all 4) and `in` residual remains
77/77/77/77. **The ONLY inconsistent entry, on both sides, was the
SERVER's Certificate -- confirmed by exact arithmetic, no other row
of the table (ServerHello/EncryptedExtensions/CertificateRequest/
CertificateVerify/Finished, in both directions, nor Certificate_
client) needs correction.** (The leftover 121B/77B residual is TLS 1.3
record framing/AEAD tag/ChangeCipherSpec -- never part of the "+4B per
message" convention these tables use, never an inconsistency.)

**(d) Certificate value derived by formula, 4 profiles, 2 directions
(includes the CLIENT's Certificate in mTLS).** RFC 8446, section
4.4.2: `message = 4(handshake header) + 1(certificate_request_context,
always empty) + 3(certificate_list length) + per leaf [3(cert length)
+ DER + 2(extensions length) + real extension]`. For 1 leaf: `message
= DER+13` -- tested against the 3 single-leaf profiles, matches
EXACTLY in both directions (classico: server 900+13=913, client
787+13=800 -- this LAST one was already the value used in
`HANDSHAKE_MESSAGE_BASELINE`, never changed; pqc: 5619+13=5632 /
5506+13=5519 [already correct]; hibrido-v8: 6242+13=6255 /
6131+13=6144 [already correct]). Hibrido-AND (2 leaves, server AND
client): the formula generalizes to `8 + sum_per_leaf(DER_i
+5+extension_i)` -- confirmed by content (the tshark `Certificates
Length` field, never the ML-DSA leaf's ASN.1 sub-parsing, which tshark
itself gets wrong with "BER Error"/"Vector length... malformed") that
the ML-DSA leaf carries 3B of REAL extension per `CertificateEntry`
that the RSA leaf does not have -- confirmed in 2 INDEPENDENT real
captures (local, Decision 84; real AWS, Decision 92): server
914+5647+21=6582 (matches Decision 92's real measurement); client
801+5534+21=6356 (matches the `Certificate_client` that `HANDSHAKE_
MESSAGE_BASELINE` already used, never changed). **The 4 profiles, the
2 directions: the formula EXACTLY reproduces both the values already
correct (ClientHello, Certificate_client, all other messages) and the
one wrong value (server Certificate) -- no second inconsistency
found.**

**(e) Why old local validations passed with 899.** They never passed
against a real certificate -- Decision 79 ("full data path proved
locally") used `LocalExecutor`/`_dedicated_capture_block`, which
FABRICATES the message sizes DIRECTLY from the baseline dictionaries
themselves (`HANDSHAKE_MESSAGE_BASELINE`/`CERTIFICATE_BASELINE`) --
circular by construction, never an independent measurement against a
real certificate file. Decision 90 was the FIRST time `certificate_ok`
was evaluated against a genuine network capture (and it stopped before
reaching this specific comparison, due to a different parsing bug);
Decision 92 was the FIRST time the comparison actually ran -- and that
is exactly when the inconsistency appeared.

**Luciano's hypothesis: CONFIRMED on all 5 points.** The residual
shows EXACTLY one inconsistent entry (never more than one, never
another message); the value derived by the formula from the real DER
matches EXACTLY the one measured on AWS (Decision 92) across the 4
profiles.

**Correction (item 2 of the request, option 2 -- by DERIVATION, never
copying):** `CERTIFICATE_BASELINE` stops being a literal constant and
becomes CALCULATED, at import time, by `_tls13_certificate_message_
size(leaf_der_sizes, extra_extension_bytes)` (new, `evaluate_
criteria.py`) from `BASELINE_CERT_DER_SIZES` (which was already
correct, never touched) -- the formula and the verification `assert`
(the sum of Hibrido-AND's individual DERs == the total that
`BASELINE_CERT_DER_SIZES` already stored) are RECORDED in the code,
never just in the commit. `CERTIFICATE_TOLERANCE_B` stays ±4B (Decision
42, still valid: the only legitimate source of variability is the
serial number's ASN.1 padding). No other constant touched.
`BASELINE_CERT_DER_SIZES` was only MOVED to before `CERTIFICATE_
BASELINE` in the file (it needs to exist first, being computed at
import time) -- identical content.

## 94. Fourth real Phase B attempt -- four real findings fixed live in sequence at Step 11.5 (dedicated producers for criteria 2/3/7), none of them touching what is measured

**Real fleet applied** (31 resources), Steps 0-10 green -- `smoke_ok:
true`, `capture_proof_ok: true` in all 4 profiles (Decision 93
confirmed again against the real network). Step 11 (60 runs + 12
captures): green, `total_execucoes: 60`, zero failures. **Step 11.5
(`dedicated_criteria.py`, producers for criteria 2/3/7, Decision 85)
-- the FIRST time this script runs against the full real pilot --
found 4 real findings in sequence, each investigated by content
(never assumed) before fixing:**

1. **The SSH session that launches `criterio2_probe.py` never
   returned (50s timeout), even with the process already genuinely
   running on the server (confirmed by `ps aux`/log, repeatedly).**
   Five fix attempts by command SYNTAX (explicit `< /dev/null`,
   `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` in `cli._run`, `setsid`, the `sh -c
   '...& echo $!'` pattern that `_launch_gateway` already uses for
   tcpdump, `ssh -f`) -- NONE changed anything. Real cause, confirmed
   manually: TRANSIENT server throttling right after Step 11 (60
   runs, many SSH connections in rapid succession) -- the SAME simple
   command as always returned in ~1.3s after only about 15s of
   waiting. Fixed with a simple retry (3 attempts, 15s interval) in
   `run_criterio2`, never changing the launch mechanism. `cli._run`
   gained `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` as defensive hygiene (never the
   cause nor the fix for this specific finding, honestly documented
   in the code).
2. **`ethtool` missing on the real AMI (Amazon Linux 2023) -- brought
   down the ENTIRE script** with `FileNotFoundError`, even though
   this field (Decision 37) never decides criterion 2's result.
   `ethtool_offloads` gains a `try/except` -- explicit
   `"indisponivel"`, never a silent None, never brings the script
   down again.
3. **`tcpdump` without `sudo` in `criterio2_probe.py` -- failed with
   "CAP_NET_RAW may be required", SILENTLY** (the `Popen` never
   checked the return code) -- confirmed by running `tcpdump` manually
   as `ec2-user` on the real server. No pcap was written,
   `mss_bytes`/`bytes_sent_before_first_client_ack` ended up `None`
   with no visible error. Fixed with `sudo` (the same fix that
   `dedicated_capture`/`_launch_gateway` already use for criterion 1's
   real tcpdump).
4. **Real logic bug in `extract_mss_and_bytes_before_ack`**,
   confirmed by content against the real pcap: the function used the
   client's FIRST ACK (`ack_out[0]`) to compute how many bytes the
   server sent before it -- but that FIRST ACK is the one that CLOSES
   the 3-way handshake (`ack_num == first_seq`, acknowledges only the
   SYN, never any data byte), making
   `bytes_sent_before_first_client_ack` ALWAYS `None` by construction,
   NEVER reflecting what the function actually tried to measure. The
   function's own docstring already described the CORRECT behavior
   ("ack_num > server data's initial seq") -- the code never
   implemented that condition. Fixed: skips any ACK that acknowledges
   <= `first_seq`, uses the first one that actually acknowledges real
   data (verified with the real pcap numbers: 2896 bytes, not `None`).

used the wrong result):** `PILOT_RUNBOOK.md` never had a step
delivering the 3 business-backend images (`auth`/`mongo_seed`/

block` (inside Step 10) broke with `auth.tar nao encontrado` on this
round's first attempt. Fixed with a new Step 8b in the runbook.

dedicated producer -- none touches `CERTIFICATE_BASELINE` or any other
pre-registered threshold, none changes what criteria 2/3/7 actually
measure (it only fixes the measurement MECHANISM). Same class as
Decisions 81/86/87/88/89 (real infrastructure findings, fixed live,
never a STOP).

Phase B complete, end to end, for the first time in this package's history -- 60/60 runs, 12/12 captures, the 7 criteria evaluated with 100% real data; 3 NEW findings (never seen before, never testable locally) found in the results, none fixed live (they would be changes to the measurement METHOD, not infrastructure)

**Steps 12-15, all green:** `collect_artifacts.py` (19 files verified
by sha256 manifest, pulled to the operator BEFORE any teardown --
a lesson applied after a sequencing error in Decision 92);
`consolidate_v9_pilot.py` (generated `RELATORIO_PILOTO.md`+
`criteria_evaluation.json` in `thesis/results/v9/piloto/
dados_oficiais/piloto-real-aws-2026-11-09/`); `emergency_stop.py` dry
(5/5/3/4 expected resources, no drift); `cleanup.py --release-eips
--force` (`all_clean: true`); independent final check (12 `describe-*`
calls, 3 regions, all empty).

**Overall result: 4/7 PASS (criteria 3/4/5/6), 3/7 FAIL (criteria
1/2/7) -- the FIRST time the 7 criteria are evaluated against 100%
real data, end to end, in this history. The 3 FAILs are NEW and REAL
findings, never seen before because no previous attempt got this far
-- none is an infrastructure/transport bug (the class that Decisions
81/86/87/88/89/94 have already resolved live); the 3 touch the
measurement METHOD itself, requiring Luciano's decision before any
correction (rule 7(e)).**

**Criterion 1 (per-message sizes) -- FAIL.** Classico/pqc/hibrido-
v8/hibrido-and: L219 and L325 PASS in all 4 (confirming Decision 91/93
working perfectly against the real network, again, now in the 12
OFFICIAL captures, not just in the smoke-test mechanism proof).
**L0 fails in all 4 profiles, always the SAME way:** of each L0
capture's 6 mTLS connections, ONLY the ClientHello and ServerHello
decrypt (183B, always correct) -- EncryptedExtensions/
CertificateRequest/Certificate/CertificateVerify/Finished never
appear, in ANY later frame, for the 6 connections, in all 4 profiles
-- confirmed that the raw packets DO EXIST in the pcap (real
tcp.len>0, never missing frames), only the TLS dissector never
decrypts them. Hypothesis (never confirmed byte for byte, needs deeper
investigation): L0 is the ONLY near-zero-RTT route -- the 6 connections
complete so fast that the keylog (`/tmp/v9_keylog.txt`, written by the
Go gateway) may not be fully flushed to disk at the moment
`dedicated_capture` does `docker exec cat` on it, moments later --
L219/L325 (real RTT) naturally give the process more time to flush
between secrets.

**Criterion 2 (real initcwnd) -- FAIL.** `segments_computed ≈ 0.32`
(2896B / 8961B MSS) vs `ss_ti_cwnd = 10` -- the two sources disagree
A LOT (diff ≈ 9.7 >> tolerance of 2). Investigated: the extracted
`mss_bytes` comes from the server's SYN-ACK (8961B, the NIC's LOCAL
jumbo-frame capacity, `pmtu:9001` confirmed in `ss -ti` itself), but
the connection's EFFECTIVE MSS (`ss -ti` shows `mss:1448`, the value
the KERNEL actually uses) is much smaller -- PMTU discovery reduces it
to ~1500 on the public inter-region path. Even recalculating with 1448
(2 segments), it still diverges from the cwnd=10 reported by the
kernel -- `ss -ti` also shows `pacing_rate 1.05Mbps`: TCP PACING
(BBR/fq, default on modern Linux kernels) deliberately limits the send
rate INDEPENDENTLY of the available cwnd, so "bytes sent before the
first ACK" may never reflect the configured cwnd on a REAL connection
with pacing enabled -- one channel may be measuring cwnd (kernel
configuration) and the other the pacing rate (send policy), never the
same quantity. Never tested against a real kernel/NIC before this
attempt.

**Criterion 7 (per-route latency sanity) -- FAIL on L219/L325 (L0
PASSES).** `rtt_ms_pcap` comes out at ~0.06-0.10ms on the 3 routes,
WAY below the nominal (0/219/325ms) for L219/L325 -- it only matches
for L0 (which coincidentally is ALSO ~0). Investigated: the `pcap`
channel extracts the delta between the SYN frame arriving and the
SYN-ACK frame leaving, BOTH captured on the SAME SERVER interface
(`dedicated_capture`, Decision 52) -- this measures only the server's
PROCESSING TIME (SYN->SYN-ACK on the same host), NEVER the real
network RTT (which would need BOTH propagation legs, client->server
AND
server->client, invisible in a capture taken only on the server).
A design that had never been exercised against a route with real RTT
>0 before this attempt -- L0 "passed" by coincidence (real RTT and
processing time are both tiny).

**Why these 3 are STOPs, never fix-and-repeats:** all three touch the
METHOD/mechanism for measuring criteria 1/2/7 (never just
infrastructure/transport) -- changing any of them CHANGES what is
measured, exactly what rule 7(e) of this authorization requires
handling with a stop. Criteria 3 (zero errors, L325), 4 (flow counts),
5 (zero errors) and 6 (instrumentation+assertions) PASS with 100% real
data, without reservation.

**Decisions pending from Luciano:**
1. Criterion 1 -- investigate the real cause of the L0 decryption gap

   `docker exec cat keylog` in `dedicated_capture`, or another
   approach.
2. Criterion 2 -- decide whether `mss_bytes` should come from the
   EFFECTIVE MSS (`ss -ti`) instead of the SYN-ACK, and/or whether
   pacing needs to enter the agreement formula between the 2 channels
   (or a different tolerance), or whether the criterion's method needs
   revisiting.
3. Criterion 7 -- the `pcap` channel needs capture on BOTH SIDES
   (client AND server) to measure real RTT, or needs to be
   redesigned/discarded as an independent channel for this criterion.

## 97. RTT-pcap Amendment to criterion 7 -- the pcap channel measured the server's LOCAL PROCESSING time (SYN arriving -> SYN-ACK leaving, both on the SAME interface), never the real network RTT; fixed to SYN-ACK leaving -> the ACK closing the handshake coming back (same capture, zero new endpoint, zero new SG rule); validated with ground truth (Decision 100)

**Formal amendment label:**
- **What changed:** the METHOD of criterion 7's `rtt_ms_pcap` channel
  -- from "client's SYN arriving -> server's SYN-ACK leaving" to
  "server's SYN-ACK leaving -> the client's first ACK (which closes
  the 3-way handshake, Decision 94 already confirmed it never
  acknowledges data) arriving back". The acceptance range (nominal
  +-10%, L0 floor from Amendment 5) and the second channel
  (rtt_ms_probe, TCP/443) do not change.
- **Reason:** a real finding from Decision 95 -- the old method
  measures two events on the SAME server interface, WITH NO network
  propagation between them -- it is local processing time (confirmed
  both by theory AND by ground truth, Decision 100: 0.024ms measured
  in a test with a REAL configured RTT of 50ms). The new method covers
  the complete outbound (server->client) AND return (client->server)
  legs on the SAME server-only capture -- genuinely real RTT, without
  needing a capture on the client.
- **Date:** 2026-11-09.
- **Pairing by tcp.stream** (never by list order/index -- streams can
  interleave under a real network, Decision 91).
- **The criterion's tolerance (+-10%, L0 floor) was read and CONFIRMED
  adequate** -- the absolute 1ms floor for L0 (Decision 32, Amendment
  5) already correctly handles the sub-millisecond case Luciano
  mentioned; no change needed there, no STOP.

criterio7_rtt.py: pcap_syn_synack_rtt/rtt_from_syn_synack_times
replaced by pcap_synack_ack_rtt/rtt_from_synack_ack_times/
pair_synack_ack_by_stream (explicit pairing by stream).
evaluate_criteria.py: criterion 7's docstring updated, no
threshold/data-format change.

**Validated with ground truth (Decision 100):** configured RTT of
5/50/200ms via tc netem (correct topology -- delay only on the client,
egress+ingress via ifb, never on the server) -- both channels (real
probe + new pcap) matched the configuration within +-2% across the 3
values; the OLD method, measured against the SAME real packets, showed
exactly the theorized symptom (0.024ms at a configured 50ms).

**Tests:** test_producers.py gains 3 (pairing by stream, a mutant
"old method measures only local processing", median robust to an
outlier with the new signature). test_dedicated_criteria.py unchanged
(the JSON interface -- rtt_ms_pcap/n_samples_pcap -- preserved, only
the internal implementation changed).

Same rules: no action on AWS, no commit before the scanner, report in
the chat.

## 98. Effective-MSS Amendment to criterion 2 -- mss_bytes came from the MSS ANNOUNCED in the SYN-ACK (the NIC's LOCAL jumbo capacity, Decision 34), never the EFFECTIVE MSS of the real path; fixed to a mandatory AGREEMENT between ss -ti and the largest real payload from the pcap, otherwise FAIL; a formal deviation from the pre-registration (Decision 34), declared for the thesis; validated with ground truth (Decision 100)

**Formal amendment label, DECLARED deviation from the pre-registration:**
- **What changed:** the METHOD for obtaining `mss_bytes` in criterion 2
  -- from "MSS from the server's SYN-ACK options" (Decision 34 said
  "read from the SYN options of the same connection, never assumed" --
  the code implemented this by literally reading the SYN-ACK option,
  which is exactly the NIC's LOCAL capacity, never the real effective
  one) to a mandatory AGREEMENT between TWO channels of the EFFECTIVE
  MSS: (1) ss -ti, the kernel's own mss field; (2) the LARGEST real
  payload (tcp.len) that the server actually put on the wire, straight
  from the pcap. The threshold (INITCWND_MIN_SEGMENTS=10) does not
  change.
- **Reason:** the real AWS run (Decision 95) measured mss_bytes=8961
  (announced in the SYN-ACK, the instance's LOCAL jumbo-frame
  capacity) but the real EFFECTIVE MSS (ss -ti) was 1448 -- reduced by
  PMTU discovery on the real inter-region path. Using the announced
  value inflated segments_computed's denominator by ~6x, making the
  criterion fail for a MEASUREMENT reason, never for the reality of
  initcwnd.
- **Date:** 2026-11-09.
- **Explicitly declared as a deviation from the pre-registration**
  (Decision 34 defined MSS from "the SYN options" without specifying
  which side of the connection nor distinguishing announced-vs-
  effective -- the literal implementation followed the SYN-ACK) -- to
  be reported in the thesis methodology.

**Method adopted:** criterio2_probe.py gains ss_ti_snapshot with the
mss field (besides cwnd, already existing); extract_mss_and_bytes_
before_ack now also returns mss_pcap_max_payload (the largest tcp.len
among the server's data segments), a new helper function
effective_mss(ss_ti_mss, mss_pcap_max_payload) -- they agree (0B
diff) => uses the value, mss_channels_agree=True; they disagree =>
mss_bytes=None, mss_channels_agree=False. The MSS announced in the
SYN-ACK is still recorded (mss_synack_announced_bytes), ONLY as
diagnostic -- never enters the calculation. evaluate_criteria.py's
criterion_2_initcwnd requires mss_channels_agree is True BEFORE any
segment calculation -- missing/False fails for that reason
specifically.

**Validated with ground truth (Decision 100):** MTU 1500 (ethtool
TSO/GSO/GRO off) -- ss_ti_mss=1448, mss_pcap_max_payload=1448, they
agree; MTU 9001 (jumbo) -- ss_ti_mss=8949, mss_pcap_max_payload=8949,
they agree -- in BOTH cases the SYN-ACK announced value (1460/8961) is
SLIGHTLY different from the effective one (TCP option overhead such
as timestamp), reinforcing why it should never be used directly. GSO
enabled (an incidental finding, before turning off the offloads for
the main test) inflated mss_pcap_max_payload into a "super-packet"
(21720B) -- the mandatory agreement correctly FAILED that case, never
accepted it by accident.

**Additional finding, not requested but relevant (see Decision 100):**
in BOTH MTU tests (configured RTT=40ms), segments_computed came out
well below ss_ti_cwnd=10 -- TCP pacing (observed pacing_rate,
5.75-35.4Mbps) throttles sending independently of the available cwnd,
reproducing in a controlled, repeatable way the SAME phenomenon that
Decision 95 had already found against the real AWS (pending decision
#2) -- strengthens that analysis: it is not a fluke of the real
network, it is a generic pacing effect on any new connection
(slow-start).

**Tests:** test_producers.py gains 6 (mss alongside cwnd in the
snapshot, effective_mss agreeing/disagreeing, a mutant "would use the
announced value by default"). test_evaluate_criteria.py gains 4
(criterion_2_initcwnd passes when they agree, fails when
mss_channels_agree=False/missing, a mutant replicating the OLD logic
that would incorrectly accept an ACCIDENTAL agreement between
segments_computed with the wrong MSS and ss_ti_cwnd).

Same rules: no action on AWS, no commit before the scanner, report in
the chat.

## 99. Capture-robustness Amendment to criterion 1 -- dedicated_capture checks for IMMEDIATE and COMPLETE decryption (6 mTLS streams, server Certificate decrypted) before accepting a capture, RETRIES (up to 3x) ONLY when the failure mode is incomplete decryption, NEVER for a size mismatch; preserves pcap+keylog from EVERY attempt (success or failure)

**Luciano's request (item 3):** do not guess the cause of the L0
decryption gap (Decision 95) -- make the capture ROBUST: before
finishing, check for immediate, complete decryption; if it is missing,
redo it (only when the failure mode is incomplete decryption, never a
size mismatch), up to 3x, recording every attempt; preserve the pcap
and keylog from all of them, including the failed ones.

**Mechanism:** evaluate_criteria.py gains capture_decryption_
complete(raw_lines, expected_streams=6) -- it factors out the
per-stream classification (_classify_streams, extracted from
_message_sizes_stream_aware without changing its behavior, confirmed
byte for byte by the whole suite passing) and checks that the
expected_streams (6, N_mTLS, Decision 91) real client-facing
connections have the SERVER's Certificate decrypted
(tls.handshake.type==11 readable) -- it NEVER decides size/mismatch,
only WHETHER the capture decrypted enough to be evaluated.

orchestrator.py's dedicated_capture was rewritten with a loop of UP TO
MAX_CAPTURE_ATTEMPTS=3 attempts: each uses its OWN pcap/keylog/log
(numbered _attemptN), fires off a NEW trigger connection, extracts via
tshark, checks capture_decryption_complete -- only accepts and exits
the loop when n_handshake_rows > 0 and complete; otherwise, tries
again (an extra 2s sleep, instead of 1s, before the docker exec cat on
the keylog -- gives more time for the disk flush, Decision 95's
hypothesis, but NEVER the only fix -- the retry covers the case where
that still is not enough). If all 3 attempts fail, it raises with the
complete log of each one (attempts_log) -- it NEVER masks, NEVER
reports an incomplete capture as if it were complete. The WINNING
attempt is copied on the server to the name WITHOUT a suffix
(criterio1_<profile>_<route>.pcap/.txt) -- run_criterio7
(dedicated_criteria.py) continues finding the pcap by the same name,
unchanged.

**Preservation (item 0, Decision 96):** _preserve_capture_attempt
pulls pcap+keylog from EVERY attempt (success or failure) to the local
capturas_dir (capturas_brutas/), PLUS the winner under the clean name
-- no attempt is silently discarded.

**A size mismatch never triggers a retry** (Luciano's explicit
requirement): the retry is only triggered by capture_decryption_
complete() == False -- a capture that decrypted everything but
diverges from the baseline (_message_sizes_stream_aware) is accepted
and reported as is, never retried.

**Tests:** test_evaluate_criteria.py gains 4 (capture_decryption_
complete with 6 complete streams, with L0-partial reproducing Decision
95's real symptom, with fewer than 6 streams, a mutant that ignores a
missing Certificate). test_orchestrator.py gains 4 (retries when the
1st attempt is incomplete and the 2nd is complete, fails after the 3
attempts with decryption always incomplete, preserves pcap/keylog from
EVERY attempt including failures, a mutant "would accept a partial

## 100. LOCAL validation (no AWS) of Amendments 97/98 with GROUND TRUTH -- tc netem on real Docker containers (RTT 5/50/200ms, MTU 1500/9001), against the REAL producers (criterio2_probe.py/criterio7_rtt.py), with no modification or monkeypatch whatsoever

**Luciano's request (item 4):** validate the fixes locally with
ground truth -- tc netem on containers (--cap-add NET_ADMIN),
configured RTT (5/50/200ms) and MTU/MSS (1500/9001), proving that the
RTT and initcwnd measured by BOTH channels match the configured values
within tolerance; mutants (wrong channel, SYN-ACK MSS).

**Topology (a real finding, fixed live, documented in
campaign/tc_netem_ground_truth/IDENTIDADE.json):** the first attempt
(symmetric 25/25ms delay on EGRESS on both sides) correctly measured
the total RTT via ping, but the pcap SYN->SYN-ACK channel showed 25ms
(not ~0) -- investigated: tcpdump captures EGRESS packets AFTER
netem's delay is applied, so delay on the SERVER's EGRESS contaminates
the "SYN-ACK leaving" event itself with an artificial LOCAL delay,
which the real network never has (propagation happens only ON THE
WIRE, never as a local queue observable by the sender itself). Fixed:
delay ONLY on the CLIENT side -- egress (outbound) + ingress via ifb
(tc filter ... action mirred egress redirect dev ifb0) -- correctly
reproducing "zero local overhead, propagation only on the wire", the
SAME premise criterion 7's new method assumes.

**Real results (criterion 7, RTT):** configured RTT 5ms -> probe
channel 5.233ms / new pcap channel 5.186ms. Configured RTT 50ms ->
probe channel 50.353ms / new pcap channel 50.564ms / OLD pcap channel
(same pcap) 0.024ms. Configured RTT 200ms -> probe channel 200.408ms
/ new pcap channel 200.218ms.

Both real channels matched the configuration within +-2% across the 3
values (well inside the criterion's +-10%); the OLD method, measured
against the SAME real packets captured at 50ms, confirms the
theorized symptom (local processing time, not RTT).

**Real results (criterion 2, effective MSS):** MTU 1500 -> ss -ti
mss=1448, largest real payload (pcap)=1448, announced SYN-ACK=1460,
they agree=yes. MTU 9001 -> ss -ti mss=8949, largest real payload
(pcap)=8949, announced SYN-ACK=8961, they agree=yes.

The two effective-MSS channels agree EXACTLY across both MTUs tested;
the SYN-ACK announced value always differs slightly (TCP option
overhead such as timestamp) -- it should never be used directly,
confirming Amendment 98. GSO enabled (an incidental finding before
turning off the offloads) inflated the pcap channel into a
"super-packet" (21720B) -- the mandatory agreement correctly FAILED
that case, never accepted it by accident.

**Additional finding (not requested, reported for relevance):** in
both MTU tests (RTT=40ms), segments_computed came out well below
ss_ti_cwnd=10 due to TCP pacing -- it reproduces in a controlled,
repeatable way the SAME phenomenon that Decision 95 reported as
pending decision #2 against the real AWS (strengthens that analysis,
does not resolve it -- the pending decision remains with Luciano).

**No producer was altered for this test** -- it runs the SAME
criterio2_probe.py/criterio7_rtt.py that goes to AWS, with no network
monkeypatch whatsoever (only real containers/tc). The containers,
networks and Docker images used were all REMOVED after collection (no
persistent resource, no real IP, no credential). Evidence (real JSON
from each run + IDENTIDADE.json with the complete method) in
thesis/results/v9/campaign/tc_netem_ground_truth/.

## 102. Window-robustness Amendment to criterion 2 -- a real finding investigated by content (never by guesswork): segments_computed=2.0 was NOT TCP pacing (Decision 101 reported it wrong) -- it was a counting bug by ACK number, never by send timestamp. Fixed, validated with real ground truth (initcwnd 4/10/20, with and without fq), reanalyzed OFFLINE from the SAME preserved pcap -- criterion 2 PASSES. Phase B: 7/7 PASS

**Investigation, by Luciano's explicit request: prove or disprove
pacing from the real packet timeline, never by assumption.**
Reconstructed the complete timeline (microsecond timestamp, tshark)
of this round's real pcap (criterio2_probe.pcap, L219, classico,
already preserved by Decision 96):

- The server's SYN-ACK leaves at t=.245875; the client's handshake ACK
  arrives at t=.465820 -- real RTT = 219.945ms (matches `ss -ti`:
  219.99ms).
- **The 1st flight's 10 segments leave between t=.484441 and
  t=.484522 -- 81us end to end, ~9us between consecutive segments.**
  The reported `pacing_rate` (1.05Mbps) would require ~11ms of
  distance between 1448B segments -- **~1000x slower** than what was
  observed. NO pacing signature in the real packets.
- The 1st flight has EXACTLY 10 segments (14.480B) -- matches
  `ss_ti_cwnd=10` exactly (snapshot taken BEFORE any sending) and the
  2nd flight (20 segments, slow-start doubling from 10 to 20,
  starting at t=.704672).
- The server had 71,680B to send (5x more than 1 window of 14.480B)
  -- never limited by lack of data.
- The client sends 5 ACK packets arriving in a tight CLUSTER
  (t=.704618-.704619, acks 2897/5793/8689/11585/14481) -- the FIRST of
  these (2897) covers only the first 2 segments of the real flight of
  10.

**Confirmed root cause:** `extract_mss_and_bytes_before_ack` (Decision
94) stopped at the FIRST ACK packet it saw with `ack_num >
first_seq` -- under real RTT, the client never sends just 1 ACK, it
sends SEVERAL arriving almost together, and the method only counted
what THAT FIRST one covered (2 of 10 segments = 2896B), never the
complete flight. Decision 101 attributed this to TCP pacing --
**WRONG**, corrected by the dated note in Decision 101 above.

**Branch, as requested:** the real `ss -ti`, taken BEFORE any sending,
reports `cwnd:10` -- NEVER less than 10. This is NOT a host/kernel
configuration finding (not a STOP) -- it is a METHOD bug, fixed below.

**Corrected method (`criterio2_probe.py`):** `extract_bytes_sent_
within_rtt_window` counts SERVER data bytes by SEND TIMESTAMP (never
by ACK number), within the window `[time of the 1st data segment,
+1 RTT]`. The RTT comes from an INDEPENDENT measurement, on the SAME
connection (`rtt_from_handshake_same_connection`: the server's SYN-ACK
LEAVING -> the client's handshake ACK ARRIVING back -- the SAME
method as criterion 7's RTT-pcap Amendment, Decision 97) -- never
derived from the DATA ACKs' behavior, which is exactly what caused the
bug. Robust to clustered ACKs and to a delayed/lost ACK, because it
never looks at the data ACKs to decide HOW MUCH was sent, only UNTIL
WHEN to count. Field renamed from `bytes_sent_before_first_
client_ack` to `bytes_sent_within_first_rtt_window` (an explicit
deviation, never a name that lies about what it measures) -- a new
field `rtt_ms_used_for_window` recorded for auditing.
`evaluate_criteria.criterion_2_initcwnd` updated for the new field
name.

**Validated with ground truth BEFORE touching any real data**
(Luciano's explicit request) -- a genuine `ip route ... initcwnd N` on
the server (never assumed), N=4/10/20, the same tc netem topology as
Decision 100, against the real `criterio2_probe.py`, with no
modification whatsoever:

| Configuration | `ss_ti_cwnd` | `bytes_sent_within_first_rtt_window` | `segments_computed` |
|---|---|---|---|
| N=4, no fq | 4 | 5.792 | **4.0** |
| N=10, no fq | 10 | 14.480 | **10.0** |
| N=20, no fq | 20 | 28.960 | **20.0** |
| N=10, **fq (real pacing) on**, confirmed by `tc qdisc show` | 10 | 14.480 | **10.0** |

Both channels matched the real configuration exactly in all 4 cases,
including with real pacing active -- proof that the method is NOT
biased to always report 10. Mutant (a response of only 2,048B, less
than 1 window of cwnd=10): the method correctly reports 2,048B (never
fakes window-limited when it is genuinely data-limited). Evidence in
`campaign/tc_netem_ground_truth/evidencia_initcwnd/`.

**OFFLINE reanalysis of the real pcap already preserved (NEVER a new
AWS round, exactly as requested) -- only AFTER the above validation
passed:** `criterio2_probe.pcap` (L219, classico, Decision 96)
reanalyzed by the corrected, validated method:

```
mss_pcap_max_payload = 1448 (mss_channels_agree=true, unchanged)
rtt_ms_used_for_window = 219.945
bytes_sent_within_first_rtt_window = 14.480
segments_computed = 10.0 (== ss_ti_cwnd, agree=true)
```

`thesis/results/v9/piloto/dados_oficiais/piloto-real-aws-2026-11-09-
v2/raw/criterio2_initcwnd.json` updated with the reanalyzed fields
(the ORIGINAL value, by the old buggy method, preserved in full in
`criterio2_initcwnd_original_bug_decisao_95_101.
json`, never deleted -- full auditability). `criteria_evaluation.
json`/`RELATORIO_PILOTO.md` regenerated by `consolidate_v9_pilot.py`
against the SAME `raw/` (no new raw data).

**Phase B's final result, 5th attempt, reanalyzed: 7/7 PASS.** The
first time in this package's history with the 7 criteria passing on
100% real AWS data.

**Honest method limitation, explicitly recorded (Luciano's request,
NEVER scope creep to resolve now):** `criterio2_probe.py` only runs on
route L219 (`CRITERIO2_PROBE_ROUTE`, Decision 85 -- L0 excluded by
design, RTT~0 makes the method meaningless; L325 was NEVER wired up,
a pre-existing gap, never noticed before for lack of evidence
exposing it). The probe only measures the server->client direction
(the server sending data to the client that connected) -- NEVER the
client->server direction, which is relevant for the CLIENT's own
flights during the real mTLS handshakes (e.g., client Certificate,
Finished). The pre-registered criterion (Decision 14/24/34) does not
explicitly specify route nor direction -- this is a real COVERAGE GAP,
declared here, never hidden, never resolved this round.

**Tests:** `test_producers.py` gains 5 (MSS separate from the old bug,
handshake RTT matches the real one, a 1-RTT window counts the real
complete flight -- 14.480B never 2,896B --, a mutant "counts by ACK
number" reproduces the old bug, a mutant "wrong window" short/long
errs the wrong way), using this pcap's REAL data as a fixture (never
just synthetic). `test_evaluate_criteria.py` updated for the new field
name. 263 tests total, all green.

**Process finding, fixed live:** `consolidate_v9_pilot.py` does
`shutil.rmtree(dest_raw)` BEFORE `shutil.copytree(collected_
dir, dest_raw)` -- passing `--collected-dir`/`--out-dir` pointing to
the SAME `raw/` (a real error this session) erases the source before

checkout` (Decision 101's commit already had everything versioned) --
no data genuinely lost, confirmed by `git status` before and after.
Fixed by reapplying the reanalysis in a STAGING copy outside the

run) and concluded "more consistent with client-side sequencing (the
6 connections are not kept continuously busy nor run in parallel)
than with extra network RTTs inside a SINGLE connection's handshake"
-- **not attributed with confidence**.

**Tested with v9's real components:**
1. **RTT-extra-per-initcwnd hypothesis: NOW DISCARDED with confirmed
   REAL data, not just assumed.** Decision 14's formula (`extra RTTs =
   max(0, ceil(flight_bytes/cwnd_bytes)-1)`) already showed 0 extra
   RTTs for the 4 profiles with an assumed `initcwnd=10` -- Decision
   102 now empirically CONFIRMS (real `ss -ti` + real pcap, not
   assumption) that the pilot's real instances genuinely have
   `initcwnd=10`. **Conclusion: 0ms of the 240-260ms residual can come
   from this mechanism, for NONE of the 4 profiles, on NONE of the
   pilot's routes** -- this reinforces (it does not literally re-prove
   it for v8, these are different instances, but it removes the same
   class of doubt v8 had) v8's own report's conclusion that the
   residual does NOT originate from extra network RTT.
2. **v9's CPU microbenchmarks (Decision 14) are ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE
   smaller than v8's "signing"/"verification" PHASES -- found that the
   two tables are NOT the same quantity, they cannot be added
   directly.** The cost of PURE RSA-2048 signing+verification (just
   the cryptographic operation, N=2000): ~858us (0.858ms) -- against
   the 16.2ms (Classico) that v8's "signing" PHASE reports, ~19x
   larger. This means v8's "signing" PHASE **never measured just the
   pure cryptographic operation** -- it includes Go's `crypto/tls`
   overhead, buffer I/O, or a wider measurement boundary than the
   isolated operation. **Honest conclusion: v9's CPU components CANNOT
   be arithmetically added to v8's residual to "explain" a fraction of
   it -- the two tables measure different quantities, attempting a
   direct sum would produce a meaningless number.**
3. **Ticket cost: NEVER applies to this residual.** v9 runs with
   `TICKETS_DISABLED=true` (confirmed in the pilot's real environment,
   Decision 101/gateway env) -- v9's residual, if there were one,
   would NEVER include ticket cost. Historical v8 may or may not have
   had tickets contributing to ITS original residual -- **a real
   asymmetry between the two setups, declared here, never hidden.**

**Final, honest conclusion, NEVER forced:** v9's real components do
not attribute v8's historical ~14% residual to a new specific cause --
they remain the SAME conclusion as v8's final report ("not
attributed", client-side sequencing, not network). What v9 genuinely
ADDS: the RTT-extra-per-initcwnd hypothesis is now discarded with
empirical confirmation (not assumption), and the scale incompatibility
between v9's CPU microbenchmarks and v8's time phases is explicitly
documented (preventing an invalid arithmetic sum a hasty reader might
attempt). Gap #5 remains **PARTIAL, not CLOSED** -- kept honest, never
forced closed.

## Decision 105 -- BLOCK B (offline, old data preserved, no AWS): real extraction of hibrido-and's dual signature + finding of an encoding bug in the experimental stack

Luciano's request (BLOCK B, item 1/2/3): extract, from the REAL handshake Certificate message (never from the source code), the two certificates involved in hibrido-and's dual signature, with proof that both were validated; and replace the `openssl asn1parse` inference of the pqc profile's ML-DSA certificate with a direct tool reading.

**Real finding 1 -- the `tshark --export-objects x509af` exporter is insufficient:** when extracting certificates from the 12 official pcap+keylog pairs (`raw/criterio1_capturas/`), the exporter correctly reassembled classico/hibrido-v8/pqc's RSA certificates, but for hibrido-and it produced, besides the 2 expected RSA certificates, 11-12 unnamed 23-24-byte objects (`(null).cer`) -- fragments, never valid certificates (`openssl` cannot decode them). Investigated thoroughly (never dismissed as "noise"): hibrido-and's real Certificate message (confirmed via `tshark -x` with the keylog, reading the "Decrypted TLS" block that tshark prints, and manually parsing the RFC 8446 Section 4.4.2 structure in Python) contains **TWO real CertificateEntry items in the SAME message**: one RSA-2048 (serial 10 server/11 client, `CN=hibrido_and_rsa_{server,client}`) and one ML-DSA-65 (serial 12 server/13 client, `CN=hibrido_and_mldsa_{server,client}`) -- with **3 zero-padding bytes not predicted by the RFC between the two entries** (a real encoding feature of this profile's experimental stack, not a parsing error in this project -- confirmed reproducible across the 3 routes, server and client, 12 identical occurrences).

**Proof that the extraction matches the real material:** the 2 ML-DSA certificates extracted from the pcap (server and client) have a sha256 IDENTICAL, byte for byte, to the real `.crt` files on disk (`certs/generated/hibrido_and_mldsa_{server,client}.crt`, the real PKI used in deployment, never source code) -- 4/4 checks `identical: true` (RSA+ML-DSA, server+client).

**Real finding 2 -- proof that both were validated:** `raw/full_container_logs/v9-mtls.log` shows 6/6 of hibrido-and's real connections (excluding the unrelated internal channel `clientCert="op"`) with `dualAuthenticated=true` and real `handshakeBytesIn`/`handshakeBytesOut` (e.g., 11902/12177 bytes) -- consistent with the additional volume of the ML-DSA certificate (~5.5KB) over hibrido-v8's RSA-only volume (~8.4KB total). The TLS stack (Go `crypto/tls`) only reaches "connection OK" after processing the whole Certificate message (both entries) with no error -- an honest limitation recorded: the INFO-level log does not distinguish "I verified RSA" from "I verified ML-DSA" as separate lines; the available evidence is the aggregated result, never a per-certificate trace.

**Real finding 3 -- replacing `openssl asn1parse`:** a minimal, generic DER parser was written in Python (`read_der_len`/`read_der_tlv`/`der_oid_to_str`/`parse_der_certificate_generic`, in `build_consolidated_report_v9.py`) that reads the OID and the byte length of the public key and the signature DIRECTLY from the ASN.1 structure (`SubjectPublicKeyInfo`/`signatureValue`), without depending on any library having NATIVE support for the algorithm (the available `cryptography` 46.x library and `openssl` 3.2.4 cannot load an ML-DSA key) and without cross-validating against the JWKS (Decision 103's method, now replaced as the primary source -- agreement with the real JWKS remains as secondary corroboration, never the main evidence). Confirmed: ML-DSA-65 (OID 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.3.18) in both pqc AND hibrido-and's PQC component, raw public key 1952 bytes, raw signature 3309 bytes -- EXACTLY the same in both profiles (an automated check FAILS HARD, never just logs, if this diverges).

**Never a pre-registration deviation** -- this is an evidence-EXTRACTION technique for a descriptive report, never a pre-registered criterion/threshold/method of the pilot's 7 criteria. No new data collected, no image rebuilt, no action on AWS -- just a deeper reading of the SAME pcap+keylog already preserved (`piloto-real-aws-2026-11-09-v2/raw/`) and the SAME log file already preserved, cross-checked against real PKI files on disk (never source code, never committed -- `certs/generated/` is not tracked by git).

**Dated correction (2026-11-09, same day, Luciano's request via the coordinator):** the paragraph above ("Real finding 1") calls the 3 zero bytes between the two CertificateEntry items "a real encoding bug of the experimental stack" -- **this is WRONG**. We went straight to the patch's source code (`toolchain/patches/and.patch`, function `marshalDualCertificate`, lines ~1889-1928) and confirmed: it is an **intentional delimiter of the AND mechanism**, explicitly documented in the patch's own comment -- "a 3-zero-byte delimiter entry carrying NO extensions field at all" -- used by `unmarshalDualAwareCertificate` (same patch, ~line 1960) to separate the classical chain from the post-quantum chain within the SAME `certificate_list`: any entry with zero-length `cert_data` is recognized as the delimiter (never a real certificate, which never has zero bytes), explicitly rejecting a repeated delimiter or one at the ends. **An implementation feature, not a bug.**

Also confirmed, by Luciano's explicit request, that `CERTIFICATE_BASELINE["hibrido-and"]` (6582, Decision 93/98, `integration/evaluate_criteria.py` line 145) **ALREADY accounts for these 3 bytes correctly** -- the formula uses `_tls13_certificate_message_size([914, 5647], extra_extension_bytes=[0, 3])`, whose result (6582) matches EXACTLY the real value measured in 2 independent captures (Decision 84 local, Decision 92 AWS) and in this very round (`Certificates Length: 6574`, `tls.handshake.length: 6578`, a decrypted buffer of 6582 bytes -- all confirmed in this session). A precision note (never a numeric discrepancy, only the source code's prose explanation): the comment on lines 140-143 of `evaluate_criteria.py` attributes the 3 bytes to the "REAL extension of the ML-DSA leaf" -- reading the patch, they are actually the 3 bytes of the delimiter (its OWN `CertificateEntry`, zero bytes of `cert_data`, with no extensions field at all), which sits BEFORE the ML-DSA leaf, not INSIDE it. The TOTAL byte sum is identical under both readings (919 RSA + 3 delimiter + 5652 ML-DSA = 6574 = 919 RSA + 5655 "ML-DSA with extra_extension_bytes=3") -- so the baseline number (6582) remains correct and needs no correction; only the code comment's explanatory sentence attributes these 3 bytes to the wrong structural element. Reported here as requested (never fixed without authorization) -- if Luciano wants, the comment on `evaluate_criteria.py` lines 140-143 can be adjusted in a future session to cite the delimiter instead of the "ML-DSA leaf's extension", without changing any number.

**14-byte difference between hibrido-and's RSA DER (914B) and classico's (900B), concrete cause identified (never assumed):** comparing the two real certificates extracted in this session, field by field -- identical SAN in both (same 10 entries, same order, same bytes), identical public key size (270B DER, 2048 bits), identical signature size (256B), no Alt-Signature/Catalyst extension (Bindel et al.) present in EITHER one (hibrido-and's RSA leaf is a pure X.509 certificate, with no extension beyond KeyUsage/EKU/AKI/SAN, the same 4 that classico has) -- the ONLY real difference is the size of the CN strings: `CN=classico_server` (15 characters) vs `CN=hibrido_and_rsa_server` (22 characters, +7 bytes) in the Subject, and `CN=classico_ca` (11 characters) vs `CN=hibrido_and_rsa_ca` (18 characters, +7 bytes) in the Issuer. +7B +7B = **+14B, exact**, closes the complete difference with no residual. It is not a different CA chain (depth 1 in both, direct root CA), not the serial (both fit in 1 INTEGER byte, serial 2 and serial 10), not validity (same UTCTime format in both).
