## Decision 107 -- BLOCK A: generalizing the orchestrator/tools to N servers (official campaign, 3 servers/8 routes), never rewriting the pilot's already-validated logic

Luciano decided (via the coordinator, 2026-11-09, after BLOCK A reported that the pilot's real orchestrator (`orchestrator.py`) assumes a SINGLE server throughout its code -- `_server_ip()`, `_server_gateway_ip(route)`, `_gateway_logs()`, `_launch_gateway()`, `_deliver_backend_images()`, `dedicated_criteria.collect_full_logs()`/`run_criterio2()`, `deliver_source.py`, `pki_relay.py` -- and that the official campaign's real topology (7 regions, **3 servers** in sa-east-1/us-east-1/ap-northeast-1, 8 routes, per the real Terraform in `terraform_campanha_oficial/`, a finding already recorded in `outputs.tf`'s own comment) would never run without adaptation): **ADAPT** the orchestrator to generalize it to N servers, never rewrite the pilot's already-validated logic (7/7 PASS, Decisions 96-103). Five rules applied, in this order:

**1. The `v9-ferramentas-congeladas` tag was never touched.** Confirmed in this Decision: `git rev-parse v9-ferramentas-congeladas` still points to the SAME commit (`eca35772ccc38aed69ffe1d02745ca0ad9952d83`) as when it was created -- no tag command run this round. All the generalization below was done by editing the `v9/fase1-local` branch's current working state, never moving nor recreating the tag it freezes.

**2. Complete survey of single-server assumptions, BEFORE changing anything** (findings, not assumption -- each item read directly in the code):
- `orchestrator.py`: `_server_ip()`, `_server_gateway_ip(route)`, `_gateway_logs()`, `_verify_gateway_binary`, `_verify_running_gateway_binary`, `_deliver_backend_images()`, `_launch_gateway()`, `start_block`/`stop_block` (inventory mutated via fixed `self.inventory["server"][...]`), `readiness_probe`/`run_execution`/`dedicated_capture` (same), `capture_ready_check()` (only tested `[self._server_ip()]`, never all servers).
- `dedicated_criteria.py`: `collect_full_logs()` (only one `server_ip`, never per-server), `run_criterio2()` (no direction parameter -- only server->client, never client->server; no label support, preventing reuse on L325/other routes simultaneously).
- `cleanup.py`, `emergency_stop.py`, `iam_dryrun_check.py`, `preflight.py`: an independent, HARDCODED region list in each of the 4 files -- a risk of divergence between them and between them and the real Terraform (the highest-risk finding, Finding #4, Luciano's condition 2).
- `deliver_source.py`: fixed `inventory["server"]["public_ip"]` -- would only deliver `SERVER_ONLY_FILES` to the first/only server, never to the other 2 in the campaign.
- `pki_relay.py` (`main()`): same pattern, `targets` built with a single fixed `"server"` target.
- Terraform (`terraform/modules/campaign_instance/main.tf`): the `Project` tag hardcoded to the PILOT's value in 6 places -- a real bug found and fixed BEFORE any apply (see below), not listed as an orchestrator finding but from the same survey.
Full list reported to Luciano (via the coordinator) as a checkpoint before any implementation, as rule 5 below itself authorized.

**3. Proof of compatibility (the 1-server/3-route pilot identical byte for byte).** Created `campaign/tests/_orchestrator_pre_generalization_baseline.py`: a LITERAL snapshot (`git show HEAD:...`) of `orchestrator.py` at the commit immediately before any generalization edit -- a frozen fixture, never edited afterward. A new test, `campaign/tests/test_pilot_regression_n_servidores.py`, loads this baseline via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` under a distinct module name, runs both versions (baseline and current) against the SAME pilot inventory, and compares literally: `_server_ip()`, `_server_gateway_ip()` (3 routes), `_client_ip()` (3 routes), and the list of SSH commands captured from `_gateway_logs()` -- 5 tests, IDENTICAL result between both versions, proven by a real diff, never by visual code inspection. The pre-existing full suite (263 tests) remains 100% green, with no assertion change needed in ~95% of the file (only 2 tests needed a signature/assertion adjustment for a legitimate API change -- `_backend_delivered` from `False` to `set()`, `_launch_gateway` gaining `route=None` -- never for a behavior regression).

**Approved design (region-suffixed labels + a ROUTE_SERVER map):** created `campaign/scripts/campaign_topology.py` as the single source of the campaign's topology -- `CAMPAIGN_REGIONS` (7), `CAMPAIGN_SERVERS` (3), `CAMPAIGN_ROUTE_SERVER` (route->server dict, 8 entries: `L0-sa-east-1`/`L123`/`L219`/`L325` -> sa-east-1, `L0-us-east-1`/`L14` -> us-east-1, `L0-ap-northeast-1`/`L30` -> ap-northeast-1 -- only the 3 `L0` routes need a region suffix to be unique; `L123`/`L219`/`L325`/`L14`/`L30` were already globally unique and stay as they were, with no change to any existing file/dict that indexes them by that name). `orchestrator.py` gained `route_server=None` in `__init__` and a new, single point of indirection, `_server_key(route=None)`: returns `self.inventory["server"]` (pilot, old behavior untouched) when `route_server is None`, or `self.inventory["servers"][self.route_server[route]]` (campaign) when configured. ALL the rest of the file that used to read `self.inventory["server"]` directly now reads through `_server_key`/`_server_ip(route)`/`_server_gateway_ip(route)` -- no duplicated logic, a single point of truth about "which server answers for this route".

**Condition 2 (single source of regions, Finding #4, highest risk):** `campaign_topology.regions_from_terraform()` extracts via regex the real regions declared in `terraform_campanha_oficial/providers.tf`; a dedicated test, `test_campaign_regions_bate_com_terraform_real` (in `test_campaign_topology.py`), FAILS automatically if `CAMPAIGN_REGIONS` (the Python constant) and the Terraform's real regions ever diverge -- never again a silent misalignment. `cleanup.py`, `emergency_stop.py`, `iam_dryrun_check.py`, `preflight.py` now consume `campaign_topology.CAMPAIGN_REGIONS` (a `--campaign` flag/`regions=` parameter, default `None` preserves the pilot's old behavior unchanged). `cleanup.py` gained `CAMPAIGN_EXPECTED_RUNNING_INSTANCES = 1 + len(CAMPAIGN_SERVERS) + len(CAMPAIGN_ROUTES)` (= 12), threaded through `count_running_instances_all_regions`/`check_self_terminate_drift`/`full_cleanup`.

**Condition 3 (label-to-scenario equivalence table):** `CAMPAIGN_SCENARIO_TABLE` in `campaign_topology.py` -- a list of dicts, one row per route, with `rota`/`servidor`/`regiao_cliente`/`nominal_rtt_ms`/`colocalizado`, covering the campaign's 8 routes. This is the official route<->scenario equivalence table for use in the thesis; recomputable by script (never a hand-typed number), derived from the same `CAMPAIGN_ROUTE_SERVER`/`CAMPAIGN_NOMINAL_RTT_MS` used by the rest of the code (never a second, parallel source that could diverge).

**Condition 4 (finding 10, full logs, per-server criterion 2 including L325 and the client->server direction):**
- CPU/mem-steal sampler: `_cpu_steal_sampler_start`/`_cpu_steal_sampler_stop_and_collect`/`_steal_pct_from_cpu_jsonl` in `orchestrator.py` -- a faithful port of v8's ALREADY-PROVEN real mechanism (`campaign_run.py`: a Python loop backgrounded via SSH, `nohup ... & echo $! > pid_path`, one JSON line per second from `/proc/stat`+`/proc/meminfo`, steal% computed as a CUMULATIVE DELTA between the first and last line, never an average nor a since-boot ratio). Entirely gated on `self.route_server is not None` -- zero effect, zero new call, on the pilot's path.
- `dedicated_criteria.collect_full_logs()`: generalized to collect logs from ALL servers in campaign mode (previously, just one); the report's key includes the server's label when there is more than one, preserving the old key (no label) in the pilot.
- `dedicated_criteria.run_criterio2()`: gained `direction` (`"server-to-client"`, default -- reproduces the pilot byte for byte -- or `"client-to-server"`, new) and `label` (`None` preserves the pilot's old fixed remote/local paths; any label produces separate `*_{label}.*` paths). A new `run_criterio2_campaign()` covers the 5 non-L0 routes (the 3 `L0` routes are co-located, nominal RTT zero, out of criterion 2's scope) x the 2 directions, including **L325 explicitly** (one of the two gaps that stayed documented as out of scope, now closed in code) -- per-combination failures are captured individually (`{"ok": bool, ...}`), never aborting the rest.
- Infrastructure that was missing to enable the client->server direction (the OTHER gap, also closed now): the pilot/campaign Security Group only opened port 9876 on the SERVERS (for the client to initiate the test connection) -- never on the clients. A new variable, `criterio2_reverse_ingress_cidrs` (default `{}`, no effect on the pilot) and a new resource, `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule.criterio2_probe_reverse`, in `terraform/modules/campaign_instance/main.tf`, applicable only to `role == "client"`. Wired into the 5 non-L0 client modules in `terraform_campanha_oficial/main.tf` (`client_ca_central_1_a`/`_b`, `client_eu_north_1`, `client_ap_southeast_1`, `client_ap_northeast_2`), each scoped to the `/32` of the specific server it serves (never a broader CIDR).
- `deliver_source.py`/`pki_relay.py`: generalized in the same pattern (`inventory["servers"]` plural, a dict per region-server, iterates and delivers/relays to EACH one; `inventory["server"]` singular, pilot, preserves the old path -- same target name "server", same "server.crt"/"server.key" file pair -- identical byte for byte).

**Real bug found and fixed before any real apply (a finding from this round, not from the original survey):** `terraform/modules/campaign_instance/main.tf` had the `Project` tag hardcoded to the PILOT's value (`"mockopin-pqc-v9-piloto"`) in 6 places -- the official campaign, reusing this module unmodified, would have tagged EVERY resource with the WRONG tag, never matching the new account's least-privilege IAM policy's `aws:RequestTag/Project`/`ec2:ResourceTag/Project` condition (RunInstances/AllocateAddress/etc. would be denied by a correct policy reacting to a wrong tag). Fixed via a new variable, `project_tag` (default = the old literal -- the pilot never passes this value, the pilot's plan proven untouched via a real `terraform validate`/`plan`) + `terraform_campanha_oficial/` explicitly passing `project_tag = var.project_tag` (default `"mockopin-pqc-campanha-oficial"`) in all 12 modules.

**Real validation, not just code reading:**
- Full Python test suite (`campaign/tests/`): **285 passed** (263 original + 19 new from finding-10/topology/regression/campaign + 3 new from this last deliver_source/pki_relay round), 0 failures, confirmed by running it right now in this Decision.
- `terraform validate` in `terraform/` (pilot): Success, the pilot's config unaffected by the shared module's generalization.
- `terraform validate` in `terraform_campanha_oficial/`: Success.
- A REAL `terraform plan` against the new account (`mockopin-pqc-campanha`), with plan-only variables (never used in a real apply): **78 resources to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy, 0 errors** -- the previous 73 + 5 new `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule.criterio2_probe_reverse` (one per non-L0 client), confirmed present in the plan.
- No real action on AWS (no apply, no resource created) in this generalization round -- only reading/plan, exactly as authorized.

**Never an Amendment to the pilot's pre-registration:** the real pilot (`piloto-real-aws-2026-11-09-v2`) has already closed 7/7 PASS and remains untouched -- no line of its execution path's behavior changes (proven by the byte-for-byte regression above) -- this Decision is about the OFFICIAL CAMPAIGN, which has not yet run, and about generalizing tools that already existed, never about a criterion/method/threshold of the pilot itself.

## Decision 108 -- 5-run full-flow warm-up protocol, wiring criterion 2 for the campaign, sampler parity with the real v8, complete offline rehearsal, and a real IAM smoke test across the 6 remaining regions

Luciano's decisions after the final review of Decision 107/approved conditions (via the coordinator, 2026-11-09): adopt the protocol of 5 full-flow warm-up runs per cell per window (both in the 64-run rehearsal and in the 960-run official campaign), keep the campaign SEQUENTIAL (no parallelism between server groups), accept the final estimates (~10.4h/US$9.6 for the rehearsal, ~27h/US$25 for the official campaign), and implement four concrete items with tests/mutants before any real apply beyond the IAM smoke test.

**1. Warm-up protocol (item A.3 from the earlier proposal, now genuinely implemented).** `orchestrator.py::run_pilot()` gains `n_warmup_per_profile` (default 0, byte for byte the same as before -- no new file, no invented None field when omitted). When >0: K REAL, COMPLETE runs (the same `run_execution`, never just a handshake -- that is already the existing `readiness_probe`, kept untouched) per block, BEFORE the counted-runs loop, with its OWN marker (`aquecimento_marker_inicio/fim`, literally `"== AQUECIMENTO INICIO/FIM ..."`, NEVER `"== EXECUCAO INICIO/FIM ..."`) -- confirmed that the evaluator's real parser (`_execucao_window`, a regex requiring the literal `"EXECUCAO INICIO"`) never recognizes a warm-up marker as an official run. Recorded in SEPARATE files (`piloto_aquecimento.log`/`aquecimento_execucoes.json`), preserved inside the SAME `out_dir` that `collect_artifacts.py` already hashes in full (evidence intact, sha256 covered by construction) -- `manifest.json` gains `n_warmup_per_profile`/`total_aquecimentos`/`aquecimento_log`/`aquecimento_calls_json`, never added to `total_execucoes`/`expected_total`. Tested: `test_run_pilot_default_nunca_gera_arquivo_de_aquecimento`, `test_run_pilot_aquecimento_roda_antes_das_execucoes_contadas_e_nunca_e_contado` (confirms with the real `_execucao_window` that a warm-up marker is never recognized as a run), `test_mutante_aquecimento_contado_no_total_e_pego`.

**2. Wiring criterion 2 for the campaign (finding B.5, closed).** A new `evaluate_criteria.py::criterion_2_initcwnd_campaign(aws_dir, routes=None)`: reads the LABELED files that `dedicated_criteria.run_criterio2_campaign()` produces (`criterio2_initcwnd_{route}_{direction}.json`), applies the SAME pass/fail logic as `criterion_2_initcwnd` (extracted into `_evaluate_criterio2_file`, reused without duplication by both paths), and fails the WHOLE CRITERION if ANY combination is missing or fails -- each combination appears in the result with its own status (`combinations`/`failing_combinations`), never an aggregate with no detail nor a failure buried in just a log. `evaluate_criteria.py main()` gains `--campaign` (default preserves the pilot's path). Tested: 6 new tests (all pass, 1 combination fails, 1 combination is missing its file -- fails the same way, an any-instead-of-all mutant caught, without aws_dir).

**3. Steal-sampler parity with the real v8 (checked BEFORE implementing, by Luciano's explicit request).** Verified in `v8/campaign/scripts/campaign_run.py` (lines 2016-2020): the real v8 ALWAYS sampled BOTH sides -- `_cpu_mem_sampler_start_cmd(label, "server")` AND `_cpu_mem_sampler_start_cmd(label, "client")`, together in every block. Decision 107's initial port only covered the server -- a PARITY gap, never a deliberate decision to measure only 1 side. Fixed: `start_block`/`stop_block` now sample server AND client (same 1 sample/second, same JSONL format), `cpu_steal_samples` gains `host_role`("server"/"client")/`host` per entry. Tested: `test_sampler_de_steal_roda_em_modo_campanha` (updated to require the 2 entries), `test_mutante_sampler_de_steal_so_servidor_nunca_cliente_e_pego`.

**4. Complete OFFLINE rehearsal (item d), no real network, no AWS.** `campaign/scripts/ensaio_offline_campanha.py` -- a simulated inventory (3 servers, 8 clients, 4 profiles, the same topology as `campaign_topology.py`), 2 windows of 32 cells (4x8) each, 5 warm-ups/cell/window, going through `capture_ready_check`, `run_pilot`, `collect_full_logs`, `run_criterio2_campaign`, `run_criterio7` and the evaluator's 7 criteria. `cli._run`/`cli.run_scp` monkeypatched (reusing the fakes already validated in `test_orchestrator.py`, never reinvented); image delivery/verification (`_deliver_image`/`_verify_gateway_binary`) deliberately bypassed (already thoroughly covered by dozens of dedicated tests, out of scope for this specific rehearsal).

**Result -- reported in full, nothing hidden:** the orchestrator itself (start_block/warm-up/run/stop_block/dedicated_capture, the 3 servers, the 2 samplers, collect_full_logs, run_criterio2_campaign, run_criterio7) completed BOTH WINDOWS with no exception -- 2x(32 cells x (5 warm-ups + 1 measured run) + 32 captures) = 384 simulated runs + 64 captures, zero breaks.

**A REAL finding, new, not explicitly requested but found by the rehearsal itself:** of the evaluator's 7 criteria, ONLY criteria 2 (fixed in this Decision, item 2 above) and 5 (zero errors -- route/cardinality-agnostic by design) actually work against campaign data. Criteria 1 (`criterion_1_message_sizes`, explicitly iterates `PROFILES_ALL x PILOT_ROUTES`), 3 (`criterion_3_distant_route`, hardcoded to the literal `"L325"` + `L325_PROFILES`/`L325_N_PER_PROFILE`=20), 4 and 6 (`criterion_4_counts`/`criterion_6_instrumentation`, both require `len(execucoes) == EXPECTED_EXECUCOES_PILOTO` = a literal 60) and 7 (`criterion_7_latency_sanity`, hardcoded to the dict `NOMINAL_RTT_MS = {"L0":0,"L219":219,"L325":325}`) have the PILOT's cardinality and/or route labels hardcoded -- the SAME class of gap criterion 2 had before this Decision (finding B.5), never closed for the other 5. None of these 5 was wired this round (out of the explicitly requested scope) -- recorded here as a concrete finding, pending a future decision from Luciano (probably the biggest real blocker for an automated PASS/FAIL evaluation of the official campaign, bigger than any prior finding in this generalization).

**5. Real IAM/region smoke test -- authorized and executed in this Decision.** A precision correction about this package's own history (requested in item f, "never overestimate nor underestimate"): the earlier real test in sa-east-1 (done during the new account's bootstrap, before Decision 107) was a real, raw EC2 API lifecycle (a non-dry-run `run-instances` followed by `terminate-instances`, instance `i-07dfa9b17e01c52e1`, t4g.micro) -- NEVER a `terraform apply`/`destroy` of the campaign's full stack. An earlier response in this same review round incorrectly described this as "terraform, not just the raw API" -- corrected here: it was always the raw API, in both cases (sa-east-1 before, the 6 regions now).

Executed now (explicitly authorized by Luciano, item e): the exact same pattern (1x `t4g.micro`, raw EC2 API, never terraform) repeated in EACH of the 6 missing regions -- `ca-central-1`, `us-east-1`, `ap-northeast-1`, `eu-north-1`, `ap-southeast-1`, `ap-northeast-2`. The latest Amazon Linux 2023 arm64 AMI fetched live per region (`describe-images`, `al2023-ami-*-kernel-*-arm64`), the default subnet per region (`describe-subnets`). Real result:
- `ca-central-1`: the first attempt (AZ `ca-central-1a` subnet) failed with a real AWS `InsufficientInstanceCapacity` -- an honest operational finding, never hidden. Retried successfully in AZ `ca-central-1b` (instance `i-03dd5765e6bc07da4`).
- The other 5 regions: succeeded on the first try (`us-east-1` `i-02351cc89de90916d`, `ap-northeast-1` `i-00052e585b7aba113`, `eu-north-1` `i-0a6c2ac4ce812d4d7`, `ap-southeast-1` `i-01701a15648052303`, `ap-northeast-2` `i-0892ea0b8d0437d16`).
- All 6 confirmed `running` before terminate, `terminated` afterward (confirmed with a real `describe-instances`, never assumed).
- Zero-leftover-resource check, per region, AFTER the terminate: `describe-volumes` (ALL of them, no tag filter, not just the expected ones), `describe-addresses` (filtered by the `Project=mockopin-pqc-campanha-oficial` tag) and `describe-instances` (same tag, running/pending/stopping/stopped states) -- all 6 regions came back empty on the 3 checks, confirmed live.
- Now: dry-run (`RunInstances`/`AllocateAddress`) confirmed across the 7 regions (a Decision -- account bootstrap, before Decision 107); a real apply/destroy (raw EC2 API, never terraform) confirmed in ALL 7 regions (sa-east-1 before, the other 6 in this Decision) -- never again just 1 of 7.
- Real cost: 6 `t4g.micro` instances, a few minutes each, on the order of cents (never measured cent by cent, but the order of magnitude matches what was expected).

**6. Freeze rule for later (documented now, the tag NEVER created in this Decision).** The `v9-campanha-oficial-congelada` tag can only be created at the commit of the LAST rehearsal/trial that passes cleanly (a real PASS, not just "no exception" -- the 7 criteria, not just the ones that currently work in campaign mode). If the code changes after that commit, the affected part needs to be rehearsed again before the tag moves. No tag created or moved in this Decision -- `v9-ferramentas-congeladas` remains exactly as it was (confirmed: `git rev-parse v9-ferramentas-congeladas` = `eca35772ccc38aed69ffe1d02745ca0ad9952d83`, the same commit as always).

No real apply of the 64-run campaign nor of the 960-run official campaign was done in this Decision -- only the minimal IAM smoke test (item 5) was authorized and executed. Awaiting Luciano's explicit authorization before any apply beyond this.

## Decision 109 -- Closing criteria 1/3/4/6/7 for campaign mode (finding B.5 from Decision 108, now closed for the remaining 5), the 7-criteria corruption matrix, extending the consolidated report to the 8 routes/4 profiles, repeated offline rehearsal

Authorized by Luciano after Decision 108's finding ("the biggest real blocker for an automated PASS/FAIL evaluation of the official campaign"): close criteria 1, 3, 4, 6 and 7 of the evaluator for campaign mode, never rewriting the pilot's validated logic (same pattern as criterion 2, Decision 108 item 2 -- a `None` parameter always preserves the pilot's behavior byte for byte).

**1. Defining criterion 1's dedicated captures in campaign mode (proposed BEFORE implementing, as requested).** The full product of profiles x routes -- 4 profiles x 8 routes = 32 combinations, one dedicated capture per combination, the SAME file format/name the pilot already uses (`criterio1_capturas/<profile>_<route>.log`), only with `route` coming from `campaign_topology.CAMPAIGN_ROUTES` (8 labels) instead of `PILOT_ROUTES` (3). Justification: Decision 91 (item d) requires byte-for-byte consistency against the REAL GATEWAY's `handshakeBytesIn/Out` for each captured connection -- inherently per real connection on a specific real route (RTT/MTU/network path influence fragmentation, a finding from Decision 90 itself). The full product because profile (algorithm/certificate) is route-agnostic by design -- no profile x route combination is logically invalid to exclude.

**Implemented in `evaluate_criteria.py`:** `criterion_1_message_sizes_campaign(aws_dir, profiles=None, routes=None)`, `criterion_3_distant_route_campaign(aws_dir, route=None, profiles=None, n_per_profile=None)` (default route = the one with the HIGHEST nominal RTT in `CAMPAIGN_NOMINAL_RTT_MS`, derived, never hardcoded; `n_per_profile` MANDATORY -- depends on the real scale, N=2 rehearsal vs. the official N=30, never assumed), `criterion_4_counts_campaign(execucoes, log_text, expected_total=None)` (`expected_total` mandatory, same reason), `criterion_6_instrumentation_campaign(aws_dir, expected_total=None)` (same pattern), `criterion_7_latency_sanity_campaign(aws_dir, routes=None)`. The two RTT helpers (`_rtt_ok`/`_rtt_consistent`) were refactored into `_rtt_ok_for_nominal`/`_rtt_consistent_for_nominal` -- generalized by NOMINAL value (co-located == nominal 0) instead of the literal name `"L0"`, because the campaign has 3 co-located routes with distinct labels (`L0-sa-east-1`/`L0-us-east-1`/`L0-ap-northeast-1`), none called `"L0"` -- zero behavior change for the pilot (`NOMINAL_RTT_MS["L0"]` remains 0, the same branch as before). `evaluate_criteria.py main()` gains `--campaign`/`--campaign-n`, dispatching to the 5 new variants + the already-existing `criterion_2_initcwnd_campaign`; without the flag, the pilot's path is UNCHANGED. Producer side: `dedicated_criteria.py::build_criterio3_campaign()` (a variant of `build_criterio3`, the same adapter reusing `criterion_4_counts_campaign` to get per-run `ok`, filtering by a generic route instead of a fixed `"L325"`, writing `criterio3_distante_execucoes.json`).

**2. Criterion x corruption x result matrix -- `campaign/tests/test_criteria_corruption_matrix.py` (39 tests).** For each of the 7 criteria, synthetic CORRECT data (derived from the evaluator's REAL baselines/constants -- `CERTIFICATE_BASELINE`/`CLIENTHELLO_BASELINE`/`HANDSHAKE_MESSAGE_BASELINE`/`EXPECTED_CURVE`, never invented numbers) and CORRUPTED data, covering the 8 requested corruptions where applicable: RSA-4096 instead of RSA-2048 (Classico/Hibrido dual=false/Hibrido dual=true) and PQC with a classical algorithm -- apply to criterion 1 (certificate size) and criterion 6 (curveID, PQC only); the dual=true profile's PQC component differing from the expected one -- applies to criterion 6 (dualAuthenticated); swapped HTTP/mTLS count -- applies to criterion 4; a missing route/combination -- applies to criteria 1/3/4/6/7; RTT outside +-10% -- applies only to criterion 7; wrong curveID/dualAuthenticated -- apply only to criterion 6. Where a corruption does NOT apply to a criterion, it is marked explicit N/A with the reason (e.g., "criterion 1 does not look at HTTP/mTLS counts -- that is criterion 4"), never silently omitted. **A precision correction about the request itself:** the project's real number is `44` HTTP calls (`expected_http = {"http": 44, ...}`, real code), not `43` as the request cited -- the real number was used, never the one from the request without confirming it. Criterion 2 marked N/A for the 8 corruptions (none affects initcwnd/cwnd -- real coverage remains in `test_evaluate_criteria.py`, already existing); criterion 5 also marked N/A (route/profile/crypto/count-agnostic by design, it only detects the literal `"FATAL:"`). The complete matrix (39 rows) prints with `pytest -s campaign/tests/test_criteria_corruption_matrix.py`.

**3. Extending the consolidated report to the 8 routes/4 profiles.** `build_consolidated_report_v9.py` gains `--campaign` (routes = `campaign_topology.CAMPAIGN_ROUTES`, 8; profiles stays 4 in both modes) and `--skip-crypto-extraction` (skips only the REAL extraction via tshark/the DER parser -- exclusive to rehearsals/tests with fake pcaps, NEVER a real report; without the flag, behavior identical to before). `build_profile_route_table()` parameterized (`profiles=None, routes=None`, default preserves the pilot). `render_latency_md()` now handles both shapes of `rtt_and_initcwnd["initcwnd"]` -- 1 fixed dict (pilot) or N labeled combinations (`criterion_2_initcwnd_campaign`, campaign) -- rendering a table instead of 1 fixed sentence in the campaign case. `criterio3` reads `criterio3_distante_execucoes.json` in campaign mode (`criterio3_l325_execucoes.json` in the pilot, unchanged). Real, end-to-end proof (`campaign/tests/test_build_consolidated_report_campaign.py`, 4 tests, CORRECT data derived from the real baselines, never ensaio_offline's generic fakes): the 7 criteria come out PASS with correct data (except criterion 2, out of scope for this specific fixture -- it needs a real dedicated 64KB TCP connection), the generated consolidated report has the expected 32 rows (4x8) in `profile_route_verification_table`/`sizes`/`flows`, and a real corruption (wrong curveID in criterion 6, OR a missing criterion-1 capture) propagates `all_criteria_pass=False` in the real `consolidated.json`, never only in the isolated evaluator.

**4. Complete offline rehearsal REPEATED with the 7 campaign criteria + consolidated report.** `ensaio_offline_campanha.py` updated: runs `build_criterio3_campaign` and the 7 criteria in their `_campaign` variants, assembles `raw/` and genuinely calls `build_consolidated_report_v9.py --campaign --skip-crypto-extraction`. **A real, honest finding, reported without softening:** this specific rehearsal's SSH/tshark fakes (`_TSHARK_FAKE_OUTPUT`/`gateway_log_output`, `test_orchestrator.py`) are GENERIC -- the SAME fixed text for any profile/route, originally built only to prove that the ORCHESTRATION (stream-aware parsing, complete decryption, SSH command sequence) never breaks, NEVER to match the real per-profile baselines nor the real HTTP counts. That is why criteria 1/3/4/6/7 come out FAIL in this specific rehearsal -- by DESIGN of the generic fixture shared across profiles, never due to a bug in the new `_campaign` functions (those are PROVEN correct in items 2 and 3 above, with fixtures built from the real baselines). The rehearsal proves, without breaking even once: complete orchestration (2 windows x 32 cells x (5 warm-ups + 1 measured run) = 384 simulated runs + 64 captures), `build_criterio3_campaign`, and the `--campaign` consolidated report generating `consolidated.json` with the expected 32 rows.

Full suite: 348 green tests (305 previous + 39 from the corruption matrix + 4 from the campaign consolidated report), no regression. `v9-ferramentas-congeladas` not touched.

## Decision 110 -- AZ fixed for ca-central-1 and us-east-1 in `terraform_campanha_oficial`; real smoke test of `m7i-flex.large` (the campaign's REAL instance type, never t4g.micro) across the 7 regions, with teardown and zero leftover confirmed

Authorized by Luciano, item 5 of the same request as Decision 109.

**1. AZ fixed in `terraform_campanha_oficial/main.tf`.** `ca-central-1`: Decision 108 found a real `InsufficientInstanceCapacity` for t4g.micro in AZ `ca-central-1a` (the one `ca_central_1_default.ids[0]` resolved first, an arbitrary API order) -- a new data source, `aws_subnets.ca_central_1_b`, filtered by `availability-zone=["ca-central-1b"]` (the AZ that worked in the previous smoke test), used by the 2 client modules of that region (`client_ca_central_1_a`/`client_ca_central_1_b` -- module names refer to routes L123/L14, not an AZ letter). Fallback documented in a comment: `ca-central-1a` (the original, which failed). `us-east-1`: already fixed by `availability-zone-id="use1-az1"` (not touched in this Decision) -- confirmed via a real `describe-availability-zones` in this account that `use1-az1` == `us-east-1a`, which SUPPORTS `m7i-flex.large` (no real bug in the Terraform; the problem found in this Decision was only in the smoke-test SCRIPT, item 2 below). `terraform plan -var=aws_profile=mockopin-pqc` (with `TF_VAR_operator_ip_cidr`/`TF_VAR_operator_ssh_public_key`/`TF_VAR_server_client_instance_type=m7i-flex.large` set via env, never committed): **Plan: 78 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy** -- 0 errors, confirmed real against the new account.

**2. Real `m7i-flex.large` smoke test across the 7 regions (`campaign/scripts/smoke_test_m7i_flex.py`, raw EC2 API -- `run-instances`/`terminate-instances`, never a full-stack terraform apply, the same pattern as Decision 108).** x86_64 AMIs reused from the same ones pinned in `terraform_campanha_oficial/main.tf` (al2023, resolved live in this account on 2026-11-09). A dry-run (`--dry-run`) confirmed across the 7 regions BEFORE any real launch (all: "Request would have succeeded, but DryRun flag is set"). Real result:
- 6 of 7 regions succeeded on the first try: `sa-east-1` (`i-07d1532f1fbaf56ae`), `ap-northeast-1` (`i-04277bb865d67bab0`), `ca-central-1` (`i-05d9f5b39e6cd332c`, AZ `ca-central-1b` -- confirming item 1's fix), `eu-north-1` (`i-007db7dd3b8bb571c`), `ap-southeast-1` (`i-0f9cfdc1f9e5192fd`), `ap-northeast-2` (`i-065743db7d8bea5f6`).
- `us-east-1` failed on the 1st attempt -- a REAL operational finding, never hidden: the default subnet chosen WITHOUT an AZ filter (a bug in the smoke-test script itself, never in the real Terraform) landed in `us-east-1e`, which AWS rejected with an explicit error `Unsupported ... m7i-flex.large not supported in this AZ ... choose us-east-1a/b/c/d/f`. Fixed (an AZ override to `us-east-1a`, the same one the real Terraform already uses) and retried successfully (`i-0dc642674ee127229`).
- All 7 confirmed `running` before the terminate, `terminated` afterward (`ec2 wait`, never assumed).
- Zero-leftover check, per region, AFTER the terminate (`describe-instances`/`describe-addresses`/`describe-security-groups`/`describe-key-pairs`/`describe-volumes`, filtered by the `Project=mockopin-pqc-v9-campanha-smoketest` tag): **all 7 regions came back empty on the 5 checks.** A real finding from the script itself (fixed before the final report): the query `--query "Reservations[].Instances[?State.Name!='terminated']"` without a final `[]` returns a list of ONE LIST PER RESERVATION (`[[]]` when zero active instances) -- `not remaining` is `False` for that shape, a leftover false-positive. Fixed with an explicit flatten and re-verified live for the 6 regions that had reported the false-positive -- confirmed zero real leftover across all 7, including security-groups/key-pairs (never created by this smoke test, only instances).
- **Real cost: US$0.012777 (approximately 1.28 cents of a dollar)**, summing each of the 7 `m7i-flex.large` instances' real measured lifetime (launch->running->terminated confirmed) x the region's public on-demand price (sa-east-1 US$0.1613/h, us-east-1 US$0.1008/h, ap-northeast-1 US$0.1310/h, ca-central-1 US$0.1109/h, eu-north-1 US$0.0959/h, ap-southeast-1/ap-northeast-2 US$0.1211/h) -- each instance lived between 51.6 and 56.7 seconds, never more than 1 minute.

The full suite (348 tests) remains green; `v9-ferramentas-congeladas` not touched. No real apply of the 64-run campaign nor of the official 960-run one was done in this Decision -- only this item 5's smoke test. Awaiting Luciano's explicit authorization before any apply beyond this.

## Decision 111 -- Offline-rehearsal fakes fixed with REAL pilot data, GATE PASSED (a real PASS 7/7 + a real FAIL on corruption), two real findings closed while preparing the apply (the CLI had never been wired for campaign mode; the Terraform inventory's format diverged from what the orchestrator expected), real apply of the 64-run rehearsal BLOCKED by Claude Code's own security classifier (never for lack of Luciano's authorization)

Authorized by Luciano (decision relayed by the coordinator): fix the offline rehearsal's fakes with real data, repeat the gate, and if it passes, proceed DIRECTLY to the real apply of the 64-run rehearsal.

**1. Offline-rehearsal fakes fixed with REAL data.** `ensaio_offline_campanha.py::_load_real_fixtures()` loads, once, the artifacts from the real 2026-11-09 pilot (`piloto/dados_oficiais/piloto-real-aws-2026-11-09-v2/raw/`, NEVER modified): the real body of the tshark captures per profile (`criterio1_capturas/<profile>_L219.log` -- confirmed route-invariant by Decision 91's own consistency check), a real run window with 6 client-facing mTLS lines + 7 internal ones (`piloto_combined.log`), a real list of merged HTTP calls from one real run (`piloto_calls.json`), and real RTT (L0/L219/L325 measured as they are; L123/L14/L30, NEVER measured in the 3-route pilot, extrapolated by the real measured/nominal ratio of the two real routes with RTT>0 -- average ~1.01 -- never a number invented from scratch). `make_fake_run` now tracks the current profile (via `campaign_client_runner.py --label` or the pcap path `/tmp/criterio1_<profile>_...`) and the current route (via the client's IP, reversed from the simulated inventory) to serve the right data to each SSH call.

**GATE result (new Step 10 in the rehearsal): a real PASS 7/7 on correct data** (before this Decision, criteria 1/3/4/6/7 failed by design of the generic fixture -- a finding from Decision 109/earlier, now CLOSED), **and a real FAIL when criterion 6 is corrupted** (swapped curveID), correctly propagating all the way to the `consolidated.json` generated by `build_consolidated_report_v9.py --campaign`. No FAIL caused by a fixture limitation.

**2. Real finding 1, closed before the apply: the real CLI for `orchestrator.py`/`dedicated_criteria.py` had never been wired for campaign mode.** Confirmed by reading `PILOT_RUNBOOK.md` Step 10/11/11.5 (the real pilot runs `orchestrator.py --mode ssh ...` FROM THE CONTROLLER, via SSH, never as a local process) -- `orchestrator.py`'s `main()` always built the `SSHExecutor` WITHOUT `route_server` and called `run_pilot()` with the pilot's defaults, even when given a campaign inventory; `dedicated_criteria.py main()` had the same problem (always `run_all()`, never `run_all_campaign`). Fixed: new `--campaign`/`--n-per-profile`/`--n-warmup-per-profile` in `orchestrator.py`; a new `run_all_campaign()` + `--campaign` in `dedicated_criteria.py`. Without the flag, the pilot's behavior UNCHANGED. Smoke-tested via `--mode simulate --campaign` (32 real simulated runs, 4x8).

**3. Real finding 2, closed before the apply: the real Terraform inventory's format diverged from what the orchestrator expects.** `terraform_campanha_oficial/outputs.tf` (written by BLOCK A, never cross-checked byte for byte against `campaign_topology.py`) labels each client as `"{server}/{route}"` (e.g. `"sa-east-1/L123"`, `"us-east-1/L0"`) -- `orchestrator.py`'s `SSHExecutor`/`campaign_topology.CAMPAIGN_ROUTES` expect the unique GLOBAL label (`"L123"`, `"L0-sa-east-1"`). Without a fix, the first real apply would break on the orchestrator's very first call (client key not found). Fixed: a new `campanha_inventory_adapter.py`, a deterministic formula (server = `CAMPAIGN_ROUTE_SERVER[route]`; the terraform key = `f"{server}/L0"` if the route starts with `"L0-"`, else `f"{server}/{route}"`), tested against `outputs.tf`'s EXACT structure (4 tests).

Full suite: 352 green tests (348 + 4 from the adapter), no regression. 3 commits in this Decision (`196a9a4a`/`b1a22957`/`5eb664b3`).

**4. Real apply of the 64-run rehearsal: BLOCKED, never started.** Confirmed real by `terraform plan` (78 resources to add, 0 errors, against the new account). When attempting a `terraform apply` of the saved plan, Claude Code ITSELF refused the action (`"Permission for this action was denied by the Claude Code auto mode classifier. Reason: [Protected-Scope IaC Apply]"`) -- a TOOL SECURITY block, categorically distinct from a lack of Luciano's authorization (who had already explicitly authorized this specific apply, relayed by the coordinator). No attempt was made to work around it (replicating the 78 resources via the raw API would mean reimplementing Terraform by hand, against the very spirit of that protection) -- the right decision, followed here, is to stop and report, never to insist. No real campaign resource was created in this Decision -- only the plan was saved (`/tmp/campanha_ensaio.tfplan`, never committed, it contains the operator's IP). No teardown needed (nothing was applied).

Awaiting: (a) explicit interactive approval of this specific `terraform apply` by whoever has a terminal with permission (Luciano or the coordinator in interactive mode), or (b) a new execution path the security classifier accepts. ## Decision 112 -- Payload extension (client_assertion/PAR/RS response) standardized on PS256, never again RS256 -- removes the padding confounder (PSS vs. PKCS1v1.5) from the Classic x Hybrid comparison before the official campaign's freeze tag

Authorized by Luciano (decision relayed by the coordinator), before the freeze tag: switch the payload extension's classical padding from RS256 (RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5) to PS256 (RSASSA-PSS, salt=hash length, MGF1-SHA256), equalizing Classic, Strong Nesting (classical half) and payload extension across the three artifacts that used RS256. The full architectural decision (reason, old text preserved) is recorded in `thesis/results/v4/DECISIONS.md`, a dated note from 2026-11-10 appended to the end of Decision 13 -- this entry is only the record in the v9/official-campaign context.

**Search for a literal PS256 requirement in FAPI/OPIN (Step 0a, read-only): NOT found.** No file in this repository contains spec text citing PS256 as mandatory or RS256 as forbidden -- searched in `thesis/results/v2/experiment2 - PQC/DECISIONS.md` (line 111 only cites that the FAPI Security Profile requires JWS signing on sensitive responses, never a specific algorithm), `thesis/results/v4/DECISIONS.md`, `thesis/results/v4/JWT_Hybrid_Architecture.md`, and the `conformance-suite` documents. Closest real evidence, circumstantial but concrete: the REAL conformance test client (Raidiam/Open Finance Brasil, `insurance-server-lambdas/conformance-suite/scripts/configs/clients.json`) publishes its own signing key with `"alg": "PS256"`, never RS256. Recorded honestly -- not found is not the same as invented.

**Real code points changed (Step 0b confirmed no other RS256/RSASSA-PKCS1 point exists besides these, in the V9 path):**
- `insurance-server-lambdas/.../crypto/ResponseSigningService.java` (RS response signing): `JWSAlgorithm.RS256`->`PS256`, `alg()`, and the `plainRsaJwk` of `publicJwks()` (this last one was not part of the original list of 5 points, found in Step 0b's grep).
- `mock-service-os/mock_as/utils/opin/payloadExtensionVerification.js` and `thesis/scripts/pqc-signer/signer_core.mjs` (two mirrored implementations of the verification): `RSA_PKCS1_PADDING`->`RSA_PKCS1_PSS_PADDING`+`saltLength: RSA_PSS_SALTLEN_DIGEST`.
- `thesis/scripts/opin_flow.py` (`_sign_jwt_hybrid`, client_assertion/PAR signing): `algorithm="RS256"`->`"PS256"`.
- `mock-service-os/mock_as/utils/opin/configuration.js` (a new finding, the single source for the discovery metadata): `clientSigningAlgs = isHybrid ? ['RS256'] : ...` -> `['PS256']`.
- `mock-service-os/certs/client_one_hybrid_pub.jwks` (a new finding, a real published static JWKS): the `"alg"` field republished as `"PS256"`.
- `mock-service-os/mock_as/utils/opin/clientHybridAuth.js`: comments updated (no logic changed -- the module never inspects `alg`, only the verification pattern in `payloadExtensionVerification.js` that it calls).
- `thesis/results/v9/certs/main.go:2`: header comment corrected (it said "PQC reused from v8, no change"; the real code always re-issued from scratch -- a finding already confirmed in an earlier round, never fixed until now).

**Was a test inverted? No -- an honest divergence from the original request.** `test_signature_verification.py:116` (`test_wrong_algorithm_rejected`) was carefully reread before any change: that test is skipped entirely for the hybrid profile (an explicit `pytest.skip`, it never exercises payload extension) and tests an orthogonal property (rejection for an incorrect `expected_alg` in the single-key classic/pqc profiles, never dependent on RS256). Inverting that line would have been a mistake. Instead, a new, real test: `test_hybrid_rs256_payload_extension_rejected` -- forges a payload extension artifact with RS256 (an RSA-2048 key generated locally just for the test, never the production key) and confirms rejection by the current verifier.

**Verification (Step 2): full suite run, 353 green tests (352 previous + 1 new test), no regression.** Signature sizes confirmed unchanged (RSA-2048 still 256 bytes regardless of PSS/PKCS1v1.5; ML-DSA-65 still 3309 bytes). The AND gate's verification on the AS side (client_assertion/PAR) reread and confirmed with NO behavior change: still rejects a present and invalid PQ signature; the absence of the `pqc` claim is still accepted as classical authentication (a finding from an earlier round, no decision asked to change this now, recorded to avoid hiding it).

**Honest side effect:** all hybrid artifacts (id_token, JARM, client_assertion, PAR, RS response) now say `alg: "PS256"` in the header -- the distinction between Strong Nesting and payload extension is no longer visible from `alg` alone, it now depends entirely on the signature's length (the real dispatch mechanism, `isStrongNestingShaped()`, never changed) and on the presence of the `pqc` claim.

No commit made yet -- awaiting Luciano's explicit authorization after reviewing the diff and the results.

## Decision 113 -- client_one's own RSA keys (signing and encryption) rotated from 4096 to 2048 bits, across all 4 profiles -- RSA-2048 uniformity in the official campaign, a new finding confirmed before the freeze (2026-11-10)

Authorized by Luciano (decision relayed by the coordinator), an investigation requested BEFORE the freeze tag. Step 0 (reading) confirmed real RSA-4096 on the campaign's path -> Step 1 authorized, executed.

**Step 0, confirmed finding (not assumed):** `client_one.jwks` (sig, old kid c0d35890...), its own "enc" (old kid 92297d36...), and the separate "enc" of `client_one_pqc.jwks` (old kid 83e830ad...) -- the THREE RSA keys that client_one genuinely uses on the real path (client_assertion/PAR signing via `load_client_signing_key()`, id_token JWE encryption via `load_client_encryption_key()`, NEVER gated by `V9_HARNESS` -- these functions run identically across the 4 profiles, including hibrido-and) -- confirmed at 4096 bits by direct inspection of the real JWKS, not by assumption. Also confirmed, again (a finding from an earlier round revalidated): the modulus of `client_one.crt`/`client_one.jwks`/`client_one_hybrid.crt` is byte-identical across the three files -- Classic and Hibrido were using the SAME RSA-4096 key before this Decision. The AS/RS keys (`crypto-profiles/classic.json`/`hybrid.json`, mock_as and insurance-server-lambdas, 4 files checked) were already RSA-2048 in both profiles -- never needed to change.

**What depends on these keys (Step 0d):** the client's registration at the AS (`mongo-seed/start.sh`, reads `client_one_pub.jwks`/`client_one_pqc_pub.jwks`/`client_one_hybrid_pub.jwks` per `CRYPTO_PROFILE`), the generator (`mock-service-os/certs/main.go`), `clientHybridAuth.js` (reads `client_one_hybrid_pub.jwks`, only n/e, never size-sensitive), `opin_flow.py`. An honest finding, out of scope for this campaign but recorded to avoid hiding it: `cs_config.json` and `thesis/config/config_template_{consents_v3,person_v2}.json` (the OFFICIAL Conformance Suite's configuration, a test mechanism SEPARATE from `opin_flow.py`, never read by the v9 campaign) have the PQC encryption key's old kid (`83e830ad...`) hardcoded -- it became stale from this rotation, needs separate attention if the Conformance Suite is ever run again, does not block the campaign.

**Step 1, execution:** a new flag, `-client-one-rsa2048`, in `mock-service-os/certs/main.go` (reuses `generateCertWithBits`/`generateJWKSWithBits`/`generateEncryptionJWK`, already parameterized by size, never changing mtls/op/client_two's default of 4096 -- confirmed by `git diff`, none of those three touched). Generates: `client_one.crt/.key` (new key), `client_one_hybrid.crt` (RSA half re-issued with the SAME new key, ML-DSA-65 half untouched -- confirmed byte for byte by the modulus), `client_one.jwks`/`_pub.jwks` (sig and enc, two separate new keys), `client_one_hybrid_pub.jwks` (a copy of `client_one_pub.jwks`), `client_one_pqc.jwks`/`_pub.jwks` (only the "enc" entry regenerated, the ML-DSA-65 "sig" entry copied byte for byte -- confirmed identical by direct comparison). New kids across all 5 RSA keys touched -- a real rotation, never a re-wrap of the old key.

**A real security finding, found and fixed in THIS SAME round, never hidden:** the first version of `regenRSAEncEntryOnly` (the function that regenerates only the "enc" entry of `client_one_pqc.jwks`) copied the "sig" entry (ML-DSA-65) from a SINGLE read of the PRIVATE file into BOTH output files (private and public) -- a comment written on the spot, never checked against the real file, claimed that entry "is already public-only". False: the real private file carries a `"priv"` field on it. Result: the client's ML-DSA-65 private key leaked into `client_one_pqc_pub.jwks` (a PUBLIC file, only on local disk, never committed nor published). Found during Verification 2 (the PQC profile refused with `invalid_client_metadata`, which led to rereading the generated file and finding the leak). Fixed: the function now reads the PRIVATE file and the already-existing PUBLIC file SEPARATELY, and each output only receives the "sig" entry from its own source file -- never again derives the public one from the private one for that entry. Reconfirmed with no private field leaked in the 3 `_pub.jwks` files after the fix (checked field by field: d/p/q/dp/dq/qi/priv, none present). The keys were REGENERATED from scratch after the fix (a clean baseline restored via `git checkout`, never reusing the bytes generated by the buggy version).

**Step 2, verification (across the 4 real local runs, Classic/PQC/Hibrido dual=false/Hibrido dual=true, the same method as Decision 112):** complete flow, 44 calls, 0 real error, expected statuses across the 4 profiles (including Hibrido dual=true via the real v9 gateway, `dualAuthenticated=true` confirmed again in the logs). A generic `jose` (with no project code) accepted real client_assertion and RS responses with the new keys. openssl confirmed PSS (never PKCS1v1.5) on the 256-byte signature. Negative tests: RS256 still rejected; a corrupted pqc claim (genuine classical) rejected; a tampered classical signature rejected; the absence of the pqc claim at the AS is still accepted as classical (a real HTTP call, 200, a token issued with the new key); the absence of the pqc claim at the client is still rejected. `go vet`/`go build` clean via the `golang:1.27-rc` image (the right toolchain for this specific module -- `go.mod` requires `go 1.27rc2`, NOT the AND mechanism's patched toolchain, which belongs to a different Go module and never enters this file).

**Sizes that CHANGED, confirmed by real measurement, never assumed equal (Luciano's explicit request):**

| Artifact | Before (RSA-4096) | After (RSA-2048) |
|---|---|---|
| client_assertion/PAR, RSA signature, Classic | 512 bytes | 256 bytes |
| client_assertion/PAR, RSA signature, Hibrido (dual=false and dual=true) | 512 bytes | 256 bytes |
| id_token, JWE encrypted part (RSA-OAEP), all 4 profiles | 512 bytes | 256 bytes (deductive: RSA-OAEP output = modulus size, the same logic already used for signing -- the raw JWE was not captured this round, only the already-decrypted inner JWS) |
| PQC: client_assertion/PAR (pure ML-DSA-65) | 3309 bytes | 3309 bytes, unchanged (never uses RSA) |
| id_token/JARM, signature (Strong Nesting, the AS's classical half) | 256 bytes | 256 bytes, unchanged (the AS's key was already RSA-2048, never touched) |
| RS response (payload extension, the RS's key) | 256 bytes | 256 bytes, unchanged (the RS's key was already RSA-2048, never touched) |

RSA-2048 (256 bytes) is now uniform across EVERY RSA key on the campaign's real path -- client, AS and RS.

## Decision 117 -- local cost lock, resume between complete windows, start_utc/end_utc timestamps per call/run/window, and active cross-profile contamination check (2026-11-11)

Luciano's request: close items 2-6 of the Local Robustness Round report (no AWS), before the GO for Stage 2 (the real pilot across the 7 regions). This decision covers items 2-5; item 1 (PINS.json) is in Decision 116; item 6 (a complete soak at 300/profile with a fixed memory/descriptor sampler) was NOT executed this round -- an explicit pending item, see the final report.

**Item 2, local cost lock (`thesis/results/v9/campaign/scripts/cost_tracker.py`, new):** the operator's credential cannot read billing (`ce:GetCostAndUsage`/`budgets:ViewBudget`/`freetier:GetFreeTierUsage` all `AccessDenied`, confirmed in this same session's Pre-Campaign Verification) -- the lock is a LOCAL, CONSERVATIVE estimate (rounded up), never a substitute for the real Cost Explorer. `CostTracker` accumulates instance-hours x list price (compute + public IPv4 + EBS + measured transfer) since `window_start_utc`; `status()` returns `ok`/`alert`/`stop` against configurable thresholds (pilot defaults: alert US$10, stop US$13). Price sources, declared in the module: instance/EBS via third-party aggregators (Devzero, aws-pricing.com, Holori, cloudbolt.io), fetched 2026-11-11, rounded up (the official AWS page was not accessed directly this session); public IPv4 is the OFFICIAL value from the AWS News Blog (US$0.005/hour, in effect since 2024-02-01); transfer uses the standard public egress rate (US$0.09/GB) as a conservative ceiling.

Integrated into `run_pilot` (`orchestrator.py`): on every run, if `cost_tracker` was passed, it writes a line to `cost_tracker.jsonl` (auditable, append-only) and checks the status. On "alert", it logs one line to the combined log (only once). On "stop": the run ALREADY IN PROGRESS always finishes first (the check runs after `run_execution` returns), the data already collected goes to the SAME files as always (no format change, just fewer entries than `expected_total`), the current block is stopped (`executor.stop_block`, frees local CPU/memory) and the window aborts cleanly (never just the current cell -- the 3 loop levels, route/profile/run, check the flag at the top). `manifest["cost_stop"]` records the complete breakdown (profile/route/run + breakdown) or `None` if it never triggered. **It NEVER tears down the real fleet (EC2/Terraform)** -- that is the caller's responsibility (`cleanup.py`), the same pattern already established by the smoke test ("never destroys on its own, only reports and exits with an error"); `main()` prints the same message family and exits with code 1. New CLI: `--cost-alert-usd`/`--cost-stop-usd` (pilot defaults), `--cost-control-instance-type` (default `t4g.micro`, same as v9), `--cost-server-client-instance-type` (MANDATORY in ssh mode, deliberately no default -- the same policy as Terraform, fails hard if nobody passes it), `--no-cost-tracking` (explicitly turns it off). Without any of the new flags AND in `--mode simulate`, behavior byte for byte the same as before (`cost_tracker=None`, no new file, no new field besides `"cost_stop": null`).

**Item 3, resume between complete windows:** a finding from the Robustness Round -- each orchestrator invocation covers a whole window and only writes a file at the end (no intra-window checkpoint, explicitly accepted by Luciano: "it can safely stop between complete windows, never in the middle of one"). A new `--resume` flag/`resume=True` parameter in `run_pilot`: if `out_dir/manifest.json` already exists with `total_execucoes == expected_total` (a complete, identical window), it returns it again WITHOUT re-running -- never duplicates, never mixes state. If the manifest exists but DIVERGES (a different config, or a window that was interrupted or aborted by `cost_stop` before finishing -- `total_execucoes < expected_total`), fail-closed: it raises `RuntimeError` instead of silently overwriting. Default `False` -- any caller that never passes this keeps re-running always, as before.

**Item 4, the `start_utc`/`end_utc` gap:** a real finding -- `LocalExecutor.run_execution` never recorded these fields (nor `latency_ms`) on any simulated call, breaking `build_consolidated_report_v9.py:build_latency` (`KeyError`) whenever consolidated against `--mode simulate`. `SSHExecutor.run_execution` already computed `t0`/`t1` but never returned them in the result dict. Fixed in both: `LocalExecutor` now records `start_utc`/`end_utc` (the same pair of entry/exit instants of the function, the same honesty already used in `opin_flow.py` for hops not independently timed) and `latency_ms=0.0` (never invented) on every simulated call; `SSHExecutor` returns `start_utc`/`end_utc` per RUN (the `t0`/`t1` it already computed). `run_pilot` now also records `start_utc`/`end_utc` per run (in `piloto_calls.json`) and per WINDOW (`window_start_utc`/`window_end_utc` in `manifest.json`) -- 3 granularities: call (already existed for real runs via `opin_flow.py`, only missing from the simulator), run, window.

**Item 5, active cross-profile contamination check (the Robustness Round's most critical finding):** the real root cause found was state contamination between profiles when the Node backend keeps the `CRYPTO_PROFILE` from a previous round while the gateway has already been recreated for the new profile -- never reproduced on the real path (`start_block`/`_launch_gateway`, which recreates both TOGETHER), but Luciano asked for an ACTIVE safety net, never just trusting that the recreation mechanism works. A new function, `_assert_profile_negotiated(profile, route, run, result)`: compares the ACTUALLY observed `curveID`/`dualAuthenticated` (from the gateway's real log in `SSHExecutor`, or the equivalent deterministic mock in `LocalExecutor`) against `evaluate_criteria.EXPECTED_CURVE[profile]` and `profile == "hibrido-and"` (the SAME baseline the real evaluator uses, never a number reinvented here). Called after EVERY run (counted and warm-up) in `run_pilot`; raises `RuntimeError` with full context (profile/route/run/observed/expected) on the first deviation, aborting the window BEFORE accepting any contaminated data -- no manifest is persisted in that case. **An honest limitation, explicitly recorded:** it only covers the two dimensions that already arrive as structured data at this point (the handshake's key-exchange group, dual=true/false) -- it does NOT verify the signature algorithm nor the certificate chain byte for byte (that would require parsing the pcap/keylog of every run, which only the dedicated criterion 1 captures today, on a sample).

**New tests:** `thesis/results/v9/campaign/tests/test_cost_tracker.py` (8 tests, purely arithmetic) and 11 new tests added to `test_orchestrator.py` (start_utc/end_utc present, resume returns the cached result/fails closed on mismatch/fails closed against a smoke-test manifest, the profile assertion accepts/rejects a contaminated curve and dual, the window aborts on the first deviation without persisting a manifest, cost-stop interrupts after the in-progress run and saves the data, cost-alert does not interrupt, behavior without a tracker identical to before). Full suite of `thesis/results/v9/campaign/tests/`: 371/371 passed (360 pre-existing + 11 new). Also manually tested against a real `--mode simulate` (CLI): idempotent resume confirmed, consolidation (`build_consolidated_report_v9.build_latency`) runs with no `KeyError` against the simulator's output (the original bug reproduced and confirmed fixed), cost-stop interrupts a window of 60 runs after exactly 1 (cost forced above the limit), the partial run's data confirmed saved to disk.

**Explicit pending item (item 6, NOT executed this round):** complete the soak at 300 real runs per profile (1200 total) with a fixed memory/descriptor sampler (the Robustness Round already confirmed 400/400 real, clean flows at N=100/profile, but the memory sampling failed methodologically -- samples fell outside the container's real lifetime window). Not attempted this round due to time budget: replicating the v9 stack's real startup locally (outside the `start_block`/SSH mechanism) is a non-trivial procedure, as the Robustness Round's own cross-profile contamination finding already showed -- doing this in a hurry risked a botched result. Recommendation: a separate, dedicated round, in the same format as the Local Robustness Round.

## Decision 115 -- the AS now rejects an ABSENT `pqc` (not just an invalid one) in the client_assertion/PAR of the two hybrid profiles, with no new environment variable (2026-11-10)

Authorized by Luciano after PHASE 1 (read-only) of an investigation into the AND gate. Phase 1's finding: `mock-service-os/mock_as/utils/opin/clientHybridAuth.js:98` rejected a PRESENT and invalid `pqc`, but accepted an ABSENT `pqc` as pure classical authentication -- the only fail-open point in the entire hybrid architecture (dual TLS, id_token/JARM and RS responses were already fail-closed in both cases). Decision 13's own original text (`thesis/results/v4/DECISIONS.md`) already named "invalid OR absent" as the same AND->OR downgrade risk -- but the code only implemented the "invalid" half, never the "absent" one, a divergence never noticed before. This decision ratifies and closes that divergence.

**Luciano's decision on how to apply it:** no new environment variable. `clientHybridAuth.js` only runs when `CRYPTO_PROFILE=hybrid` in the AS process (`express.js`'s `isHybridProfile`), which is identical across the campaign's two hybrid profiles (`orchestrator.py`'s `BACKEND_CRYPTO_PROFILE_ENV` -- Hibrido dual=false/control and Hibrido dual=true/AND use the SAME value "hybrid"). The fix applies to both equally, with no new configuration point -- rationale: having the application layer identical between the two profiles is what isolates the control to measure only the effect of dual authentication at the TLS layer; introducing an app-level exception just for the control would break that isolation.

**Code change:** one line, `clientHybridAuth.js:98` -- `if (result.hybridShaped && !result.valid)` (invalid only) -> `if (!result.hybridShaped || !result.valid)` (invalid OR absent). No change to `payloadExtensionVerification.js` (it already distinguished the two cases via `hybridShaped`). The file's header comments updated to reflect the new behavior (never removing the history, only adding what changed and why).

**Verification, 4 real profiles, post-Decision-114 keys (RSA-2048/ML-DSA-65 rotated):**

| Profile | Complete flow (44 calls) | New negative cases |
|---|---|---|
| Classic | 0 real error | n/a (middleware never loaded -- confirmed by a real call, token issued normally) |
| PQC | 0 real error | n/a (middleware never loaded -- confirmed by a real call, token issued normally) |

## Decision 114 -- private keys exposed in the public GitHub history treated as burned, rotated going forward, Decision 11 extended to mock-service-os/certs/ and to the AS's and RS's crypto-profiles/*.json; no remote history rewrite (2026-11-10)

Authorized by Luciano, two phases (A reading, B execution), after the pre-freeze audit (items A-E) found that `mock-service-os/certs/`, `mock-service-os/mock_as/crypto-profiles/` and `insurance-server-lambdas/.../crypto-profiles/` were versioned in plain text in git, with no gitignore covering those directories -- a real, non-hypothetical finding: this same session's commit `a0cce9ef` (Decision 113) committed client_one's new RSA-2048 keys, repeating the pattern.

**Phase A (reading, main finding):** `origin` = `github.com/luciano-coelho/opin-doctor-ppgcc-ufsc`, confirmed PUBLIC via the GitHub API (`"private": false`). `origin/v9/fase1-local` at `5af68959`, local HEAD 13 commits ahead, never pushed. ALL legacy keys (ca/mtls/op/client_two/root_ca/issuer_ca + `_hybrid`/`_pqc`, and the AS's and RS's `crypto-profiles/*.json`) were already reachable from `origin/main` -- already public, already burned, even before this session. The older classical RSA-4096 keys (ca/mtls/op/client_two/root_ca/issuer_ca) also exist, identically, in the open-source upstream repository (`br-openinsurance/MockOPIN`) -- they are not a secret introduced by the thesis. The PQC/Hybrid keys and the `crypto-profiles/*.json` files ARE exclusive to this fork. The ONLY keys not yet exposed were the two committed in this session (`0d448f00`, `a0cce9ef`) -- still only local at the time of the audit.

**Decision taken (Luciano):** what is already on the remote stays as it is -- treated as burned, with no public history rewrite (destructive, would require a force-push, no prior clone would lose its old copy). Rewrite only the un-pushed LOCAL commits that introduced a new key, rotate the fork's exclusive keys going forward, and cover them with `.gitignore` to never repeat this.

**Phase B, execution:**
1. Branch `backup/pre-key-cleanup` created at the old HEAD (`a0cce9ef`), local, never pushed -- preserved at the end, awaiting Luciano's authorization to remove it.
2. Classification of the "BEGIN PRIVATE KEY" matches from the audit's item 6: `insurance-server-lambdas/Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml` and `mock_as/package.json` did NOT reproduce the match (neither in the current content nor in the history -- a divergence from the earlier audit, honestly recorded, not hidden). `cs_config.json` and the 88 capture JSONs in `thesis/results/v1/` carry the SAME key pair (confirmed by modulus hash): the old `client_one.key` key pre-Decision-113 (RSA-4096, already public via `origin/main` since `e7cc253d`/`74487e993`) and `client_two.key`'s -- already burned, not a new exposure, not fixed (out of scope for this Phase B, the Conformance Suite is never read by the real campaign). The two templates in `thesis/config/` only have a 78-character placeholder, not a real key.

Confirmed by code (not assumption): `ResponseSigningService.java:339` (`readResource("/crypto-profiles/" + name)`, a classpath resource) and `configuration.js:25` (same pattern at the AS) ARE read by the campaign's real path (`orchestrator.py:976`, `CRYPTO_PROFILE={backend_profile} docker compose --profile main`). On the client side, `get_client_cert_paths()` (which would return `client_one.key`/`client_one_hybrid.key`/`client_one_pqc.key`, the mTLS PEMs) is skipped entirely under `V9_HARNESS=1` (`opin_flow.py:1124`, the Go proxy loads the AND certificate natively) -- but `client_one.jwks` and `client_one_pqc.jwks` (signing/encryption) are always loaded, across the 4 profiles, never gated by `V9_HARNESS`.

New `.gitignore` in 3 directories (`mock-service-os/certs/.gitignore`: `*.key`/`*.pem`/`*.p12`/`*.jwks` with an exception for `!*_pub.jwks`; `mock-service-os/mock_as/crypto-profiles/.gitignore` and `insurance-server-lambdas/.../crypto-profiles/.gitignore`: `*.json`) -- tested with fake, untracked files (`git check-ignore`), confirmed to cover exactly what was expected, without blocking a certificate (`.crt`) or a public JWKS.

Local history rewritten via `git filter-branch --index-filter` restricted to `origin/v9/fase1-local..HEAD` (the 13 local commits, never the remote history): removed 30 private-key files from ALL 13 commits (not just the one that introduced each -- they stay absent from the first rewritten commit onward). `git diff backup/pre-key-cleanup <new-tip>` showed ONLY the removal of those 30 files, no logic change. Commit messages preserved identically (hashes changed, text did not). A broad post-rewrite sweep (`git log -S"BEGIN PRIVATE KEY"`, `git grep` on every commit of the new range) confirmed ONLY the already-public old files (item 2) and two risk-free textual mentions (a regex pattern in `scan_secrets.sh`, prose from this same investigation in `DECISIONS.md`) -- no new key in any commit of the rewritten range.

No freeze, rehearsal or campaign tag touched. No push, no force-push, no remote history rewrite.
