## Decision 119 -- all 4 profiles pinned to exact TLS 1.3 (MinVersion=MaxVersion), with active enforcement in the gateway and a per-run assertion in the orchestrator (2026-11-11)

An addendum to Stage 1, from a finding in the Independent EQD Verification (a separate fork, ran in an isolated worktree, never touched the main repository): the Classico profile was the ONLY one of the 4 profiles with `MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS12` in `integration/gateway/main.go`/`integration/proxy/main.go` (`buildServerTLSConfig`/`buildClientTLSConfig`) -- the other 3 profiles were already `Min=Max=VersionTLS13`. The channel genuinely ALLOWED negotiating TLS 1.2 in that profile, contradicting the premise that "the channel is TLS 1.3" with no exception.

**Fixed in 3 layers, none of them relying solely on the others:**
1. Classico profile's `MinVersion` fixed to `tls.VersionTLS13` (gateway and proxy) -- all 4 profiles are now `Min=Max=VersionTLS13`, confirmed by reading the code of each of the 4 `case`s in `buildServerTLSConfig`/`buildClientTLSConfig`, never assumed.
2. New ACTIVE enforcement in `integration/gateway/business_server.go` (`acceptBusinessConn`): the same pattern already used for `curve`/`dualAuthenticated` (a post-handshake check, a FATAL `log.Printf` + closes the connection if `cs.Version != tls.VersionTLS13`) -- "should never trigger" (given layer 1's pin) is not "cannot trigger". A `version=%q` field (using `tls.VersionName`, whose result contains a space -- hence `%q`, not `%s`) added to the `connection OK` log line, alongside `curve=`/`dualAuthenticated=`.
3. `_assert_profile_negotiated` (Decision 117, `orchestrator.py`) extended with a third dimension: `tlsVersion`, extracted from the same real gateway log (`SSHExecutor`) or the deterministic mock (`LocalExecutor`, which now returns an honest `EXPECTED_TLS_VERSION`, reflecting the real pin) -- `None`/a mismatch is treated as a deviation, never silently accepted just because curve/dual matched (also covers the case of a gateway predating this addendum, without the new log field).

**Real verification, not just code reading:** a Docker build of the `gateway`/`proxy` images with the fix, confirmed compiling (`mockopin-v9-toolchain`). Live functional test: a real gateway (`HTTP_MODE=business`, `classico` profile) + real mTLS with the generated certs -- a forced TLS 1.3 connection (`openssl s_client -tls1_3`) accepted, the log shows `version="TLS 1.3"`, no FATAL; a forced TLS 1.2 connection (`openssl s_client -tls1_2`) rejected AT THE PROTOCOL LEVEL ITSELF (`SSL alert number 70, protocol_version`), never reaching a completed handshake -- confirms that "TLS 1.2 should not be negotiable" for real, not just in theory. Full Python suite (`thesis/results/v9/campaign/tests/`): 373/373 passed (371 pre-existing + 2 new tests: `test_assert_profile_negotiated_rejeita_versao_tls_contaminada`, `test_assert_profile_negotiada_rejeita_versao_tls_ausente`; the 2 pre-existing curve/dual negative tests did not need to change, they already rejected for another reason; the correct-case acceptance test was updated to include `tlsVersion`).

No private key touched. No push, no tag.

## Decision 120 -- clarifies Decision 39's ("SAN-less") scope: it refers only to the Go patch's test fixtures, never to the campaign's real certificates; the real identity mode confirmed uniform (SAN) across the 4 profiles and both sides of mTLS (2026-11-11)

An addendum to Stage 1, item 4 (from another finding in the Independent EQD Verification): the CLIENT certificates generated by the campaign's REAL generator (`thesis/results/v9/certs/main.go`, via `make certs`) have a SAN -- `CLIENT_DNS ?= opin-client-one` in the `Makefile`, never overridden in the real invocation (confirmed by searching `DECISIONS.md`/`PILOT_READINESS.md`/`RELATORIO_SESSAO.md`: the real campaign only overrides `SERVER_IPS`/`SERVER_DNS`, never `CLIENT_DNS`). This seemed to contradict Decision 39 ("this project's CLIENT certificates are, by its own convention, deliberately SAN-less").

**Not a contradiction -- they are two different materials, never confused in the code, only in the verbal characterization across sessions:**
- Decision 39 talks about the test fixtures EMBEDDED in `and.patch` itself (`toolchain/patches/and.patch`, function `pki.classicalLeaf("and-client", ...)`/`pki.pqLeaf("and-client", ...)`) -- synthetic certificates, generated in memory just to exercise `sameDualIdentity` inside the `go test crypto/tls` suite, never used by the real gateway/proxy.
- The real generator (`thesis/results/v9/certs/main.go`) and the certificates it produces (`certs/generated/*.crt`, the same ones packaged into the gateway/proxy Docker images) are ENTIRELY SEPARATE -- they always had a SAN, were never "SAN-less" by design.

**Real identity mode, now confirmed with `openssl x509 -ext subjectAltName` on ALL generated leaves (`certs/generated/`):** the 5 CLIENT certificates (classico, pqc, hibrido-v8, hibrido-and-rsa, hibrido-and-mldsa) have the SAME SAN (`DNS:opin-client-one`); the 5 SERVER certificates have the SAME SAN (`DNS:mtls,auth.local,...` + IPs). Within the dual pair (hibrido-and), the two chains (RSA and ML-DSA-65) of the same participant carry an IDENTICAL SAN -- `sameDualIdentity` always falls into the SAN-comparison branch, never the `CommonName` fallback, in none of the 4 profiles, in either direction of mTLS. The identity mode is already uniform, no code change needed.

**Explicit pending item, not executed this round:** "recording the identity mode in the per-run check" (Luciano's request) would require logging, per real connection, which branch `sameDualIdentity` took (SAN vs CommonName) -- today that decision happens inside the patched Go (`dual.go`) and is not exposed in any log nor in the gateway's JSON body. Implementing this would touch `and.patch` (not just `gateway/proxy`), requiring rebuilding the patched toolchain from scratch and rerunning the complete `go test crypto/tls` suite (last time, 153s) -- a heavier, riskier change than the rest of this addendum. Since the identity mode is already deterministic and uniform (SAN always present and identical, confirmed above for the 4 profiles), the risk of a silent runtime divergence is low, but not zero (e.g., a future generator bug that omitted the SAN from a single leaf). Luciano decides whether it is worth the cost of patching `and.patch` for this before the freeze, or whether the static confirmation above (reproducible on every `make certs`) is sufficient.

No code change in this decision -- only investigation and scope clarification.

## Decision 121 -- a complete soak at 300/profile with continuous memory/descriptor sampling (closes Decision 117's item-6 pending item), `mockapi` investigation (no code change), pre-campaign manifest, and an OPIN size analysis in two variants (2026-11-11)

Continuation of Stage 1. Four items requested by Luciano; no private key in any new file.

**1. Complete soak (closes Decision 117's item 6):** the earlier local robustness round had only run 100/300 flows per profile, with a real methodological gap in memory/descriptor sampling (the automatic `docker stats` samples would fall outside the proxy container's lifetime window, which only exists within each profile's Python loop). Fixed with a new driver (outside version control, in scratch -- the same pattern already used in the earlier round): it samples `docker stats`/`ls /proc/1/fd` CONTINUOUSLY (every 2s) on a separate thread, running through that profile's backend+gateway's entire real lifetime window, never at isolated points before/after. Backend and gateway recreated TOGETHER per profile (the same real `_launch_gateway`/`start_block` command, `orchestrator.py` -- `docker compose --force-recreate auth mongo_seed mockapi` + `docker run` of the gateway with `HTTP_MODE=business`/`--network-alias`), avoiding the cross-profile state contamination already identified earlier.

The `mockopin-v9-gateway`/`mockopin-v9-proxy` images rebuilt from scratch before the soak (an incidental finding: Decision 119, the TLS 1.3 fix, had changed `gateway/main.go`/`proxy/main.go`, but the `:latest` tag of these images still pointed to the Image ID FROM BEFORE that change -- only the `:pinned` tag, never touched, intentionally stays on the old version. The `:latest` tag is used only by this soak/local tests, never by the real campaign -- see the pending item below).

Real result, 1200 flows (`opin_flow.run_insurance_flow`, `V9_HARNESS=1`, 4 profiles x 300): **1200/1200 OK, zero error.** Per-flow duration with no degradation in any profile -- overall average 1.16-1.24s; each profile's last 10 flows were, on average, FASTER than the first 10 (a cache/JIT effect, not drift). Memory and file descriptors, across the 3 monitored components (gateway `v9-mtls`, `auth`, `mockapi`), show the same pattern across the 4 profiles: grows in the first samples and then STABILIZES INTO A PLATEAU (each series' last 5 samples practically identical) -- no series shows continuous growth across the 300 runs. The gateway's file descriptors, in particular, RISE and then FALL back to the initial level (~8) -- no sign of a leak. The only real observation (not a defect): `mockapi`'s memory plateau in the PQC profile sits higher (~782MB) than in the other 3 profiles (~637-678MB) -- plausibly a larger JVM heap for the ML-DSA-65 objects, but it also stabilizes, it does not keep rising.

**Explicit pending item:** the `:latest` images used in this soak reflect the current code (post-Decision-119), but `PINS.json` still pins the earlier Image ID (`mockopin-v9-gateway`/`proxy`, Decision 61/68) -- the same as the already-known `mockapi` gap (next item). Re-pinning requires an explicit numbered Amendment (Decision 55's policy, item 1) -- not done here, just recording that the soak used binaries newer than the official pin.

**2. `mockapi` -- investigation, no code change (Luciano's explicit request):** the image used by the real campaign: `raidiam-insurance-lambdas:latest` (see `insurance-server-lambdas/docker-compose.yml`), NEVER published to any registry (no digest, only pinned locally by `tar_sha256` in `PINS.json` -- the same pattern as the other 3 images, which are also local only). A real build (`gradle build`, inside the `Dockerfile`'s builder container) fails on an internal Raidiam Gradle/Maven dependency, `com.raidiam.trustframework.mockinsurance:insurance-swagger:1.2.0.2` (`build.gradle:111`), resolved only via `mavenLocal()`/`mavenCentral()` (`build.gradle:50-53`) -- never published to Maven Central nor to any private repository configured in the project (`grep` in `build.gradle`/`settings.gradle`/`gradle.properties`: no private registry URL). The jar (+ pom/module/sources/swagger.yaml) exists today in this development machine's LOCAL `~/.m2` cache (from some earlier build outside this pipeline), but the Dockerfile's builder runs in a container with its OWN empty `~/.m2` -- which is why it always fails when rebuilt via Docker, even on this same machine.

For a third party to reproduce it: they would need the `insurance-swagger-1.2.0.2` jar through some channel that does not exist in this repository today (internal Raidiam access, or receiving the jar externally). Three alternatives, as Luciano requested, without implementing any of them: (a) publish the dependency to an accessible registry (outside this project's control, depends on Raidiam); (b) vendor the jar (+pom) as a local Maven repository embedded inside the git repository itself (`insurance-server-lambdas/vendor/maven-repo/...`, referenced via `maven { url uri('vendor/maven-repo') }` in `build.gradle`, and copied into the Dockerfile's build context) -- the smallest change that preserves third-party reproducibility, using the jar that already exists on this machine; (c) accept and document that `mockapi` can only be obtained pre-built (the image pinned by `tar_sha256`), never rebuilt from source by someone without internal Raidiam access. Recommendation: (b), as it is the only one that closes the reproducibility gap (claim 18 of the Independent EQD Verification) without depending on a third party. Luciano decides.

**3. Pre-campaign manifest** (`thesis/results/v9/campaign/scripts/pre_campaign_manifest.py`): reads the real certificates from `certs/generated/` (via `cryptography`, the same library already used in the project -- confirmed to decode ML-DSA-65 natively, with no need for external openssl/OQS) and builds the artifact x profile x participant matrix (algorithm, key size, signature size, certificate size, SHA-256 fingerprint of the DER, SAN) -- with no secret (only public material). Checks and ABORTS (`exit 1`, never just a warning) if the SAN diverges between Hibrido-AND's two chains, between the 4 profiles, or between the two sides of mTLS -- automates Decision 120's manual confirmation. Tested both ways: passes cleanly against today's real certificates; also tested against a copy with a deliberately corrupted SAN (an ad-hoc `openssl req`, outside the repository) -- correctly aborted, pointing to exactly which variant diverged.

**4. OPINsize analysis in two variants** (`thesis/results/v9/campaign/scripts/opinsize_analysis.py`): a finding while looking for the source before implementing (Luciano's explicit request) -- Schardong et al.'s (2022) Equation 3.1, as cited in `thesis/scripts/report_build/ARCHITECTURE.tpl.md`/`CONSOLIDATED_REPORT.tpl.md` and in v7/v8's final reports, is the THREE-term formula (`N_mTLS x handshake_bytes + N_JWT x JWT_size + N_JWK x JWK_PK_size`); this thesis already EXTENDS it with a fourth term, `N_PKI x PKI_bytes`, since v5 -- the PKI/CRL term is therefore reported as a SEPARATE row in the new script's two variants, never summed inside the JWT term, and the script emits both sums (3 terms, equivalent to the original Eq. 3.1; 4 terms, this thesis's extended formula) side by side. Schardong's own paper is not in this repository (only cited as a bibliographic reference, to be completed) -- it is not possible to confirm here whether "JWT_size" means the whole token or just the signature; so the script computes BOTH variants (`jwt_total_size_bytes`: the whole compact token, same as today's real collector; `jwt_signature_size_bytes`: only the third segment, decoded from base64url to raw bytes), instead of assuming one or the other. Tested with a synthetic JWT of known signature size (the math confirmed both ways) and with a malformed token (aborts with a clear error). **A real limitation found and reported, not hidden:** the real collection pipeline (`baseline_automation.py:compute_metrics()`) only persists `jwt_sizes_bytes` (sizes) in the final `baseline_metrics.json` -- the RAW token texts are never written to disk by the standard pipeline, so the "signature only" variant cannot be retroactively recomputed from a collection already done; it only works with a list of raw JWTs from a fresh capture.

No private key in either of the two new scripts (`git ls-files`/`git grep` on the tips confirmed clean). No push, no tag, no real campaign. Stage 2 not started.

The collector now persists the signature size by construction** (`thesis/scripts/baseline_automation.py:jwt_sig_breakdown()`/`extract_jwt_sig_breakdowns()`, called at the 3 points where `jwt_sizes` was already computed -- `opin_flow.py` lines ~1792/2098, `baseline_automation.py` line ~553): by the header's `alg` and, when needed, by the payload's `pqc` claim -- `PS256` with no `pqc` claim = classical only (JWS 3rd segment); `ML-DSA-65` = PQ only; `MLDSA65-RSA2048-PSS-SHA256` (Strong Nesting) = a fixed 256B sigma1 + the rest = PQ; `PS256` WITH a `pqc.signature` claim (Payload Extension) = classical (3rd segment) PLUS the PQ from the claim, decoded separately -- the two are physically distinct, not concatenated, so they must be summed, not just the 3rd segment (the way an earlier version of the analysis script did it, which WOULD UNDERESTIMATE those tokens). Never persists the raw token/claims -- only the sizes and a construction label (`jwt_sig_breakdown`, a list parallel to `jwt_sizes` in each `call`, aggregated in `compute_metrics()`). **3. `opinsize_analysis.py` fixed to avoid confusing Variant A with Schardong's Eq. 3.1** (a finding from the Independent EQD Verification, Luciano's explicit request): Variant A (complete token) is NEVER called "equivalent to Eq. 3.1" in any output text/label -- it is this thesis's own metric. Variant B (raw signature) now uses `jwt_sig_breakdown()` (classical+PQ summed when physically separate) instead of decoding only the 3rd segment -- this CHANGES the Payload Extension number specifically (previously underestimated, counting only 256B; now counts 256+3309=3565B, the same sum Strong Nesting already gave). `jwt_sig_size`, in the sense Luciano confirmed from Schardong's thesis (Ch. 3, Eq. 3.1/Table 4 -- RSA-2048=256B, Dilithium3=3293B as a reference from ANOTHER implementation, not this project's, which uses ML-DSA-65=3309B), is exactly this Variant B.

**4. Live validation across the 3 requested profiles, the real stack, `V9_HARNESS=1`:** Classic 20/20 calls OK, always `classic_only` (256, None); PQC 20/20 OK, always `pqc_pure` (None, 3309); Hibrido dual=true 20/20 OK, both `payload_extension` and `strong_nesting` (256, 3309) -- confirms live exactly the synthetic test's numbers, across the 4 real construction types. **A real finding during validation, root-caused and fixed:** the first two attempts gave an intermittent TLS error (`SSLEOFError`, the failure point varying each attempt) -- real root cause: a `v9-mtls` container from an earlier round (Decision 121, the soak) had been left running, registered under the SAME network alias `mtls` as this validation's gateway -- two containers with the same alias on the same Docker network makes name resolution non-deterministic, explaining the randomness of the failure point. The stale container removed; the next 3 validations ran clean. `pre_campaign_manifest.py` rerun, still passing (5/5 SAN invariants).

## Decision 125 -- the pre-flight check (local and campaign) now checks for orphan Docker containers/networks before every window, aborting if any are found (2026-11-11)

A real finding (during Decision 122's validation): a `v9-mtls` container from an earlier LOCAL round (the soak, Decision 121) kept running and registered under the SAME network alias `mtls` as this validation's gateway -- two containers with the same alias on the same Docker network makes name resolution NON-DETERMINISTIC, causing intermittent TLS failures whose cause was only found live, through manual investigation. `v9-mtls` is the real name `SSHExecutor` uses for the gateway in the genuine campaign (`gateway_container="v9-mtls"`, the constructor's default, `orchestrator.py`); `mtls` is the name used by the local test `integration/run_t5.sh`. Either one, or the `mockopin-v9-net` network, left standing from an earlier round can silently corrupt the next one.

**LOCAL pre-flight:** `preflight.check_no_orphan_docker_resources()` (new) lists local Docker containers (`docker ps -a`, including stopped ones -- a name occupied by a stopped container still collides with `docker run --name`) and networks (`docker network ls`), by EXACT NAME (never substring -- `auth` should not match `auth-gateway-v2` from another project on the same host). `integration/run_t5.sh` gained the same check in bash, at the top of the script, aborting (`exit 1`) BEFORE building anything if it finds leftovers -- tested live, both ways: with an `auth` container+`mockopin-v9-net` network simulated on purpose, it correctly aborted listing both; with both cleaned up, it passed clean.

**CAMPAIGN pre-flight:** `preflight.check_no_orphan_docker_resources_remote(host)` (new) does the same check via SSH on a real instance -- relevant because stop/start between windows preserves the disk (Decision 43/45), so a Docker leftover from an earlier window would survive the same way. `SSHExecutor.check_no_orphans()` (a new method) runs this on ALL servers in the window (`_all_server_ips()`, the same pattern as `capture_ready_check`). `orchestrator.run_pilot()` calls `executor.check_no_orphans()` right at the start -- BEFORE `out_dir.mkdir()`, BEFORE any run -- and raises `RuntimeError` with the exact list of what was found if `go=False`; tested live with a fake executor that fails, confirming no file is written to `out_dir` before the abort.

**`LocalExecutor.check_no_orphans()` deliberately NEVER performs the real check** (always `go=True`, the same pattern already established by `capture_ready_check` for this class) -- `LocalExecutor` is pure simulation, it never genuinely brings up Docker, and the 374 existing `run_pilot` tests use a real `LocalExecutor()`; forcing a real Docker call there would make the test suite fragile to the Docker state of the machine running it. The genuine local pre-flight is the responsibility of whoever actually brings up Docker locally (`run_t5.sh`, or any new script that calls `check_no_orphan_docker_resources()` directly).

10 new tests in `tests/test_preflight.py` (exact match vs. substring, local/remote detection, Docker/SSH unavailable, real integration with `run_pilot` aborting before writing any file, `LocalExecutor` always passing). Full suite: 383/383 (373 before + 10 new).

No private key in any file. No push, no tag, no real campaign. Stage 2 not started.

## Decision 126 -- N_JWK resolved by real capture (queries, not entries); 3 reproducibility bugs fixed (gitattributes, golang pin, single-file bind-mount) (2026-11-11)

**N_JWK (addendum item 1).** Brought up the real business stack (`docker compose --profile main up -d --force-recreate auth mongo_seed mockapi`, insurance-server-lambdas) and captured `/jwks` live from the AS (port 3000) and the RS (port 8081), across the 4 profiles (hibrido-v8 and hibrido-and share the same backend, `BACKEND_CRYPTO_PROFILE_ENV["hibrido-v8"]==BACKEND_CRYPTO_PROFILE_ENV["hibrido-and"]=="hybrid"` -- an identical capture, not redone). Full evidence in `thesis/results/v9/campaign/evidence/jwks_capture_2026-11-11.json` (public material only -- a JWKS key has no private component by nature).

Real result: two DIFFERENT definitions coexist and both are correct, each measuring something different.
- **HTTP queries to /jwks per flow:** CONSTANT, 2 (one to the AS, one to the RS), confirmed in `opin_flow.py` (lines 2116/2203) across the 4 profiles. This is the definition `opinsize_analysis.py` uses as `--n-jwk` (now documented in the module's docstring and the argument's help text).
- **Entries in the JSON response (`keys`), summed across AS+RS:** NOT constant. The AS always publishes 2 (sig+enc, across the 4 profiles -- the id_token's encryption remains classical even under PQC, Decision [EQD item 12]). The RS publishes 1 in Classic/PQC (sig only) but 2 in Hibrido (the combined `kty=HYBRID` entry PLUS a separate `RSA`/PS256 entry, same kid -- compatibility with a legacy verifier that ignores the PQC extension, see `ResponseSigningService.java` lines 70-82). Summing AS+RS: 3 (Classic/PQC) vs 4 (Hibrido) -- the real origin of the "N_JWK: 3 vs 4" finding from an earlier verification round, which had not managed to reproduce this live (localstack failed in that session). The finding was real, it was just measuring the wrong thing for `opinsize_analysis.py`'s purpose.

No code had "3 vs 4" hardcoded (n_jwk is a mandatory CLI argument, with no default) -- there was no numeric bug to fix, only the definitional ambiguity, now closed with real evidence and documented in the script itself.

**Reproducibility hygiene (addendum item 3), 3 findings from the independent EQD verification, now genuinely fixed (not just worked around in a disposable worktree):**

(a) `.gitattributes` gained `*.patch text eol=lf` -- without this, a fresh `git worktree add`/clone on Windows (with `core.autocrlf=true`, Git for Windows's default) converts LF->CRLF in `thesis/results/v9/toolchain/patches/and.patch`, breaking `git apply` and preventing the Go toolchain from being rebuilt from scratch on that platform. The git blob was already correct (LF) -- it was purely a checkout artifact.

(b) `mock-service-os/certs/Dockerfile` pinned `golang:1.23-alpine`, but this module's `go.mod` requires `go 1.27rc2` -- the real build always failed. Swapped for the same digest already used and verified in `thesis/results/v9/certs/Dockerfile`/`thesis/results/v9/toolchain/Dockerfile` (`golang:1.27.3-alpine@sha256:d200d2dd...`), for pin coherence across the project, never a new, unverified digest. Tested live: complete build, success.

(c) `preflight.check_legacy_bind_mount_files()` (new, testable with no real Docker): `insurance-server-lambdas/docker-compose.yml` and `mock-service-os/docker-compose.yml` (the `localstack` service in both) mount `mock-service-os/certs/{op,op_pqc,op_hybrid}.{key,crt}` as a SINGLE-FILE bind-mount -- if the file does not exist on the host (a fresh clone, before the generator runs), Docker creates a DIRECTORY in its place, blocking any LATER certificate generation until someone notices and removes it by hand (blocked the earlier EQD verification several times). Detection only, never automatic correction -- the same pattern as every pre-flight check in this project: reports a missing file or "is a directory" with a clear note, never deletes/recreates anything on its own. 3 new tests (`tmp_path`, with no real Docker).

(d) `thesis/results/v9/campaign/scripts/teardown_backend_main.sh` (new): `docker compose down`, WITHOUT `--profile main`, does NOT remove the `main` profile's containers (auth/mongo_seed/mockapi/psql/localstack/mongodb) -- exits with code 0 and does nothing, a real process finding from the earlier EQD verification. Confirmed live this round: reproduced the bug (a plain `docker compose down` left 5 of the 6 containers running), then confirmed the helper (`docker compose --profile main down`) genuinely removes everything, including the network.

**`pre_campaign_manifest.py` (addendum item 2):** gained the `grupo_tls_esperado_por_perfil` section, reading from `evaluate_criteria.EXPECTED_CURVE` (the SAME single source `orchestrator._assert_profile_negotiated` already uses in its active per-run assertion since Decision 119 -- that assertion itself already existed and already covered exactly the 4 requested values, `CurveP384`/`MLKEM1024`/`SecP384r1MLKEM1024`/`SecP384r1MLKEM1024`; only the EXPECTED value was missing from the manifest too, never duplicating the verification logic here).

**Proof of no regression (Luciano's explicit requirement):** a SHA-256 hash of `PINS.json` and of `pre_campaign_manifest.py`'s output taken BEFORE and AFTER item 3's changes -- identical in both cases (`PINS.json`: `3b025aa3...`; manifest: `775c0948...`). The hygiene changes (Dockerfile, gitattributes, preflight, teardown) never touched a certificate or pinned image. Full suite: 386/386 (383 before + 3 new).

## Decision 127 (Amendment, 2026-11-11, v9 pilot Stage 2 -- real execution on AWS)

**A real finding during Stage 2:** when running `deliver_images.py` against the freshly created real infrastructure, Decision 68's fail-closed correctly aborted: the local tar_sha256 of the gateway/proxy (`mockopin-v9-gateway:latest`/`mockopin-v9-proxy:latest`) no longer matched the one pinned in Decision 123. Root cause: at least one independent verification fork in this session (between Decision 123 and the start of Stage 2) rebuilt gateway/proxy inside an ISOLATED git worktree for testing -- but a Docker tag is a GLOBAL daemon resource, never isolated per worktree, and it was overwritten, invalidating the pin before the pilot even ran.

**No wrong image was delivered** -- the fail-closed worked exactly as designed (Decision 68), aborting before any scp.

**Investigation (extracting and hashing the binary from inside the fresh image, not just the .tar):** the Go BINARY inside the rebuilt image is BYTE FOR BYTE IDENTICAL to the `binary_sha256` pinned in Decision 123 (gateway `33f3871b...`, proxy `07c9fb03...`) -- reproducibility confirmed again, no code regression since the TLS 1.3 fix. Only the `tar_sha256`/`rootfs_layers[2]`/`image_id` changed, due to the ephemeral/random `COPY certs` layer (the same pattern already documented in Decision 123) -- a `make certs` ran between the two pinnings.

**Re-pinned** with the fresh values (new tar_sha256/rootfs_layers/image_id, unchanged binary_sha256) for gateway and proxy in `PINS.json`.

**A process risk to fix before the official campaign:** verification forks/sessions that rebuild Docker images under the SAME tag used by the real delivery, even while working in an isolated git worktree, mutate the host's shared Docker daemon -- worktree isolation NEVER isolates the Docker daemon. Recommendation: any verification/test rebuild should use a distinct tag (e.g. `:verify`, `:test`), never overwrite the tag used by the real delivery (`:latest`).

**A new local preflight (item 5), closing the gap that let Stage 2 spend an entire real apply before discovering this:** `preflight.check_local_images_match_pins()`, now called inside `run_preflight()` -- compares `RootFS.Layers` + a subset of `.Config` (NEVER the raw `image_id`, the same criterion already established in Decision 68: the Image ID diverges across Docker versions even with identical content) of EVERY pinned image present locally against `PINS.json`, failing with the exact list of what diverges. Runs BEFORE any `terraform apply` -- `deliver_images.py` (Decision 68) remains the last-line fail-closed, on the remote-delivery side, but now the problem is caught without spending a single minute of real infrastructure. A pinned image missing locally does NOT fail (it will be caught at the right time by `deliver_images`) -- this only detects a divergence in an image that EXISTS but changed.

## Decision 129 (Amendment, 2026-11-11, final validation and re-pin of mockapi)

**Luciano's request, conditionally authorized ("accept the new image IF proven"):** a complete soak of 50 real OAuth flows per profile (Classic, PQC, Hibrido dual=true, and the dual=false control if time allowed) against the new mockapi image, a request-by-request comparison against the old soak (300/profile, commit `93e57b2f`), a memory-plateau comparison, an explanation of the divergent bytecode found in Decision 128, and a conditional re-pin if all of this comes out OK.

Continuous memory/fd sampling through the containers' entire real lifetime window (the same corrected methodology as the original soak).

**Item 2 (request-by-request comparison):** `n_calls=20` constant across ALL 200 new flows, identical to the old soak's pattern (`n_calls=20` constant across the 1200 flows of `93e57b2f`). Zero structural divergence. Signature size/type per artifact already confirmed identical in the earlier validation (`/jwks`/`/health` differential test, 6/6 matching against Decision 126's persisted capture) -- not redone here because already proven, to avoid repeating work.

Plausibly the optimized build (Micronaut AOT) reduces reflection/bean-context overhead at runtime -- not an anomaly, a favorable result.

The only real difference is a name-variant mapping entry (dot/dash) that Micronaut AOT generates for environment variables PRESENT ON THE BUILD HOST at the moment Gradle ran -- the entry `EFC_11068_4126798990` (the old 11/10 build) matches the `EFC_<PID>_<random suffix>` pattern of a sandbox variable from this very tool's OWN execution session (confirmed: the current environment has `EFC_<current PID>_<same suffixes>` variables, including the same `4126798990` suffix) -- never a real application configuration, never referenced anywhere in the project's source code. **No behavioral effect:** that table is just a lookup optimization; a missing entry makes Micronaut fall back to the normal (non-optimized) property-resolution path, which always resolves correctly -- never a functional failure.

## Decision 130 (Amendment, 2026-11-11/12, a real incident -- the controller self-terminated mid-window)

**What happened:** during Stage 2 (the real AWS pilot), the infrastructure came up successfully across the 7 regions (78/78 resources, 12/12 instances). In the middle of image delivery/preparation of the first block, the controller and the 5 resources depending on it (the sa-east-1 server + the 3 clients routed through it: L123/ca-central-1, L219/eu-north-1, L325/ap-southeast-1) SELF-TERMINATED (not stopped -- genuinely terminated, with the root EBS deleted because `DeleteOnTermination` was never set to false).

**Root cause:** `self_terminate_hours=4` (a decision from this very session, an "extra safety margin" for the pilot) was a FIXED deadline, counted from boot, independent of real activity -- combined with `instance_initiated_shutdown_behavior="terminate"`. The real preparation (delivering and verifying the per-server backend image, ~690MB over inter-region network + docker load + sha256 verification + `docker compose up` waiting for postgres/mongodb/localstack) measured, live, at ~55-65 minutes PER SERVER, serially -- for 3 servers that already consumes ~2-3h, hitting the 4h deadline before the real measurement window even started.

**Real confirmed loss:** controller + sa-east-1 server + 3 dependent clients, 6 instances, the controller's root EBS deleted (confirmed: zero orphan volumes, zero snapshots in sa-east-1). Surviving partial data (never officially counted) recovered from the 6 resources that were NOT affected (us-east-1/ap-northeast-1 and their clients): real pcap captures of the Classico profile on 4 of the 8 routes, continuous CPU/memory samples for the 4 profiles on those same routes -- discarded by the author's decision (the earlier window invalidated, nothing counted).

**Fix applied:**
1. `instance_initiated_shutdown_behavior` changed from `"terminate"` to `"stop"` across ALL 12 modules in `terraform_campanha_oficial/main.tf`, and applied via `aws ec2 modify-instance-attribute` on the 6 surviving resources (without recreating them).
2. The safety switch stopped being a fixed deadline and became a **renewable dead man's switch**: `SSHExecutor.renew_safety_timers()`/`_renew_local_safety_timer()` (new, `orchestrator.py`) send an "I'm alive" heartbeat to the active hosts on every `start_block` and every counted run, pushing `/etc/mockopin-campaign/deadline` to +3h (`SAFETY_TIMER_RENEW_HOURS`) -- it only triggers STOP (never again terminate) if the heartbeat stops arriving for 3 full hours. The heartbeat runs INSIDE the `orchestrator.py` process the controller executes via `nohup` -- it never depends on an external call from whoever operates the session, so it survives any connection/session drop on the operator's side.
3. The 6 lost resources were recreated via an incremental Terraform apply (6 add, 14 change -- the survivors' shutdown behavior + EIP reassociation + 2 SG rules --, 0 destroy). All public IPs came back identical to before (real EIPs, never destroyed, only disassociated by the termination).
4. A related process finding, fixed in the same batch: STOPPED (not removed) containers from before the incident (`v9-mtls` on the servers, `pqc_signer_service_run`/`tls_kem_proxy_run` on one client) remained as a real leftover, caught by the preflight check (Decision 125) and cleaned up manually before relaunching.
5. An additional process finding: the adapted inventory delivered to the recreated controller still had the old PRIVATE IP of the sa-east-1 server (the public EIP is preserved on recreation, the private one is NOT) -- confirmed via the container's real log (`tls_kem_proxy_run` dialing the wrong private IP, "no route to host"). Fixed by regenerating the inventory from Terraform's real state after the recreation.
6. `cost_tracker.py`/`orchestrator.py` gained `--cost-window-start-utc`, allowing the cost clock to be reconstructed from an earlier REAL launch time (the original launch, 2026-11-11T22:11:25Z) instead of "now" -- conservative by design, it counts the whole interval including the real gap during which 6 instances were terminated, never underestimating.

**Open pending item, not fixed in this Decision:** `deliver_source.py` does not have `campaign_topology.py` nor `cost_tracker.py` in the list of files delivered to the controller, even though `orchestrator.py`/`preflight.py` depend on them -- worked around manually (direct scp) twice in this same Decision; the definitive fix to the file list is left for this session's batch of process-fix commits.

## Decision 131 (2026-11-12, official campaign design -- authored by Luciano)

**The author's decision:** the official campaign abandons the design of 3 windows of 10 runs/cell (which in practice were stitched together with no real temporal separation) and becomes **ONE window of 10 runs/cell**, median and dispersion as the statistic, keeping the 4 profiles measured together in the same campaign (the dual=false control remains reserved, outside the main reports). The author's literal reason: the 3 windows never had real temporal separation in practice, so the formal split into 3 added nothing a single, larger window would not give.

**Effect on estimates/reports:** the pilot's calibration report now highlights variant V1 (10/cell, 1 window) as the current design; V2/V3 remain only as historical/comparative context. The marginal cost of an extra Classico block (3/cell) as a temporal-drift control, if the author decides to include it, is estimated separately, never decided by the session.

## Decision 132 (2026-11-12 04:03 UTC, raised cost-stop ceiling -- the author's authorization)

**The author's decision:** the cost-stop ceiling (`--cost-stop-usd`) rises from **US$13 to US$20**. Literal reason: the US$13 ceiling was a safety lock (never an official real-cost number, see `cost_tracker.py`), and Decision 130's incident accounting (reconstructed from the original launch, 22:11:25Z, via `--cost-window-start-utc`) keeps counting the entire wall-clock time -- including the incident's gap -- which reduced the remaining headroom before any additional real run could be measured. The author explicitly kept the honest count (not resetting the clock) and asked for the higher ceiling instead.

**Applied:** the orchestrator process restarted with `--cost-stop-usd 20.0` at a moment when no counted run yet existed in this window (only warm-ups, which never count) -- zero real loss. The stop mechanism remains `stop`, never `terminate` (Decision 130). If the US$20 ceiling is reached, the in-progress cell is completed before stopping (existing behavior, `cost_stop_info`/`break` at the end of the counted-runs loop, never mid-cell) and the matrix's exact point is recorded in the manifest, for future resumption.

**The author's explicit rule for the future:** if the completion forecast indicates US$20 is not enough, the session must warn BEFORE taking any action -- never extend the ceiling on its own again.

## Decision 133 (2026-11-12, a second real crash -- the dedicated-captures phase killed the process after the whole matrix had already finished in memory; the structural fix is to redo the complete pilot -- authored by Luciano)

**Incident:** the main 32-cell matrix finished entirely, in memory, with no failure at all. The process only persisted `manifest.json`/`piloto_calls.json`/etc at the END of `run_pilot()`, after a SEPARATE dedicated-captures phase that iterated profile-outer/route-inner (the opposite order of the main matrix, route-outer/profile-inner). That phase revisited routes/clients the main matrix had already finished hours earlier and whose dead-man's-switch heartbeat had already legitimately expired (safely stopped, never terminated -- Decision 130). The delivery call to an already-stopped host raised an unhandled exception, killing the entire process and discarding the whole 32-cell matrix, despite it already being 100% complete in memory.

**The author's decision (option a, with the additions below):** properly fix the code and redo the complete pilot from scratch, WITHOUT touching anything from the official one. Do not spend the whole matrix just to test -- validate the fix locally before running again on the real AWS. Raise the stop ceiling from US$20 to US$25. Record the decision and only commit once authorized. Suspend the conditional authorization for automatically starting the official campaign. A complete final report only at the conclusion.

**Implemented in `orchestrator.py`:**
- `_atomic_write_json(path, obj)`: atomic write (a tempfile in the same directory + `os.replace`), never leaves a partially written JSON.
- Each run/warm-up now writes its own file to `out_dir/runs_raw/{profile}__{route}__run{NN}.json` (or `run00_warmupN.json`) IMMEDIATELY after being produced, before anything else.
- `_persist_incremental()` (a local closure): rewrites `piloto_calls.json`, `criterio6_execucoes.json`, `aquecimento_execucoes.json` and a new `manifest_partial.json` (with `complete: false` and the running totals) after EVERY completed cell -- not only at the end.
- **The dedicated-captures phase was merged into the main per-route loop** (runs right after that route's cells, in the same already-shuffled `order`, with the client still "warm"/recently renewed) -- eliminates the root cause (revisiting), not just mitigates it.
- Each individual dedicated capture runs in an isolated `try/except`: a failure goes to `capturas_dedicadas_falhas` (never brings down the process); a success goes to `capturas_dedicadas_feitas`.
- A new `SSHExecutor.renew_all_safety_timers()`, called once at the start of `run_pilot()` (before creating `out_dir`), renewing ALL hosts in the inventory -- prevents a host whose last heartbeat came from an earlier round (already irrelevant) from expiring before the new process reaches its route.
- At the end, `manifest.json` is also now written via `_atomic_write_json`, and `manifest_partial.json` is removed once the final manifest is successfully written.
- Two new tests in `test_orchestrator.py` validate the fix WITHOUT spending real runs: `test_persistencia_incremental_sobrevive_a_queda_no_meio_da_janela` (injects an exception on the 3rd run, confirms that 2 `runs_raw/*.json` files and 2 entries in `piloto_calls.json` survive, even with no final `manifest.json`) and `test_captura_dedicada_falha_isolada_nunca_derruba_o_processo` (injects a failure into a specific capture, confirms the process finishes normally with the isolated failure recorded). 395 tests passing (393 + 2 new) before any new real attempt on AWS.

**Applied:** the cost-stop ceiling raised from US$20 to US$25 (`--cost-stop-usd 25.0`), explicitly authorized by the author during incident recovery. The pilot redone from scratch with the fixed code, started after the local tests passed.

**Result:** the redone pilot completed **64/64 counted runs, 160/160 warm-ups, 32/32 dedicated captures, zero failures** (`capturas_dedicadas_falhas: []`, `cost_stop: null`), final cost US$20.71 (within the US$25 ceiling).

**The author's request:** organize the redone pilot's results in the EXACT layout the official campaign will use, to validate the organization and the consolidated report before the GO -- `artifacts/`, `size/` and `latency/`, each with `experiment1 - Classic`/`experiment2 - PQC`/`experiment3 - Hybrid`/`experiment4 - Control` (control outside the consolidated report), one folder per route, `runs/runNN.json` (latency also `run00_warmup.json`), plus derived `median_metrics.json`/`MEDIAN_REPORT.md`. Parameterizable (`--expected-runs-per-cell`, 2 in the pilot, 10 in the official campaign -- fails hard if the found number diverges), re-runnable (idempotent -- overwrites the destination, never the source). The layout now requested for v9 (flat by route, no region level, `size`/`latency` separated at the top, `runNN.json` as the primary data) is deliberately simpler and does not match v8's pattern. **Proposal:** keep the new layout as specified (the author's decision, not the session's) -- v8 is already frozen and never needs to be retroactively reorganized; v9 can adopt its own layout without breaking anything in v8, as long as the divergence stays documented here (done).

## 135. Mandatory confirmations before the official campaign (Phase 0, the author's decision) -- all satisfactory, GO released

The author's decision after the redone pilot's report: the official campaign runs the 32 dedicated captures, code frozen at the redone pilot's commit (`4a1210ea`), a local tag `v9-campanha-oficial-congelada` created at that commit (no push). Four confirmations required before relaunching the fleet -- all verified against the redone pilot's real data (`thesis/results/v9_pilot/`), never estimated:

**(a) Breakdown of the 44 calls/run:** identical across the 4 profiles (Classico, PQC, Hibrido-v8, Hibrido-AND), 16 `runNN.json` files per profile, `calls/run` and `jwts/run` with a SINGLE distinct value across all of them (44 and 28, respectively) -- no variation between profiles. By call origin (`src`, the same across the 4 profiles): `CallProtectedResource` 14/run (14 JWTs -- consent-state query + protected insurance data), `login` 12/run (the OIDC flow's login/consent interaction, 0 JWT), `FetchServerKeys` (`/jwks`) 4/run (0 JWT), `OpinInsertMtlsCa` (`/root-ca.pem`+`/issuer-ca.pem`, PKI/CRL) 4/run (0 JWT), `CallTokenEndpoint` (`/token`) 4/run (6 JWTs), `CallPAREndpoint` (`/request`) 2/run (4 JWTs), `JARM` (`/auth`) 2/run (2 JWTs), `CallConsentEndpointWithBearerToken` 2/run (2 JWTs). Sum: 44 calls, 28 JWTs, the same across the 4 profiles -- confirmed by direct aggregation of the `runNN.json` files, not by sampling.

**(b) What the dedicated captures measure, and whether the handshake/mTLS are recoverable:** each dedicated capture runs `tcpdump`+`tshark` (with a decrypted `KEYLOG_PATH`) on the server's primary interface, producing PER-MESSAGE handshake size (ClientHello/ServerHello/EncryptedExtensions/Certificate/CertificateRequest/CertificateVerify/Finished, with SNI to separate client-facing `mtls` connections from server-to-server `matls-api.local` ones) -- feeds `artifacts/` (raw pcap/keylog/log) and, by extension, the aggregated sizes in `size/`. Verified live in the 4 L0-sa-east-1 `.log` files (classico, pqc, hibrido-v8, hibrido-and): **6 distinct TCP streams with SNI `mtls` in each of the 4 profiles** -- confirms that the COUNT of mTLS handshakes per run (6) is, just like the bytes per message, recoverable from the data the official campaign will generate, under the same mechanisms already validated in the pilot. No code fix is needed. (Note: this count is sampled ONCE per profile×route cell via a dedicated capture, never once per each of the cell's measured runs -- valid because the business flow is deterministic and identical on every repetition.)

**(c) Sizes vs. preflight and CPU steal:** the raw ML-DSA-65 signature (`pq_sig_bytes`) = 3309 B in EVERY occurrence in the redone pilot's real data (PQC profile) -- matches exactly the preflight's expected value. Aggregated CPU steal: the maximum observed across any of the 64 real runs (`cpu_client`/`cpu_server`) was 0.068% -- well below the 5% ceiling set for the official campaign's automatic stop.

**A side finding (not a bug, just verified to avoid propagating a false positive):** the first reading of the `v9_pilot/` tree seemed to indicate profiles swapped between `experiment3 - Hybrid` (contains `hibrido-and_*` files) and `experiment4 - Control` (contains `hibrido-v8_*` files). Checked against `PROFILE_TO_EXPERIMENT`/`CONTROL_PROFILE` in `organize_v9_results.py` and against `DECISIONS.md`'s own title ("Hibrido-AND, dual-certificate TLS authentication") and Decision 1: Hibrido-AND IS the third main profile ("Hybrid dual=true", this thesis's new two-independent-chain architecture), Hibrido-v8 IS the control (a profile inherited from v8, kept outside the consolidated report to isolate the dual-TLS effect). The mapping in the script is CORRECT; not a bug, no fix needed.

**Result:** all 4 confirmations satisfactory. GO released for Phase 1 (the official campaign's real run).

## 136. Official campaign's cost ceiling raised to US$45 (alert US$40) -- the author's decision, a partial report in progress

The author's decision, after a partial report of the official campaign already running: raise the ceiling from US$35 to US$45 accumulated, and the alert from US$30 to US$40, keeping the count from the same clock (2026-11-11T22:11:25Z, never reset). Reason recorded by the author: the preparation cost (~US$6, the fleet on during Phase 0's investigation and the heartbeat/orphan fixes before the real launch) consumed part of the projected margin, and the run order (`PROFILES = [classico, pqc, hibrido-v8, hibrido-and]`) leaves the Hibrido-AND profile ("Hybrid dual=true") LAST -- a ceiling reached too early would interrupt the window right before measuring this thesis's most important profile.

**A real limitation, honestly recorded:** the orchestrator process is ALREADY RUNNING (launched 2026-11-12T16:13:10Z, PID on the controller) with `--cost-stop-usd 35 --cost-alert-usd 30` fixed in memory from the command line -- this code has no mechanism for dynamically rereading the threshold (no intermediate file/env var, confirmed by reading `cost_tracker.py`/`orchestrator.py`). Raising the ALREADY RUNNING process's ceiling would require restarting it -- and `run_pilot(resume=True)` ONLY resumes a COMPLETE, identical window (`total_execucoes == expected_total`); there is no intra-window checkpoint (an explicit, already-accepted decision by the author, documented in `run_pilot`'s own docstring: "interrupting mid-window always loses that window"). Restarting now would redo the already-persisted runs from scratch -- exactly what the author asked NOT to do ("without interrupting the ongoing campaign"). So the new US$45/US$40 ceiling is recorded here as the current decision, but it will ONLY actually be applied by the code if/when the process needs to be relaunched for another valid reason; the currently running instance continues internally at US$35/US$30 until then.

**Real projection, from the numbers measured right now (16:58 UTC, ~45min into the real window):** estimated cost US$26.92 (the conservative clock since 22:11:25Z, status "ok"), measured marginal rate ≈US$1.43/hour (fixed as a function of elapsed wall-clock time, never of run pace). Remaining margin to the OLD US$35 ceiling: ≈US$8.08, i.e. ≈5.6h from now (≈22:35 UTC). The window's projected total duration (from its 16:13 UTC launch, ~5.2h with dedicated captures): estimated completion ≈21:25 UTC -- BEFORE the old US$35 ceiling is reached, with ≈1h of margin. In other words: by the current numbers, the original US$35 ceiling would probably have been sufficient anyway: the new US$45 ceiling works as additional safety margin, not as a fix for an already-predicted overrun -- but it is recorded and will be applied on any future relaunch of this window.

## 137. Plan B for resumption: ceiling raised to US$60, pre-authorized, mechanism designed and tested locally (never against the real hosts)

The author's decision (a continuation of Decision 136, without touching the running process): the PLAN B RESUMPTION ceiling rises from US$45 to **US$60 accumulated**, counted from the same clock, 2026-11-11T22:11:25Z. The US$35 ceiling of the currently running process remains UNCHANGED (no action taken on the running process).

**Plan B pre-authorized:** if the running process's US$35 ceiling triggers before the window finishes, the already-expected behavior (completes the in-progress run of that cell, calls `stop_block`, persists incrementally, stops the window with `stop`, never `terminate`) is accepted as is. When that happens, WITHOUT waiting for new authorization: resume ONLY the cells not yet completed (never repeating what is already persisted in `runs_raw/`), in a SECOND window, with a US$60 ceiling. Document in the final report that a second window happened, and why.

**Resumption mechanism -- designed and tested NOW, in parallel, without touching the ongoing campaign and without using any of the 12 real hosts:** two new scripts, in `thesis/results/v9/campaign/plano_b_retomada/` (its OWN folder, separate from `campaign/scripts/`, never mixed with the frozen code):

- `resume_plan.py` (sha256 `375eb35c63553f522489a9b71e3254d09c6f0b756ffffde2664a13a632834672`): READ-ONLY on a window's (partial or complete) `runs_raw/`/`criterio1_capturas/` -- computes, per (profile, route), exactly which run/warm-up numbers are missing and whether the dedicated capture is missing, deciding nothing on its own.
- `resume_runner.py` (sha256 `5c7c0a0634fcdbb03f07e5f132dd4544ec97ccc0f6c649b7423b545e5b1bb831`): consumes the plan and calls `orchestrator.run_pilot` -- the SAME frozen module, imported with no modification whatsoever -- once per pending cell, with `routes=[route]`/`profiles=[profile]` and `n_per_profile`/`n_warmup_per_profile` equal exactly to the MISSING number (never the window's total). Each call writes to its own subfolder (local numbering 1..N); the runner copies/renames the resulting files to the REAL number that was missing from window 1 (e.g., a cell missing `run03` -> this call's single run, locally numbered `run01`, is copied as `run03` at the destination), with fail-closed if any destination already exists (never overwrites).

**Local test performed (never against AWS):** a complete window generated with `--mode simulate` (4 profiles x 3 routes x 3 runs + 1 warm-up = 48 files in `runs_raw/` + 12 captures), then an artificial cut to simulate a mid-cell stop (one route completely untouched, one cell missing only the last run + its capture, two cells of the same route never started) -- 23 of 48 files, 5 of 12 captures. `resume_plan.py` identified exactly the 7 pending cells and the right missing numbers. `resume_runner.py` ran only what was missing (e.g., 1 run for a cell missing only 1) and, after the copy/rename, returned: 25 new files + 23 from window 1 = 48, identical to the original complete window's total; 7 new captures + 5 = 12, likewise; zero duplicate names, zero overwrites.

**Never applied to the 12 real hosts nor to the running process.** These two scripts are a documented deviation from the frozen commit `4a1210ea` -- they are NOT part of the official campaign's code (which remains byte for byte identical to the commit, see the already-recorded sha256 check) -- and will only actually be used against the real AWS if Plan B triggers (i.e., if the current process's US$35 ceiling is reached before the end). If/when that happens, the second window runs with a real `--mode ssh`, a US$60 cost ceiling, and the same clock since 22:11:25Z -- never restarting the count.

## 138. A real crash in the official campaign's first attempt -- cause, state, the author's decision to restart from scratch

**The crash:** the orchestrator process (launched 2026-11-12T16:13:10Z) died between ~19:28Z and ~19:34Z, discovered when checking progress at the author's request. A `RuntimeError` in `_tcp_preflight` -- the L14 route's client (ca-central-1, <fleet-ip-client-L14-attempt1>) became unreachable by SSH.

**Real cause (not assumed -- verified against the real AWS state after the crash):** the L14 route's host itself had already safely stopped (`Client.InstanceInitiatedShutdown`, `stop`, never `terminate`) BEFORE the main loop reached it. Root: `renew_all_safety_timers()` (called once at the start of `run_pilot`) gives a 3h margin to ALL hosts at once; the PER-ROUTE renewal (`renew_safety_timers(route)`, inside the loop) only touches a route's host when the main loop REACHES that route. The official campaign's real window lasts ~5.2h -- LONGER than the initial 3h margin -- so a route near the END of the run order (L14, 6th of 8 routes in this window's order) had its original deadline expire before the loop reached it. The same design (only an initial batch + per-route renewal) had already caused a similar incident during this same session's preparation (fixed manually, seen in the earlier partial report) -- but the initial 3h deadline, even renewed, was never enough for a window whose TOTAL duration exceeds 3h. A definitive fix recorded in this same Decision, "Heartbeat fixed" item below.

**Exact state at the moment of the crash (verified in the real persisted data, never estimated):** 200 of 320 measured runs (62%), 100 of 160 warm-ups, 20 of 32 dedicated captures, **0 run/measurement failures** -- the crash was of the PROCESS (an unhandled crash in `_tcp_preflight`), never of a cell. Estimated cost at the time of discovery: ≈US$30.64 (the clock since 2026-11-11T22:11:25Z, never reset). Real fleet after the crash: 7 instances already self-stopped (the dead man's switch), 5 still `running` (controller included) -- none terminated/destroyed; the remaining 5 were manually stopped (`stop`) at the author's request, confirmed against the real AWS: 12/12 `stopped`, 12/12 EIPs preserved (allocated and associated, none released).

**The author's decision:** do NOT resume this attempt (despite Decision 137's resumption mechanism being ready and tested) -- restart the WHOLE official campaign from scratch, in a new single window, with the already-approved design (3 profiles x 8 routes x 10 runs + 5 warm-ups, control, Hibrido-AND last). This attempt's 200 results were archived, untouched, in `thesis/results/v9_aborted_attempt_1/` (an exact copy of the controller's `oficial_out/` at the moment of the crash, never moved from the source, never mixed with the final analysis) -- see that folder's `README.md` for the summary. This directory NEVER enters `thesis/results/v9/`'s final organization/analysis.

**Heartbeat fixed (the author's request: its OWN renewal, independent of the main loop, with a margin greater than the window's estimated TOTAL duration):** `orchestrator.py` gained `_start_heartbeat_thread(executor)` -- a `daemon=True` thread that pings ALL hosts (`renew_all_safety_timers()` + `_renew_local_safety_timer()`) every `HEARTBEAT_THREAD_INTERVAL_SECONDS=300` (5min), with a safety ceiling `HEARTBEAT_THREAD_MAX_HOURS=12` (much larger than any real estimated window duration, ~5.2h) -- never depending on which route/profile the loop is processing. Called once, right after the already-existing batch renewal, at the start of `run_pilot`. A single host's failure in one cycle never brings down the thread nor the following cycles (the same individual-failure tolerance already used elsewhere in the heartbeat mechanism). Diff: insertion only, 68 lines, 0 removal/change (`import threading` + the new function + a 1-line call inside `run_pilot`) -- no other logic in the file touched.

**Local test, before using it in the real relaunch (never against the 12 hosts):** (1) an isolated test with a fake executor that only records the time of each call -- 7 renewals in 6.5s at a 1s interval (configured only for the test), a real delta between calls of 1.02-1.04s (within tolerance), and the thread genuinely stops after `stop_event.set()` (confirmed: 0 new calls in the following 2.5s). (2) a complete regression: one entire local window (`--mode simulate`, 4 profiles x 3 routes x 2 runs + 1 warm-up) with the new thread integrated into `run_pilot`'s real flow -- finished normally (36 runs, 12 warm-ups, 12 captures, no error, no hang on process exit).

**A new commit, a new freeze, a new tag (the author's request -- the earlier `v9-campanha-oficial-congelada` tag refers to the PREVIOUS commit, which will no longer be used):** see the next paragraph of this same Decision for the commit hash and the new tag's name, and the sha256 check against the 12 real hosts BEFORE the relaunch.

**Written answers, requested by the author before the relaunch (context of the real campaign, not estimates):**

**(a) Relationship between the 7 pre-registered criteria and the complete OIDC-FAPI flow (`opin_flow.py`):** mixed, verified in `evaluate_criteria.py`, never assumed. Criteria 4 (flow counts), 5 (zero errors) and 6 (instrumentation/negotiated profile) read the SAME data from `opin_flow.py`'s real runs (each run's `insurance`/`person` list, plus the combined log) -- they only extract/validate different fields from it (HTTP/JWT counts, absence of error, curveID/dualAuthenticated), never a second independent measurement. Criterion 3 (farthest route) filters this SAME data to a specific route. Criteria 1 (handshake message size), 2 (initcwnd) and 7 (per-route RTT) come from SEPARATE, PARALLEL sources: 1 from the dedicated captures (tcpdump/tshark on its own "settling" connection, never one of each cell's 10 measured runs), 2 from a dedicated TCP probe (`criterio2_probe.py`, only on the highest-RTT route), 7 from a dedicated RTT probe that runs on both sides (`criterio7_rtt.py`, a `probe` channel on the client + a `pcap` channel on the server). Conclusion: some criteria reuse the SAME business-flow data (just another reading of it), some come from deliberately separate additional instrumentation -- never a redundant duplication of the same number.

**(b) Does the raw per-run JSON contain OPINsize's inputs?** Verified against `opinsize_analysis.py` and the aborted attempt's real data (`thesis/results/v9_aborted_attempt_1/`) -- YES, with one DELIBERATE and correct exception, never an omission: JWT sizes (`jwt_sig_breakdown`, raw bytes, classical/PQ separate) and JWK sizes (`jwk_sizes`, per key, kid/kty/use/size_bytes) and PKI/CA (`request_bytes`/`response_bytes` from the real calls to `/root-ca.pem`/`/issuer-ca.pem`) are ALL present in each run's own `runs_raw/{profile}__{route}__run{NN}.json` -- confirmed by reading the real fields. `handshake_bytes` is NOT in the per-run JSON -- it is an explicit, mandatory parameter of `compute_opinsize_variant()` (`--handshake-bytes`), because the Certificate/ClientHello/etc. message size is DETERMINISTIC per profile (same key/certificate, same negotiation) and never varies across a cell's 10 repetitions -- it only needs to be measured ONCE per profile, via the dedicated capture (`criterio1_capturas`), and supplied as a constant when computing that profile's OPINsize. There is no MISSING input -- no code fix was needed here.

**(c) Real size of the 4 `/jwks` responses per profile, measured in the aborted attempt's real data (never estimated):** there are 2 distinct sessions per run, each making 2 `/jwks` calls (one larger + one smaller, always the same pair within the same profile) -- classico: 2x1814B + 2x606B; PQC: 2x4071B + 2x2887B; Hibrido-v8: 2x4366B + 2x3713B; Hibrido-AND: 2x4366B + 2x3713B (identical to Hibrido-v8, consistent with Hibrido-AND fully reusing Hibrido-v8's application/JWKS config, only the TLS mechanism differs).

**(d) What `wasted_seconds` is:** a field in `timing` (`opin_flow.py`/`latency_automation.py`) that accumulates the wall-clock time spent on a DISCARDED ATTEMPT (e.g., a login run that expires with no callback, a PAR retry) -- excluded from the measured `T_fluxo` (`naive_elapsed_seconds - wasted_seconds`) and from the bytes (`calls`), under the same principle: a discarded attempt is measurement-environment noise, never a real flow cost. Behavior: starts at 0.0 on every run, only increases when an attempt is genuinely discarded/repeated (rare -- most runs have `wasted_seconds=0.0`), persisted per run (`timing["wasted_seconds"]`, rounded to 6 places) alongside `timing["retries"]` (a list of which step, which attempt, how many seconds each discard cost).

## 139. A second real crash -- a transient SSH blip with no retry in `run_execution`; retry implemented, tested with an injected failure, a new v3 freeze

**The second crash:** the campaign relaunched with the fixed heartbeat (Decision 138, commit `beced991`) ran from 2026-11-12T20:05:38Z and crashed again, now at a different point -- a `RuntimeError` in `run_execution`, an SSH timeout to the L123 route's client (ca-central-1, <fleet-ip-client-L123-attempt2>) on the `classico/L123` cell's 3rd run.

**The fixed heartbeat worked correctly this time** -- confirmed against the real AWS state: the 12 instances stayed `running` the whole time, none self-stopped. The L123 host was reachable normally again a few minutes later (continuous uptime, never rebooted) -- a transient network/SSH blip, never a persistent problem nor related to the heartbeat.

**Real root cause:** `run_execution` never had any retry logic -- a SINGLE transient SSH failure (`rc=255`, OpenSSH's convention for "I did not complete the connection/command") killed the entire process, even with all hosts healthy and reachable seconds later. This gap existed in the ORIGINAL frozen code (never introduced in this session) -- it had just never been exercised live before this real window.

**State at the moment of the crash:** 40 of 320 runs (12%), 20 of 160 warm-ups, 4 of 32 dedicated captures, 0 invalid-measurement failures. Archived untouched in `thesis/results/v9_aborted_attempt_2/` (see that folder's `README.md`) -- never enters the final analysis. Real orphan containers found and confirmed to belong ONLY to the campaign before removing (no instance/volume/EIP/key/SG touched): `pqc_signer_service_run`+`tls_kem_proxy_run` on the L123 client (from the interrupted run), `v9-mtls` on the sa-east-1 server (the gateway serving that same run) -- all confirmed by name/image before `docker rm -f`, never someone else's container.

**Fix implemented (the author's decision: option b, retry, with a full restart -- never a resume):** `run_execution` gains retry ONLY for TRANSPORT failure (`rc=255`, never the REMOTE command's rc, which is passed through 0-254 -- an application/criterion error raises immediately, same as before, never masked by retry). Up to `EXECUTION_TRANSPORT_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3` attempts, with growing waits between them (`EXECUTION_TRANSPORT_BACKOFF_SECONDS=[2, 5]`) -- each new attempt is already a new SSH connection by construction (`cli.run_ssh` always opens a new `ssh` process), never reusing anything from the previous attempt. The discarded attempt never contributes `stat_before`/`t0`/`t1`/log to the final data (the same principle as `wasted_seconds`, Decision 139 item (d) above) -- only the attempt that succeeds feeds the rest of the result. Once the 3 attempts are exhausted (all transport), the process STOPS with a clear `RuntimeError`, listing each attempt and its reason -- never continuing silently. Each run/warm-up records `retry_attempts` (1 in the common case, no retry) and `retry_failures` (an empty list in the common case, or `{attempt, rc, stderr, at_utc}` per discarded attempt) in its own persisted raw JSON -- `execucao_entry`/`aquecimento_entry` in `run_pilot` also needed the addition (a real finding on review: the original construction of these dicts listed explicit fields, never copied the whole `result` -- the new fields would be silently dropped without this extra adjustment).

**Real diff (insertion/restructuring of the call block only, no other logic touched):** +75/-11 lines in `orchestrator.py` -- the 11 removed lines are exactly the old single call (`stat_before`/`t0`/`proc`/`result`/`t1` sequential, no loop), replaced by a `for attempt in range(1, EXECUTION_TRANSPORT_MAX_ATTEMPTS+1)` that redoes the SAME sequence each attempt, plus 2 new constants and the 2 new fields in both persistence dicts.

**Local test with an INJECTED SSH failure (simulated, never against the 12 real hosts) -- 4 cases, all passing:**
1. A transport failure (`rc=255`) on the 1st attempt, success on the 2nd: exactly 2 SSH calls, `retry_attempts=2`, `retry_failures` with 1 entry (`attempt=1, rc=255`), and the measured data (`insurance`) comes EXCLUSIVELY from the winning attempt -- never a mix.
2. A normal run, zero failure: exactly 1 SSH call, `retry_attempts=1`, `retry_failures=[]` -- byte for byte the same behavior as before this Decision.
3. An APPLICATION error (`rc=1`, never 255): raises `RuntimeError` immediately, ZERO retries -- confirms the transport-vs-application distinction is correct, never masking a real error.
4. Exhausting the 3 attempts (all `rc=255`): a clear `RuntimeError` after exactly 3 calls, the 2s+5s waits genuinely respected (7.0s measured).

**New freeze:** a commit (see the next hash record in this same Decision, or the report sent to the author), a new tag `v9-campanha-oficial-congelada-v3` (the earlier `v9-campanha-oficial-congelada`/`-v2` tags are no longer used). sha256 of all deployed code re-verified on the 12 real hosts before the relaunch.

## 141. The OPINsize's authoritative source for `handshake_bytes` -- the gateway log, never the dedicated capture; complete JWT token vs. signature only, side by side

**The author's request after reviewing the report:** (1) show whether `jwt_sig_bytes_avg` is the signature or the whole token, and recompute with the whole token in parallel; (2) explain and decide the ~238B divergence between the dedicated capture and the gateway log for the handshake term.

**(1) JWT -- confirmed: the original calculation was SIGNATURE ONLY, never the complete token.** Real code: `thesis/scripts/opinsize_v9_oficial.py:84` (`_jwt_sig_bytes`, sums `classical_sig_bytes`+`pq_sig_bytes` from `jwt_sig_breakdown`) and the call loop at `:123-127` (now `:126-137` after the addition below). That number is deliberately Variant B (comparable to Schardong's Eq. 3.1, raw signature only) -- it was never Variant A (complete token, this thesis's own convention) by omission, only because it had never been requested until now in this new tool.

Fixed: the script now computes BOTH variants side by side, never one in place of the other, using the real `jwt_sizes` field (the COMPLETE TOKEN's size as transmitted -- header.payload.signature in base64url, encrypted JWE included where applicable) which already arrives PARALLEL to `jwt_sig_breakdown` in each persisted call (alignment verified across the 320 real runs: 0 misalignments). Real averages (N=28 JWTs/run, 320 runs):

| Profile | JWT signature-only (average) | JWT complete-token (average) |
|---|---|---|
| Classico | 237.71B | 1.209.04B |
| PQC | 3.072.64B | 5.377.39B |
| Hibrido-v8 | 3.310.36B | 7.041.32B |
| Hibrido-AND | 3.310.36B | 7.041.32B |

(The 1,385B figure the author cited from v7 is the same order of magnitude as the 1.209.04B measured here for Classico-complete-token -- consistent with v7 already using the complete-token convention, never signature only; the small difference is expected, a different flow/claims between v7 and v9, never investigated byte for byte.)

**(2) handshake_bytes -- decision: the gateway log (`handshakeBytesIn`+`handshakeBytesOut`) becomes the AUTHORITATIVE source, the dedicated capture stays informational only.** Reason: it is FIRST-PARTY instrumentation -- measured by the VERY process doing the handshake, at the real boundary of `crypto/tls.Handshake()`, never inferred from an external packet capture that depends on tshark's TLS 1.3 dissector CORRECTLY marking every post-handshake message type. Most likely hypothesis for the ~238B gap (constant, measured across the 4 profiles -- never proportional to the handshake size, which points to a FIXED-size element, never a percentage fraction): a server `NewSessionTicket` message, which TLS 1.3 sends inside the SAME generic "Application Data" record type that carries application data -- the filter used in the dedicated capture (tshark's handshake-type column) does not mark it, so it never enters the per-message sum; Go's OWN counter, which sums raw bytes at the handshake boundary with no dependence on external reclassification, probably includes it. **This hypothesis was NOT confirmed by byte-for-byte inspection of the pcap/keylog** -- recorded as the most likely explanation given the evidence (a fixed, never proportional gap), not as a certainty.

Real values (average of handshakeBytesIn+Out, N=488 real mTLS connections per profile -- the 320 official runs + warm-ups):

| Profile | handshake_bytes (gateway, authoritative) | handshake_bytes (capture, informational) | gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Classico | 3.125B | 2,887B | 238B |
| PQC | 21.606B | 21,368B | 238B |
| Hibrido-v8 | 16.949B | 16,711B | 238B |
| Hibrido-AND | 24.080B | 23,841B | 238B |

`thesis/scripts/opinsize_v9_oficial.py` (sha256 `dab168dc5ab4842f60b1e736756af8d2321a6f68247b5bdfb3aa94567fa7e1da`) updated: `_handshake_bytes_from_gateway_log()` (new, reads `piloto_combined.log`) is the source used in the terms; `_handshake_bytes_from_capture()` preserved only as an informational field (`handshake_bytes_capture_derived_informativo`), never again used in the calculation. The complete result recomputed in `thesis/results/v9/opinsize_v9_oficial.json`.

## 142. Classico's ClientHello: 308B measured (real AWS) vs. a 336B baseline (local test) -- a formal deviation, a likely cause

**A finding from the author, verified:** Classico measured ClientHello=308B, reproducible across the official campaign's 8 routes (`criterio1_capturas/classico_*.log`, stream 0, all 8 captures), against `CLIENTHELLO_BASELINE["classico"]=336` (`thesis/results/v9/integration/evaluate_criteria.py:175`), 0 tolerance -- a FAIL on criterion 1. The other 3 profiles match EXACTLY their respective baselines (PQC 1.779B, Hibrido-v8 1.876B, Hibrido-AND 1.858B, 0 deviation) -- the problem is EXCLUSIVE to Classico.

**Real cause of the 336B baseline:** never measured against the real campaign -- it comes from a LOCAL loopback test (`measure.sh`/T6, Decision 15, "tickets off"), recorded in `thesis/results/v9/DECISIONS.md` around line 1730: "Classico 332+4=336, real frame 341 (336 + 5B TLS record header)". It is a bench calibration, local, from an earlier round -- never re-validated against a genuinely real AWS deployment before this campaign.

**Verdict:** the real MEASUREMENT (308B, reproduced across 8 independent routes, never a single sample) is reliable; it is the BASELINE (336B) that is probably stale for Classico specifically -- some 28B difference between the T6 local test's conditions and the real deployment (plausible candidates, NEVER confirmed by extension-by-extension inspection: a TLS extension present/absent, or a different SNI/session_id size -- the other 3 profiles have a ClientHello dominated by the ML-KEM key_share, on the order of thousands of bytes, where a 28B deviation is invisible/within noise; only Classico, with a small ClientHello and only classical groups, has zero margin for any difference). **Not investigated byte for byte this round** -- recorded as a formal deviation, pending the author's decision on whether to recalibrate `CLIENTHELLO_BASELINE["classico"]` to 308 (or investigate the exact extension first).
