Local ClientHello = 336B (matches the baseline exactly), the same SNI "mtls", the same 32B `session_id`, the same 11 extensions in the same order as the real capture -- only the CONTENT of 3 extensions differs: `cipher_suites` (26B local vs 6B real, +20B -- the Go test client `thesis/results/v9/integration/proxy/main.go:227` announces 13 suites including 10 legacy TLS 1.2 ones even with MinVersion/MaxVersion fixed to TLS 1.3, because Go does not filter the announced list by the minimum version when `CipherSuites` is not restricted), `signature_algorithms` (+6B) and `signature_algorithms_cert` (+2B). Exact sum: 20+6+2=28B, reconciling 100% of the difference. Root cause: the campaign's real client (`opin_flow.py`, Python, `requests.Session`+pyOpenSSL) and T6's calibration client (the Go `proxy` binary, used only by `measure.sh`, never in the real campaign) are different TLS stacks. **This is not an error in the real measurement (308B) -- it is an expected difference between two distinct TLS clients.** `CLIENTHELLO_BASELINE["classico"]` was not changed (that would mean changing a pre-registered criterion); criterion 1 remains FAIL.

The check script (`verify_consolidated_report_v9.py`) rerun after all fixes: 0 divergences. A final grep for "v7"/"v8"/"inherited" in the report: 0 occurrences (the only "hibrido-v8" occurrence in the repository related to this phase is the functional string cited in item (1), outside the report's prose).

## 147. Real variation of handshake_bytes (min/median/mean/max), defining JWT_Sig as Schardong's Equation 3.1 (p.60), and OPINsize recomputed with the raw signature + raw key material as the main variant -- the author's request, no new collection

**The author's request, two rounds:** (1) confirm how `handshake_bytes` is obtained (mean/median/single value) and its real variation among a run's 6 connections and among the 320 runs; (2) promote the JWT signature-only variant to OPINsize's main definition (as it corresponds to `JWT_Sig` from Schardong's Equation 3.1, p.60), explain why the Hybrid/Control average is 3.310.36B and not 3.565B, extract the raw public-key-material size from the 4 `/jwks` per profile, recompute OPINsize (3/4 terms) with the raw signature+key, and record all of it in the consolidated report with the complete-token variant as supplementary. No new collection, no infrastructure change -- only reading and recomputing the already-persisted `piloto_calls.json`/`piloto_combined.log`.

**(1) handshake_bytes: confirmed it is the MEAN (`statistics.mean`, `opinsize_v9_oficial.py:88-115`), never the median nor a fixed value.** Recomputed by isolating each of the 320 real runs' `start_utc`/`end_utc` window (480 connections/profile, strictly official, excluding the 8 warm-up points the production script adds to the 488): the recomputed mean matches the official script's in all 4 profiles (difference <0.01B). Within the same run, the 6 connections use the SAME client certificate and the SAME TLS parameters -- there is no systematic difference by connection position/type (tested across the 320 runs, a histogram by position 1-6).

| Profile | Min | Median | Mean (used in OPINsize) | Max | Runs with all 6 connections identical |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Classico | 3.125 | 3.125 | 3.125 | 3.367 | 79/80 |
| PQC | 21.606 | 21.606 | 21.606 | 21.606 | 80/80 |
| Hibrido-v8 | 16.949 | 16.949 | 16.949 | 17.183 | 79/80 |
| Hibrido-AND | 24.079 | 24.079 | 24.080 | 24.313 | 78/80 |

The few outliers (1 run in Classico, 1 in Hibrido-v8, 2 in Hibrido-AND, 0 in PQC) occur at different positions from each other (never always the same one of the 6 connections) -- compatible with normal TLS handshake jitter, a one-off cause not investigated (does not affect the mean used in OPINsize's term).

**(2) JWT_Sig = Schardong's Equation 3.1 (p.60), RECORDED ON THE AUTHOR'S DIRECT INSTRUCTION -- not verified by this document against Schardong's thesis (not present in this repository).** Real mapping of the 28 JWTs/run by `src` (constant across the 4 profiles, recomputed from `piloto_calls.json`): 16 resource-layer tokens (14 `CallProtectedResource` + 2 `CallConsentEndpointWithBearerToken`), 6 client assertions (4 from `CallTokenEndpoint` + 2 from `CallPAREndpoint`), 2 request objects (`CallPAREndpoint`), 2 JARM, 2 id_token in JWE (`CallTokenEndpoint`) -- sums to 28, matching exactly the author's breakdown.

Bytes counted by `_jwt_sig_bytes` (`opinsize_v9_oficial.py:118-126`): `classical_sig_bytes + pq_sig_bytes`, both from `jwt_sig_breakdown`, never from the raw token. By real construction (`jwt_sig_breakdown`, constant across the 320 runs):
- `classic_only` (Classico): RSA-PSS signature only (PS256), 256B.
- `pqc_pure` (PQC): ML-DSA-65 signature only, 3.309B.
- `payload_extension` (Hybrid/Control, 24 of the 28 tokens -- the 16 resource ones + 6 client assertions + 2 request objects): RSA-PSS (256B) + ML-DSA-65 (3.309B) embedded as an extra claim in the payload = 3.565B.
- `strong_nesting` (Hybrid/Control, only the 2 JARM): the same sum 256B+3.309B=3.565B, only the STRUCTURE differs (a signed JWT nested inside another, instead of an extra claim) -- the signature byte count is identical.
- `jwe` (the 2 id_token, all profiles): `classical_sig_bytes`/`pq_sig_bytes` both `None`->0 -- the id_token is encrypted (JWE/AEAD), never signed via JWS, so there is no signature to count.

**Why the Hybrid/Control average is 3.310.36B and not 3.565B:** of the 28 tokens/run, 26 (24 `payload_extension` + 2 `strong_nesting`) have a 3.565B signature and 2 (`jwe`, the id_tokens) have 0B -- `(26x3.565 + 2x0)/28 = 92.690/28 = 3.310.36B`. The 2 unsigned id_tokens dilute the average. Same reasoning for Classico: `(26x256+2x0)/28=237.71B`; for PQC: `(26x3.309+2x0)/28=3.072.64B`. Identical value between Hibrido-v8 and Hibrido-AND confirmed: the token signature is an application layer (JWS/JWE), independent of the TLS/mTLS profile transporting the call.

**JWK: raw public key material, decoded, with no JSON envelope** -- `baseline_automation.extract_jwk_sizes` (`baseline_automation.py:385-425`) already computes exactly this (`size_bytes` = the decoded bytes of `n`/`pub`/`pk_hybrid`, never the envelope's JSON), confirmed constant across the 320 runs:

| Profile | 1st call/session (AS) | 2nd call/session (RS) | Average per call (N_JWK=4) |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Classico | RSA sig 256B + RSA enc 256B = 512B | RSA sig 256B | 384 |
| PQC | AKP(ML-DSA-65) sig 1,952B + RSA enc 256B = 2,208B | AKP sig 1,952B | 2.080 |
| Hibrido-v8 / Hibrido-AND | HYBRID sig 2,208B + RSA enc 256B = 2.464B | HYBRID sig 2,208B + RSA sig 256B = 2.464B | 2.464 |

**OPINsize recomputed, raw signature + raw key (gateway's handshake_bytes, Decision 141, unchanged):**

| Profile | 3 terms (no PKI) | 4 terms (with PKI) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Classico | 26.941,88 | 35.793,88 |
| PQC | 223.989,92 | 256.429,92 |
| Hibrido-v8 (Control) | 204.240,08 | 242.008,08 |
| Hibrido-AND (Hybrid) | 247.026,08 | 255.878,08 |

The complete-token + full-`/jwks`-response variant (this thesis's own convention) is preserved as supplementary, with the SAME values already recorded in Decision 141/143 (unchanged: only the main/supplementary role was swapped).

**Consolidated report updated** (`Consolidated_Metrics_Report_FINAL.md`, Executive Summary and Section 3): the signature-only+raw-key variant is now the main one (citing `JWT_Sig` from Schardong's Eq. 3.1, p.60, on the author's instruction), complete-token+full-`/jwks`-response becomes supplementary, with an explicit note that the Hybrid-vs-Control ORDER INVERTS between the two variants (Hybrid > Control in the raw signature, from paying the PQ signature live twice per handshake; Control > Hybrid in the complete token, from paying more extension/token bytes on every call) -- both effects are real, neither "corrects" the other. A local-only change in this revision, no commit or push (not requested by the author this round).

## 148. A real measurement failure in the Hybrid's PKI_bytes (the ML-DSA-65 pair never distributed), a fix, complete local tests, and an independent finding about criterion 1 (ClientHello) that requires a relaunch

**1. A real, audited failure.** The CA distribution endpoint (`/root-ca.pem`/`/issuer-ca.pem`) served, for `hibrido-and`, only the RSA pair (identical to Classico) -- never the ML-DSA-65 chain that the Hybrid's two-independent-chain, dual-signature design requires (`business_server.go:243-252`, `realCAFilesForProfile`, the old `default` branch included `hibrido-and`). A complete audit of the client, proxy, gateway, AS/RS and orchestrator found no other point of the same type: the real mTLS handshake (`proxy/main.go:278-311`, `dualClientConfig`) already verifies and transmits both chains in both directions, with a real AND gate (`and.patch`, `handshake_client_tls13.go`); the application layer (AS/RS) deliberately uses `CRYPTO_PROFILE=hybrid` for `hibrido-and` (`orchestrator.py:443-458`, Decision 50, already documented, by design, not a failure).

**2. Fix applied and tested locally (local Docker, no AWS).** `business_server.go` (`realCAFilesForProfile`/a new `readAndConcatCAFiles`) now concatenates `root_ca.crt`+`root_ca_pqc.crt` (and `issuer_ca.crt`+`issuer_ca_pqc.crt`) for `hibrido-and` -- the existing PQC pair, the same file the PQC profile already serves (identical SHA-256 confirmed). `opin_flow.py` (`verify_ca_chain`, a new `_split_pem_certificates`) gained a branch for `hibrido-and` that splits the bundle's two blocks and runs the TWO already-existing verifications (RSA against `ca.crt`, self-signed ML-DSA-65 + issuer signed by the root). Classico and PQC unchanged, confirmed by test.

**Go: `go vet ./...` clean; `go build` ok; a new `ca_handler_test.go` (3 tests: per-profile file mapping, the Hybrid's bundle with exactly 2 CERTIFICATE blocks in RSA->ML-DSA-65 order, and EXACT `response_bytes` via real HTTP/raw TCP across the 4 profiles) -- all PASS. A real finding while writing the test: the gateway's response uses `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` (never `Content-Length`) when the client does not request `Connection: close` -- confirmed against the REAL gateway+proxy running locally (Docker, complete topology: a `hibrido-and` gateway + a real relay-mode proxy, a real dual handshake `dualAuthenticated=true curve=SecP384r1MLKEM1024`), not merely inferred: the header overhead is EXACTLY 103B, independent of the body size (including the Hybrid's new 5-digit bodies, 10.107/10,127B) because "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" has a fixed size -- there is no risk of the overhead changing due to the digit count of a `Content-Length` that never exists in this response.

**response_bytes confirmed real (real gateway+proxy, local Docker, loopback):** Hybrid `/root-ca.pem`=10,210B, `/issuer-ca.pem`=10,230B (body 10.107/10,127B + 103B of headers) -- identical to what was calculated from the files in the earlier round. Classico and PQC confirmed unchanged (2.209/2.217 and 8.104/8.116).

**Python: `verify_ca_chain` tested against the 4 profiles' real bundles (all pass) and 3 negative cases** (the ML-DSA-65 half with 1 base64 character swapped -- fails; swapped order, issuer in root's place -- fails; a bundle with only 1 certificate -- fails), all raising `SignatureVerificationError` as expected, using the real `pqc-signer` service (local Docker) for ML-DSA-65 verification, never mocked.

**4-term OPINsize recalculated (mTLS/JWT/JWK unchanged, Decision 147):** Hybrid goes from 255.878,08 (official, incomplete RSA pair) to **287.906,08** with the ML-DSA-65 pair included -- 12.3% ABOVE PQC (256.429,92), no longer practically equal.

**3. An independent finding about criterion 1 (ClientHello), out of scope for the PKI fix but needing to be resolved before any relaunch:**

a) Confirmed by code AND by a real local run (Docker, complete gateway+proxy topology, a real handshake captured): whoever dials the real mTLS connection against the gateway, across the 4 profiles, IS THE GO PROXY (`thesis/results/v9/integration/proxy/`, relay mode, `-listen`), never Python directly -- `orchestrator.py:657-662` (`_client_env`) unconditionally sets `V9_HARNESS=1` for every real client run, which makes `opin_flow.py` (`_USE_TLS_KEM_PROXY`/`start_tls_kem_proxy`) always point to the local proxy (`127.0.0.1:TLS_KEM_PROXY_PORT`), never directly to the gateway. Python only speaks TLS with the local proxy (a disposable self-signed certificate, irrelevant for security); the proxy is the one doing the real handshake, with real `RootCAs`/`Dual.RootCAs` (no `InsecureSkipVerify`), against the real gateway.

b) **Classico's ClientHello, now captured locally from the REAL `proxy` binary (the same code as the official campaign, never rebuilt nor assumed), matches EXACTLY what was measured on AWS: tcp.len=313B, handshake body=304B (308B including the message header), SNI="mtls" -- identical, byte for byte, to what `criterio1_capturas/classico_*.log` had already captured in the real campaign.** The EARLIER local reproduction (336B, cited in Section 10 of the already-published report) used the cached Docker image `mockopin-v9-measure:latest` -- that image was STALE (28B larger): rebuilding the proxy from the CURRENT source code (the same as the official campaign) and capturing again, the result drops to 304B, identical to the real one. The 28B difference between the stale image and the current code is explained, byte for byte, by three ClientHello extensions: cipher suites (13 suites/26B -> 3 suites/6B, -20B), `signature_algorithms` (28B->22B, -6B) and `supported_versions` (5B->3B, -2B) -- all three are a symptom of the SAME commit, `836ff11a` ("Decisions 118/119": fixes Classico to TLS13..TLS13 on the client, `proxy/main.go`), which changed `MinVersion` from TLS12 to TLS13 only for Classico. **Conclusion: this is not, and never was, a Python-vs-Go difference -- it is a calibration image (`mockopin-v9-measure`) never rebuilt after commit 836ff11a, mistakenly used as if it were representative of the real client.** The explanation recorded in Section 10 of the already-published report ("two DIFFERENT TLS stacks, Python+pyOpenSSL vs. the calibration Go") is WRONG on both points: the campaign's real client is the Go proxy (item 3a), and the cause of the 28B is a stale image, not a stack choice.

c) The reference value of 336B (`CLIENTHELLO_BASELINE["classico"]`, `evaluate_criteria.py:175`) was measured via `measure.sh` back at the time of Decision 29/30 -- BEFORE commit `836ff11a` (Decisions 118/119) fixed TLS13 for Classico. The baseline was never updated after that fix.

d) **A new campaign, with the current code (without touching the proxy/gateway TLS), will measure 304B again for Classico -- and criterion 1 will FAIL AGAIN, for the SAME reason as always (0 tolerance, a stale baseline), now with the exact cause definitively proven (item b), no longer just a plausible explanation.** There is no pending fix in the proxy -- the proxy's code is already correct and is what will run. The only possible fix is updating `CLIENTHELLO_BASELINE["classico"]` from 336 to 308 (or 304, depending on which of the two numbers the criterion actually compares -- to be checked in `evaluate_criteria.py` before any edit) -- a pre-registration change, the author's decision, not done here.

e) **Reassessing "none of the 7 criteria needs reassessment" (an earlier answer):** that sentence remains true REGARDING THE PKI FIX (item 1/2 of this decision) -- confirmed that handshake_bytes and the ClientHello are entirely unrelated to the CA distribution endpoint, no test changed. But criterion 1 has a REAL, INDEPENDENT problem (item d above), which already existed before this round and which a new campaign will re-expose with no additional code change -- the earlier sentence did not cover this finding because it had not yet been investigated. The author's decision is needed: fix the baseline before relaunching (criterion 1 would pass), or relaunch as is and accept another pre-registered FAIL (same cause, now exhaustively documented).

**Containers/images used, all local, none destroyed from the official data record:** `mockopin-v9-toolchain`, `mockopin-v9-gateway`/`-proxy` (tags `-localtest`, discarded after use), `mockopin-v9-measure` (an existing cache, read-only use), `mockopin-pqc-signer`. No action against AWS, no account touched, no file in `thesis/results/v9/campaign/oficial_raw/` or the already-published report/opinsize altered this round.

The unit confirmed first: `evaluate_criteria.py` never compares a raw `tls.handshake.length` -- `_message_sizes_legacy` (line 427) and the per-stream path (line 557) compute `clienthello_bytes = tls.handshake.length + 4` (4B for the handshake message header: 1B type + 3B length) BEFORE comparing against `CLIENTHELLO_BASELINE` (line 386). For Classico, current code: `tls.handshake.length=304` -> `clienthello_bytes=308`.

**Text correction (Decision 158, the author's request):** this Decision's original sentence cited `criterio1_capturas/classico_*.log` as the evidence that 304/308 "matches the campaign's real data". That was WRONG -- rechecked this round, the 3 `criterio1_capturas/classico_*.log` files that exist in the repository show "sizes"=332 (not 304), because they are from a capture BEFORE this same commit `836ff11a` -- no file with 304/308 for Classico was ever committed. ## 152. Classico's HTTP overhead on the 2 CA endpoints is 97B, not 103B -- `TestDirectoryHandlerResponseBytes` fixed with Docker back, Decision 151's answer key recalculated (2026-11-13)

**1. A finding, with Docker back.** `TestDirectoryHandlerResponseBytes` failed for Classico: expected 1.809/1.823, observed **1.803/1.817**. Root cause confirmed live (a real gateway + a real Python client, not just the Go test): the `net/http` internal constant `bufferBeforeChunkingSize = 2048` makes the server choose the response framing based on the body size at the handler's first (and only) `Write()` -- a body that fits entirely in the buffer (< 2048B) allows computing `Content-Length` directly (an overhead of **97B**: `Content-Type`+`Date`+`Content-Length`); a larger body forces `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` (an overhead of **103B**), because the total size is not yet known when writing starts. Classico's new bodies (1,706B/1,720B, the RSA-2048 pair from Decision 151) happened to fall below 2048B -- the other 3 profiles (PQC 8,001B/8,013B, Control 9,337B/9,341B, Hybrid 9,707B/9,733B) stay above, so they remain chunked/103B, untouched. **Not a bug, not a handler regression, no framing was forced** -- correct, expected `net/http` behavior reacting to a smaller body.

**2. The test fixed, not the handler.** `ca_handler_test.go`: the case table gained a 4th field, `wantFraming` (`"content-length"` for Classico, `"chunked"` for the other 3); `rawResponseBytes()` now also returns the observed framing mode (`"chunked"`/`"content-length"`/`"neither (EOF-terminated)"`, read from the same raw-response parsing that already existed), compared against `wantFraming` -- a future `net/http` behavior change (or a new certificate crossing the 2048B threshold again, in any profile) is caught structurally, not only by a byte count that could be misread. Classico's expected values updated to 1.803/1.817. The file's header comment rewritten: the old claim of a "universal 103B overhead" removed, replaced by the explanation of `bufferBeforeChunkingSize` and Classico's exception. **The handler (`directoryHandler`/`business_server.go`) NOT changed** -- no framing was forced. Reconfirmed via Docker (`mockopin-v9-toolchain:latest`): `go vet`/`go build -trimpath`/`go test -v ./...` -- **all PASS**, including the new `wantFraming` assertions (Classico `framing=content-length`/97B; PQC, Control and Hybrid `framing=chunked`/103B).

**1. A real finding, running the complete flow across the 4 profiles (an item from the earlier round):** classico and pqc passed; hibrido-v8 and hibrido-and failed. hibrido-and was an operational cause (a stale gateway image -- see Decision 154). **hibrido-v8 is a real code bug**, independently confirmed via `pytest thesis/scripts/tests/test_verify_ca_chain.py` (with no dependence on any Docker round besides `pqc-signer`): `verify_ca_chain()` (`thesis/scripts/opin_flow.py`) had exactly 2 branches with a dedicated `if` ("hibrido-and", "pqc") and a `default` that Decision 151/152 changed to assume classico's NEW structure (a self-signed root). "hybrid"/"hibrido-v8" never had its own branch -- it fell into the `default` by accident, and `root_ca_hybrid.crt` (never migrated, still signed by a separate `ca.crt`, not self-signed) was rejected with an error citing "root_ca_rsa2048" (the wrong branch's message). Never caught before because this file's 5 tests that need `pqc-signer` stayed SKIP the whole session (Docker unavailable) and were never rerun once it came back.

Any `crypto_profile` outside the 4 known ones now raises an explicit `SignatureVerificationError` -- no profile falls into any branch by accident anymore. `_verify_cert_signed_by_mldsa65` checks `hasattr(issuer_pubkey, "public_bytes_raw")` before use -- a wrong type gets a clean rejection, never a crash. **13 tests (8 old + 5 new: hibrido-v8 under both names, classico under both names, an unknown profile, an improper hibrido-v8<->classico swap, a unit helper for ML-DSA-65 against an RSA key) -- 13/13 PASS, 0 skip.**

## 154. Autonomous overnight local validation -- the internal carve-out broke 100% of calls (wrong certificate), fixed; the complete real flow across the 4 profiles passes for the first time; the 7th connection explained (a probing artifact, the right count is 6); the pinned venv only matches hashes inside amazonlinux:2023; 1 real incomplete-profile bug found and fixed in the gate; the lambdas image digest obtained (2026-11-13/14, the author's overnight authorization, no cloud action at all)

**1. Root cause of the real flow's total block: the internal carve-out presented a CLIENT certificate as the SERVER identity.** Running the complete flow across the 4 profiles right after rebuilding the images (still without this fix), all 4 profiles failed identically on the internal `getConsent()` (AS->RS) with `unsuitable certificate purpose` on the Node side. Cause confirmed with direct evidence (`openssl x509 -noout -purpose`): `attachInternalCallerCarveOut` (`business_server.go`) loaded `mock-service-os/certs/mtls.crt` as the SERVER identity on the `matls-api.local` hop -- but that file is generated by `certs/main.go`'s `generateCert`/`generateCertWithBits` with `ExtKeyUsage=ClientAuth` ONLY, the same template shared with `op.crt`/`client_one.crt`/`client_two.crt` (all genuinely used as CLIENT identity elsewhere). Go's `crypto/tls` never deliberately checked the EKU, so this worked silently the project's whole life; Node's TLS, now with `rejectUnauthorized=true` (this same round's fix, Decision 151), started checking and rejecting.

**Fixed WITHOUT touching `mtls.crt` nor the shared template** (several certs it signs ARE measured -- JWK/certificate sizes feed real OPINsize terms, never risked by this fix). A new function, `generateInternalServerCert` (`certs/main.go`, an isolated `-internal-server-name` flag, loads the EXISTING CA via `loadCACert` -- never regenerates `ca.crt`) generates `mtls_internal_server.crt`/.key (RSA-2048, `ExtKeyUsage=ServerAuth` only, signed by the same real `ca.crt`), and `attachInternalCallerCarveOut` now loads this new file. 2 new Go tests (`internal_carveout_test.go`) confirm `ServerAuth` (never `ClientAuth`) on the certificate the carve-out returns, across the 4 profiles -- 5/5 Go tests pass. Commit `bfd2b489`.

**2. The complete real flow across the 4 profiles -- PASS on ALL of them, for the first time this session (a `--no-cache` rebuild of the gateway from commit `bfd2b489`):**

Cause: `opin_flow.start_tls_kem_proxy()`'s own readiness probe (`_wait_for_tls_kem_proxy_ready_detached`) opens a real mTLS connection through the proxy just to confirm it is listening, ONCE per block startup (a proxy restart), never once per run. A finding before the measurement: the 3 `criterio1_capturas/classico_*.log` files already in the repository (in `piloto/dados_oficiais/.../raw/`) show **332B/1513B** (the PRE-fix values) -- none of them is evidence of the current value (308B/1485B) Decision 149 cited as "measured by the official campaign"; the official campaign genuinely used these values (confirmed in the campaign's CSV/JSON), but the specific proof file cited in `evaluate_criteria.py:181`'s comment does not exist in the repository -- the citation is imprecise, even though the VALUE itself is correct (now confirmed by a fresh, independent measurement).

- Fixed fields: legacy_version(2) + random(32) + session_id_len(1) + session_id(32) + cipher_suites_len(2) + cipher_suites(6, 3 TLS1.3 suites) + compression_len(1) + compression(1) + extensions_len(2) = **79B**
- Extensions (11, each 4B header + body): server_name(13) + ec_point_formats(6) + renegotiation_info(5) + extended_master_secret(4) + signed_certificate_timestamp(4) + status_request(9) + supported_groups(8) + signature_algorithms(26) + signature_algorithms_cert(36) + supported_versions(7) + key_share(107) = **225B**
- 79 + 225 = **304B** of Client Hello body = `tls.handshake.length` (confirmed by tshark). +4B of message header (type+length) = **308B total, exactly `CLIENTHELLO_BASELINE["classico"]`**. MATCHES -- no fix needed.

Side note: the patched client announces `mldsa44/65/87` in `signature_algorithms`/`signature_algorithms_cert` even in the Classico profile (and.patch does not filter by profile) -- inflates the ClientHello relative to a stock Go, but this is the REAL deployed binary, so the measured number (308) is the right number for this implementation, not an artifact to fix.

In other words: the BASELINE today was fixed by the CLIENT's counter (proxy), not by the GATEWAY's counter as the methodology's specification textually requires ("handshake_bytes read from the gateway's counter") -- and the gateway's counter, now measured live, diverges from the baseline by exactly the size of the first post-handshake request, suggesting that the server-side `Handshake()`'s (buffered) read is pulling connection bytes that, semantically, already belong to the next message. Tested only in `measure` mode (a dedicated binary); `business` mode (what the real campaign uses) uses the same `countingConn`+post-Handshake-snapshot pattern, so the same effect is expected there, but this was NOT confirmed live against the complete stack (would need `REAL_CERTS_DIR`/an auth upstream, outside this targeted check's scope). No line of code was changed by this finding -- recorded for the author's decision.

## 159. The handshake counter fixed (a TLS-record-aware limiter in countingConn), the gateway re-pinned, a decisive check (4 profiles, 2 client modes, 240 connections): ZERO difference in 100%

**1. Fix implemented, without touching crypto/tls, and.patch nor the toolchain pin.** `countingConn` (`gateway/main.go`) gained a `framingActive` field (true from `Accept()` until `Handshake()` returns) and a `readFramed()` method: while active, `Read()` never asks the raw `net.Conn` for more bytes than remain in the current TLS record -- it reads the 5B header (type+version+length, always in the clear, RFC 8446 Sec 5.1) and then exactly the declared body, never more, using `net.Conn.Read`'s own guarantee of never returning more bytes than the passed buffer. `disableRecordFraming()` called in `gateway/main.go:handleConn` and `gateway/business_server.go:acceptBusinessConn` (the campaign's REAL path) right after `Handshake()` returns -- from then on, unrestricted passthrough, same as before. Commit `879661e0`.

**2. Tests (items 1a/1b), both passing:**
- `counting_conn_test.go`: synthetic TLS record flows (2 "handshake" records + 1 "application data" record, simulating the client's post-handshake write), fed by a fake `net.Conn` with 8 different fragmentations (byte by byte, all at once, at each record's boundary, boundary +-1) -- all produce the SAME `in` count, zero bytes of the next record counted while framing is active.
- `counting_conn_handshake_test.go`: a REAL TLS 1.3 handshake over TCP loopback (not `net.Pipe`, which would never reproduce the OS buffer race), the client writes immediately after its own `Handshake()` returns (the exact race that caused the leak), **100 iterations, all 100 with the same count** (1531B, identical -- this test's own synthetic config, not comparable to any real profile).

**3. Decisive check (item 1c), an agent with no history, 4 profiles x 2 client modes (immediate write and a 150ms delay) x 30 connections = 240 connections, against a real decrypted capture:**

| Profile | Decrypted capture IN/OUT | Gateway log IN/OUT | Difference (60 connections) |
|---|---|---|---|
| classico | 1485 / 1640 | 1485 / 1640 | **0 in 60/60** |
| pqc | 10728 / 10878 | 10728 / 10878 | **0 in 60/60** |
| hibrido-v8 | 8397 / 8552 | 8397 / 8552 | **0 in 60/60** |
| hibrido-and | 11902 / 12177 | 11902 / 12177 | **0 in 60/60** |

**240/240 connections, ZERO difference, across the 2 client modes, across the 4 profiles.** Satisfies the conditional continuation's pre-condition (a).

**4. Re-pinning the gateway in PINS.json.** A `--no-cache` rebuild from the clean working tree at commit `879661e0`, 2 independent builds under dedicated tags (`:repro1`/`:repro2`, never directly on `:latest`): the extracted binary IDENTICAL in both (`sha256:9d21b901...906618`) -- `binary_sha256_reproducible` reconfirmed `true`. `tar_sha256` and `rootfs_layers[1]` (the binary's layer) changed, as expected; `rootfs_layers[0]` (base) and `rootfs_layers[2]` (certs) identical to the earlier pin. `go_version_m_sha256`/`go_version_m_text` identical (toolchain/build flags unchanged). `image_id` updated (informational, never verified, Decision 68).

**4b. An additional finding: `measure` ALSO needed re-pinning.** Checking "only the gateway changed across the build contexts" (requested by item 5/the conditional continuation): `measure/Dockerfile` COPIES the gateway/proxy source code (`COPY gateway ./gateway`) as a build INPUT, to assemble its standalone diagnostic harness -- so, even with not a single line of `measure/Dockerfile`/`measure.sh` changed, the CONTENT of the `/usr/local/bin/gateway` binary embedded in that image changes along with the countingConn fix. Confirmed by 2 independent `--no-cache` builds: `tar_sha256` and 3 of the 6 `rootfs_layers` come out different between the two builds (the same BuildKit timestamp-metadata volatility Decision 101 already documented for this harness, now across 3 layers instead of 1) -- but the `/usr/local/bin/gateway` binary extracted from BOTH builds is byte for byte IDENTICAL to each other AND identical to the standalone gateway's `binary_sha256` re-pinned above (`9d21b901...906618`); `/usr/local/bin/proxy` also identical across both builds (`07c9fb03...edb85`). ## 161. Fixing the failure classification (a real finding from the re-audit), investigating the proxy's error signal (report only), and a theoretical counter limitation documented

**1. Fixing `classify_failure()`, commit `ab391cc8`.** The re-audit found that `isinstance(exc, requests.exceptions.ConnectionError)` matches `SSLError` and `ProxyError` (both are subclasses) -- a real cryptographic/TLS failure became "network_transport" (retried) instead of "fail_closed". Fixed: `_NETWORK_TRANSPORT_EXACT_TYPES` is now a `frozenset` of CONCRETE types (`requests.exceptions.ConnectionError`/`ConnectTimeout`/`ReadTimeout`/`Timeout`, builtins `ConnectionError`/`ConnectionReset`/`Refused`/`Aborted`/`BrokenPipe`/`TimeoutError`), compared by `type(exc) in set` (the exact type, never `isinstance`) -- a subclass outside the list falls into `fail_closed` by exclusion, even inheriting from something on the list. 74 new tests (`test_classify_failure_exhaustive.py`): introspects at runtime ALL classes of `requests.exceptions` (pinned to `requests==2.32.5`), `urllib3.exceptions`, and relevant builtins/ssl, builds an instance of each, and compares the REAL verdict (never a hand-written table in parallel) against the expected one. `SSLError`/`ProxyError` explicitly confirmed `fail_closed`, with a dedicated regression test. 91/91 passing (the exhaustive suite + the existing retry tests).

**2. Investigating the proxy's error signal -- REPORT ONLY, the proxy was not changed.** Question: how does the local proxy (`integration/proxy/relay.go`) signal an upstream failure to Python (TLS/chain verification, Hybrid dual failure, connection, timeout)? Answer, confirmed by code reading AND a live reproduction: **NONE of the 4 causes generates an HTTP 502/504 response (nor any other status) -- a `grep` for "502"/"504"/"Bad Gateway"/"Gateway Timeout" across all of `integration/proxy/` and the legacy `tls_kem_proxy` returns zero real occurrences** (only a false positive in a base64 certificate fragment). `handleRelayConn` (relay.go) handles the 3 upstream-hop failure causes (`tls.Dial` failed, `cs.CurveID != want`, hibrido-and with `DualAuthenticated=false`) IDENTICALLY: `log.Printf(...)` followed by `return` -- closes the LOCAL connection (hop 1, Python<->proxy) abruptly, with no body or header bytes, not distinguishing one cause from another.

**A live reproduction** (a real classico gateway + a real relay deliberately pointed at the incompatible `hibrido-and` profile, to force a real TLS failure on the upstream hop): the relay logged `dial upstream mtls:18443: remote error: tls: handshake failure` -- and Python, on the other side, received `requests.exceptions.ConnectionError(ProtocolError('Connection aborted.', ConnectionAbortedError(...)))`. **Not an `SSLError`, not a 502/504 status -- the EXACT type item 1's fix above classifies as `network_transport`.** In other words: even after fixing `SSLError`/`ProxyError`, a REAL cryptographic/profile failure occurring on the proxy's upstream hop (not on the local Python<->proxy hop, which uses a separate disposable certificate and almost never fails for a cryptographic reason) is still, today, INDISTINGUISHABLE from a generic network failure -- and would be retried, not aborted fail-closed.

**A minimal fix proposed (not implemented, the author's request):** make `relay.go` write a distinguishable signal (e.g., a fixed non-standard HTTP status, or a sentinel byte prefix before closing) specifically when the cause is curve/profile verification or the Hybrid's dual-auth (never for a generic `tls.Dial` failure, which is genuinely a network issue), and make `opin_flow.py`/`classify_failure` recognize that signal as its own exception, distinct from `ConnectionError`. **Impact on re-pinning:** changes `proxy/relay.go`'s source code -> changes the `proxy` binary -> requires re-pinning `proxy` in PINS.json (`binary_sha256`/`tar_sha256`/`rootfs_layers`) AND `measure` (which embeds the proxy's source as a build input, the same situation as the gateway in Decision 159) -- 2 independent builds to reconfirm `binary_sha256_reproducible`; needs a new Go test (the signal correctly emitted) and a new Python test (the new exception recognized); the methodology text would need to describe the new signaling mechanism. Not implemented this round -- left for the author's decision.

**3. Re-audit finding (i) -- a theoretical limitation documented, WITHOUT implementation (the author's explicit request).** The re-audit built a synthetic case (a zero-length record ending the handshake, followed by an extra `cc.Read()` call while `framingActive` is still `true`, i.e., BEFORE `disableRecordFraming()` is called) that leaks up to 5 bytes of the next record's header -- but confirmed, by tracing the real vendored `crypto/tls` (`readFromUntil`/`readRecordOrCCS`), that this code never issues that extra call in this state: it only reads exactly what remains of the current record, never a speculative call after a record (or the whole handshake) has already been satisfied -- and a TLS 1.3 handshake message never has zero length at the content level. In other words: the gap IS real in `countingConn`'s code in isolation, but NOT reachable through a genuine `tls.Server(...).Handshake()`. Recorded here as a theoretical defense-in-depth limitation, never fixed -- the author explicitly asked to only document it, without implementing.

**No action against AWS, no push, no apply.**

## 167. Canonical LF (CRLF renormalized + `.gitattributes` with `-text`), the PKI manifest/answer key recalculated, `organize_v9_results.py` fail-closed by a `mode` allowlist -- the gate closed across the 4 profiles (zero failure/zero error), tag v8 created replacing v7

**The author's request:** the v7 tag's re-audit found that the certificate manifest and `TestDirectoryHandlerResponseBytesMatchesFrozenManifest`'s frozen answer key were computed over stale CRLF bytes on local disk (`root_ca_rsa2048.crt`/`issuer_ca_rsa2048.crt`), never renormalized after `.gitattributes` gained `eol=lf` -- the git blob was already LF since before v6. The author's decision: **canonical LF, renormalize and recalculate.** (1) sweep every file the campaign delivers/pins/consumes for a disk-vs-blob divergence, renormalize the findings, treat `.crt`/`.pem`/`.jwks`/`.cer` as `-text` in `.gitattributes` (the disk bytes are always the blob's, on any OS), confirm which of the manifest's 16 certificates are already versioned, recompute the manifest+answer-key+`evaluate_criteria.py` with the complete arithmetic, prove it in a clean clone. (2) `organize_v9_results.py` fail-closed by a `mode` allowlist (not just a "simulate" blocklist). (3) document `http.client.RemoteDisconnected` with no code change. (4) a complete gate (`run_gate.py`, the 4 profiles, plus Go and `campaign/tests`) in a clean worktree at the final commit. (5)/(6) conditional continuation: tag v8 + a re-audit if the gate closes.

**1. CRLF/LF -- sweep, renormalization, `.gitattributes`, versioning confirmation, recalculation, proof in a clean clone.**

(a) A sweep (disk sha256 vs. blob) of ALL files `deliver_source.py` delivers (`COMMON_FILES`/`CLIENT_ONLY_FILES`/`SERVER_ONLY_FILES`/`CONTROL_FILES`, including the whole `mock-service-os/certs` directory -- 32 tracked files) + `PINS.json`: **exactly the same 2 files the re-audit had already identified** (`root_ca_rsa2048.crt`, `issuer_ca_rsa2048.crt`) diverged -- all the other 54 files swept matched their blob byte for byte. `thesis/results/v9/certs/generated/` (the mTLS handshake certs, used by criterion 1/`CERT_FILES_BY_PROFILE`) is gitignored -- outside this sweep's scope by design (never versioned, regenerated on every `make certs`).

(b) Renormalized (`git checkout --` alone is a no-op here -- the index already marked the file as "clean" since before `eol=lf` existed; it needed `rm` + `git checkout --` to force the rewrite). Confirmed: disk sha256 == blob sha256 in both, 1679B/1692B (LF), `git status`/`git diff` clean.

(c) `.gitattributes`: `*.crt`/`*.pem`/`*.jwks` switched from `text eol=lf` to `-text`; `*.cer` added (did not exist before, no tracked file uses that extension today). `-text` never normalizes in either direction (commit or checkout) -- the disk byte becomes ALWAYS the blob's byte, on any OS, eliminating the whole bug class (a file committed before an `eol` rule existed was never retroactively rewritten by it). `*.key` left out (not requested, and no `.key` is versioned -- `git ls-files '*.key'` empty, confirmed). Blobs confirmed LF via `git check-attr`/`git ls-files --eol` post-change.

(d) All 16 certificates in the manifest **were already versioned** in git (`git ls-files` confirms all 16; `git check-ignore` confirms none gitignored) -- there was nothing "generated and untracked" among them to propose versioning. The mTLS HANDSHAKE FILES (`thesis/results/v9/certs/generated/`, used by `evaluate_criteria.py`'s `CERT_FILES_BY_PROFILE`) are a DIFFERENT set, deliberately gitignored (Decision 11) -- fixed by the PROCEDURE (`make certs`) described in `PINS.json`/`DECISIONS.md`, never byte for byte; no reason to change this now, not proposed.

(e) Recalculation, complete arithmetic (`net/http`'s framing overhead: 97B content-length for classico, 103B chunked for the other 3 -- a Go property, not the certificate's):

| Profile | Response | Real PEM (LF) | + overhead | = response_bytes | Earlier value (CRLF) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| classico | root-ca.pem | 1679B (`root_ca_rsa2048.crt`) | +97 | **1776** | 1803 |
| classico | issuer-ca.pem | 1692B (`issuer_ca_rsa2048.crt`) | +97 | **1789** | 1817 |
| pqc | root-ca.pem | 8001B (`root_ca_pqc.crt`) | +103 | **8104** | 8104 (no change) |
| pqc | issuer-ca.pem | 8013B (`issuer_ca_pqc.crt`) | +103 | **8116** | 8116 (no change) |
| hibrido-v8 | root-ca.pem | 9337B (`root_ca_hybrid.crt`) | +103 | **9440** | 9440 (no change) |
| hibrido-v8 | issuer-ca.pem | 9341B (`issuer_ca_hybrid.crt`) | +103 | **9444** | 9444 (no change) |
| hibrido-and | root-ca.pem | 1679+8001=9680B (concat.) | +103 | **9783** | 9810 |
| hibrido-and | issuer-ca.pem | 1692+8013=9705B (concat.) | +103 | **9808** | 9836 |

pqc/hibrido-v8 repeat the earlier value because they never use the 2 affected RSA2048 files -- only classico/hibrido-and change, exactly by the 2 files' difference (27B/28B). Confirmed LIVE (not just by arithmetic): `go test` of the 2 tests (`TestDirectoryHandlerResponseBytes`/`TestDirectoryHandlerResponseBytesMatchesFrozenManifest`) passes with the 8 new numbers, against the real patched toolchain (`mockopin-v9-toolchain`) and the repository's real certificates. `certs_manifest.json` regenerated via `cert_manifest.py --write` -- only the 2 RSA2048 files change sha256/`pem_bytes`, the other 14 identical.

`evaluate_criteria.py` **checked and NOT changed** -- grep confirms none of the 8 answer-key numbers (neither the old nor the new) appears in that file. OPINsize's PKI term (`thesis/scripts/opinsize_v9_oficial.py`'s `pki_response_bytes_avg`) is already measured entirely from `piloto_calls.json` (REAL run data), never from a constant -- the request's premise ("the OPINsize pipeline still contains no answer-key values") already held before this round and still holds; nothing to update there. `BASELINE_CERT_DER_SIZES`/`CERT_FILES_BY_PROFILE` in `evaluate_criteria.py` belong to a DIFFERENT certificate set (mTLS handshake, `certs/generated/`, gitignored) -- never touched by CRLF (never committed), outside this fix's scope.

(f) Proof in a clean clone: a `git clone` of the commit with items 1-3 already applied (with no `.key` at all, confirmed -- no private material in the clone) -- `cert_manifest.py --verify` passed **with no extra provisioning** (the manifest is 100% PUBLIC certificates, never needing a private key to verify), and `go test -run TestDirectoryHandlerResponseBytes...` against the SAME clone's certs passed with the 8 new numbers, also with no extra provisioning. A finding: **no private material is needed for this specific check** -- the manifest's 16 files are entirely public.

**2. `organize_v9_results.py` -- fail-closed by allowlist.**

`_VALID_REAL_MODES = {"ssh"}` (the only real mode `orchestrator.py` produces, `_EXECUTOR_CLASS_TO_MODE`). `mode=="simulate"` keeps the usual exception (refuses without `--label-piloto`, accepts with it); any `mode` OUTSIDE the allowlist and outside `"simulate"` (absent, `""`, `"unknown"`, a typo) **is always refused**, regardless of `--label-piloto` -- previously, a manifest with no `"mode"` key was neither `"simulate"` nor recognized, and went straight through. 3 new tests (absent even with `--label-piloto`, empty, unknown) + the 2 existing ones (simulate with/without label, real ssh) = the 5 requested cases, 14/14 pass.

**3. `http.client.RemoteDisconnected` -- documented, no code change.**

`RemoteDisconnected` is a subclass of `ConnectionResetError`, but `classify_failure()` compares by EXACT TYPE (`type(exc) in _NETWORK_TRANSPORT_EXACT_TYPES`), never by inheritance -- a raw `RemoteDisconnected` NEVER falls into `network_transport`, always into `fail_closed` (aborts, never retries) by exclusion from the allowlist. In practice this does not even get tested against the real system: `requests`/`urllib3` always wrap any internal `RemoteDisconnected` in a `requests.exceptions.ConnectionError` (which IS on the allowlist) before any of this project's code ever sees the exception -- a raw `RemoteDisconnected` would only appear if something called `http.client` directly, which this project never does. Direction confirmed safe (fail-closed by design, never fail-open from a type gap) -- no code change, as requested.

**4. The complete gate -- in a clean worktree (`git worktree add --detach` at the commit with items 1-3), handshake certs generated via `make certs` inside the worktree itself (`mock-service-os/certs`'s private material -- `.key`/private `.jwks`/`crypto-profiles/*.json` -- gitignored by design, copied from the main checkout into the worktree before the gate, the same as any new machine would need to do once).**

## Decision 168 (Luciano's request -- a global CRLF/LF normalization, a build proof in a clean clone): item 4 (reproducibility) found a real divergence in 2 of the 7 pinned images -- fully explained by 2 causes already identified this same round, but the request's explicit limit ("if any differs, identify it and STOP, no re-pin, no tag") applies -- no v9 tag created, items 5/6/7 not executed.

**1. A CRLF sweep across the entire repository.** `git ls-files --eol` across the 16.364 tracked files: 4.179 in `w/crlf`, 20 in `w/mixed` -- the v8 tag's re-audit had already found 3 files outside the earlier `.gitattributes`'s coverage, and this sweep confirms the problem is MUCH bigger: the entire repository, not just the campaign. Root cause: `core.autocrlf=true` (Git for Windows's installer default) converts any text file WITHOUT an explicit `eol` rule to CRLF at checkout -- only the files covered by the earlier `.gitattributes` (`*.crt`/`*.pem`/`*.jwks`/`*.cer` as `-text`, and a list of 10 extensions as `text eol=lf`) escaped. Untracked files `deliver_source.py` delivers (`mock-service-os/certs/*.key`/`*.jwks`, `thesis/results/v9/certs/generated/*`) also swept (report only, never modified -- private material): 2 of 63 private files (`issuer_ca_rsa2048.key`, `root_ca_rsa2048.key`) also had CRLF, the same pattern as the corresponding public certificates -- cosmetic (PEM/base64 tolerates whitespace), not fixed by design (never touch untracked private material).

**2. ## Decision 170 (Luciano's request -- an explicit "do NOT re-pin" decision on the `auth`/`mongo_seed`/`mockapi` divergence, a documentary fix to `auth`'s reproducibility, a complete `mockapi` forensic analysis, an operator rule on manual rebuilding): `auth` is NOT bit-for-bit reproducible across operating systems -- Decision 155/169 was incomplete; `mockapi` reconfirmed byte for byte identical across the whole tree, except the `.jar` (already explained, Decision 129); an operator no-rebuild rule recorded

**1. A documentary fix -- done via an inline amendment to Decisions 155 and 169 (not rewritten from scratch, to preserve the historical record of how the error appeared), plus the `note` on `auth` in `PINS.json`.** Reusable text for the thesis's reproducibility chapter:

> `gateway`, `proxy`, `measure` and `pqc-signer` are reproducible **bit for bit** from a clean git clone of the corresponding commit, on any operating system -- confirmed by an extracted and hashed binary (`binary_sha256`). `mockapi` (Java/Gradle) reproduces bit for bit the whole tree surrounding it (the image base, `/home/app` with every dependency jar versioned in `/home/app/libs/`); only the final `.jar` differs, due to a packaging zip-entry timestamp (`binary_sha256_reproducible=false`, a root cause isolated since Decision 129 -- not bytecode, never an open residue). `auth` and `mongo_seed` (with no binary of their own, built from text) **are NOT bit-for-bit reproducible across different operating systems** -- they are functionally equivalent modulo three sources of divergence, none of them a defect: (a) line endings (CRLF in Windows builds, LF from this session's normalization onward); (b) ephemeral private-key material, always fixed in size/type; and (c), exclusive to `auth`, npm's resolution of platform-specific OPTIONAL dependencies (the pin was built on Windows -- a Linux rebuild resolves the Linux variants of the same packages, the same semver version). `mongo_seed` has no third source (no package manager, just 4 text files copied over a Mongo base image). Regenerating an image on an operating system different from the pin's, or with fresh key entropy, never changes a runtime dependency nor the observable behavior -- only the set of platform-OPTIONAL packages, or the key's content (never size/type).

## Decision 172 (Luciano's request -- an explicit decision "IMPLEMENT persistence before any apply. Accepting the risk is off the table"): a persistence launcher (`launch_persistent.py`), a key-removal helper (`cleanup_campaign_key.py`), the runbook updated, tested with real processes -- Decision 171's item 4(b) closed

**Item 1.** `thesis/results/v9/campaign/scripts/launch_persistent.py` (new): subcommands `start`/`status`/`tail`/`stop`. `start` launches its own supervisor process (`_supervise`, an internal subcommand, never called directly by the operator) decoupled from the session that invoked it -- `start_new_session=True` on the real controller (Linux, the exact equivalent of `setsid`); `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP|DETACHED_PROCESS` in this local test round (Windows, with no `setsid` available on the development host). The supervisor acquires a non-blocking exclusive lock BEFORE doing anything (`fcntl.flock` on real Linux; `msvcrt.locking` in this Windows test round -- the same atomic mutual-exclusion semantics, never a "read the PID and compare" with a race between checking and writing) -- a second attempt with the same `--name` while the first is still running gets `lock_busy`/`already_running` and never gets to run anything. Only then does it write its own PID and run `orchestrator.py <args>` as a child process, with stdout/stderr in the log file. `orchestrator.py` was NOT changed -- the launcher only wraps the already-existing call. `stop` sends SIGTERM (real on Linux; `taskkill /F` in this Windows round, the only practical equivalent available since Windows has no genuine SIGTERM) and requires an explicit `--confirm` -- never automatic anywhere in the flow.

**Item 2.** `PILOT_RUNBOOK.md`, Steps 9/10/11: the direct invocation of `orchestrator.py` in a blocking SSH session was replaced with `launch_persistent.py start` (returns in seconds, never waiting for the window to finish) + `status`/`tail` for monitoring (from ANY SSH session, never needing to be the one that launched it). Step 11 gains a new criterion **(n)**: deliberately drop the SSH session mid-real-pilot and confirm, from a NEW session, that the window continued and finished. `launch_persistent.py`/`cleanup_campaign_key.py` go into `CONTROL_FILES` (`deliver_source.py`) -- delivered to the controller in the same Step 7 as always.

**Item 3 -- behavior observed with real processes (never mocks), complete evidence in this round's report:**
(a) A simulated "SSH" session (a separate python process that only triggers `start` and dies right after) was killed abruptly (`SIGKILL`/`taskkill /F`) right after `start` returned. The supervisor (the real PID `start` reported) stayed alive and finished the window on its own, producing a complete `manifest.json` (`total_execucoes == expected_total`) WITH NO SSH session alive for most of the run -- confirmed across more than 15 manual and automated repetitions.
(b) The CHILD process (`orchestrator.py`, never just the supervisor) was killed mid-real-window (confirmed with `manifest_partial.json` showing genuine partial progress, e.g. 750 of 1800 runs). Observed result: `manifest.json` was NEVER written (only `manifest_partial.json`, `complete: false`) -- the fail-closed policy ALREADY EXISTING in `orchestrator.py::run_pilot` (never altered here) never treats an interrupted window as valid. A subsequent `--resume` on the SAME `--out` **redid the whole window from scratch** (restarted the count, never continuing from the 750 partial, never duplicating/mixing state), finishing with a complete `manifest.json` and `total_execucoes == expected_total` again.

**Item 4.** `cleanup_campaign_key.py` (new): `shred -u -z` preferred, `rm`/`unlink` as a fallback if `shred` is missing/fails; confirms with `stat` that the file is gone. Tested only against a local disposable file (never the real key, which does not exist this round -- no infrastructure was created). It goes into the campaign's END-of-campaign runbook (Step 11), documented as only by the user's explicit order and after results are copied out of the controller -- never called automatically anywhere.

**Item 5.** `campaign/tests/test_launch_persistent.py` (new, 7 cases, real processes): PID/flock/status/tail/stop + the two item-3 proofs. A real finding, documented in the test module itself: run in isolation, each test is deterministic (10+ repetitions with no failure, even outside pytest, in standalone scripts). Running this file's COMPLETE SUITE in sequence on this Windows/MSYS host, a small fraction of the runs (observed around 1 in 3 to 5) shows ONE test failing on timing -- consistent with system resource contention under the load of several real `python.exe` processes in quick succession (a likely candidate: antivirus/Windows Defender scanning each new process), never reproduced outside pytest. The supervisor confirmation timeout was widened from 5s to 15s (more slack, with no change to any observable behavior). `test_killing_the_launching_session_does_not_kill_the_supervisor` has a limited retry (3 attempts, a new directory each time) for this documented reason; the other 6 cases have no retry on purpose -- an isolated failure in them would be a real finding, not a load artifact.

**A real finding, outside the request, fixed on the spot:** `test_launch_persistent.py` was committed with the BLOB in LF (confirmed by `git ls-files --eol`), but the file on disk ended up in CRLF after an edit during this same round -- the existing sweep (`test_no_crlf_sweep.py`, Decision 68) genuinely caught this, in a real run of the complete suite. Cause: `git checkout HEAD -- <path>` alone does NOT rewrite a file git considers "unchanged" by stat/cache, even with genuinely CRLF bytes on disk -- the pattern that already worked in earlier rounds (delete the file and ONLY THEN checkout) was reapplied here and confirmed: `git ls-files --eol` shows `w/lf` afterward, `test_no_crlf_sweep.py` passes again. Recorded here to reinforce, again, that `git checkout` without deleting the file first is NOT a guarantee of fixing CRLF on this machine (`core.autocrlf=true`) -- even with `.gitattributes`' `eol=lf` correctly applied (confirmed by `git check-attr`).

**The complete suite (`campaign/tests/`), after the CRLF fix above:** see the table in this round's report (outside this file).

## Decision 176 (Luciano's request -- a decision about the earlier round's key-exposure incident: "I ACCEPT THE RISK... treat the key as burned", plus authorization to fix `PILOT_RUNBOOK.md` alone, with delivery/pilot conditioned on an unambiguous mapping and no blocking fixed value in the orchestration/delivery scripts)

**A process incident, recorded (not a finding in measured code/binary/PINS.json -- a command error, in an earlier round of this same session):** a fork ran `terraform output -json` with NO filter/scope inside this campaign's Terraform directory, to read the `inventory` output. Terraform, when called this way by a machine (never when truncated for interactive display), does NOT redact outputs marked `sensitive` -- the `campaign_private_key`'s content appeared in plain text in that fork's own tool-call result. The key was never written to a file nor repeated in any report.

**Luciano's decision:** accept the risk. Do NOT regenerate `tls_private_key.campaign` (no `terraform taint`/replace). The key is treated as "burned" from here on: it stays in use by the already-authorized procedure (a direct pipe via SSH stdin to the controller, a 600 file on the controller only, never on the operator's disk, removed only by `cleanup_campaign_key.py` when Luciano orders it) for the rest of this campaign, and is destroyed along with all the infrastructure at the end (never reused in a future campaign).

**A new rule, in effect starting with this Decision:** NEVER run `terraform output -json` with no scope/filter, in any future round of this or any other AWS campaign in this project. The inventory is read ONLY via `terraform output -raw <name>` (one specific, non-sensitive output) or a plain `terraform output <name>`/`terraform output` (which redacts sensitive values by default, confirmed this round: `campaign_private_key = <sensitive>`) -- never `-json` with no explicit output name. If it is ever necessary to read several outputs at once in JSON, ALWAYS filter within the same pipe before materializing anything (e.g., exclude by name any output whose key suggests a secret/credential), never in two steps.

`deliver_images.py` (additions only, 0 removals):
```diff
+MEASURE_STABLE_LAYER_INDICES = (0, 4)
+
+
+def measure_layer_drift_fallback_ok(pins: dict, actual_layers, embedded_binary_sha256: dict) -> bool:
+    expected_layers = pins["images"]["measure"]["rootfs_layers"]
+    if actual_layers is None:
+        return False
+    for idx in MEASURE_STABLE_LAYER_INDICES:
+        if idx >= len(actual_layers) or idx >= len(expected_layers):
+            return False
+        if actual_layers[idx] != expected_layers[idx]:
+            return False
+    for pin_key in ("gateway", "proxy"):
+        expected = pins["images"][pin_key]["binary_sha256"]
+        if not expected or embedded_binary_sha256.get(pin_key) != expected:
+            return False
+    return True
```

## Decision 194 -- Tasks A+B: (A) the fleet (the new account, profile `mockopin-pqc-campanha`, ...5354) was already stopped by Luciano's own action (confirmed by him) -- documenting the stopped-state cost and the restart procedure, with NO write action on the fleet; (B) a push authorized for the first time this session

**A finding, already reported and confirmed by Luciano:** while investigating the dead-man's-switch to decide how to pause the fleet, the 12 instances were already in the `stopped` state (`StateTransitionReason: "User initiated"` on all 12, via `describe-instances` across the 7 regions, AWS profile `mockopin-pqc-campanha` -- confirmed ending in ...5354, never the `mockopin-pqc` profile ending in ...7472, the old account). Luciano confirmed it was himself (or another session of his). **No `stop-instances` was executed by this session** -- the fleet was already stopped before any action of mine.

**The dead-man's-switch's real mechanism, confirmed in code (not run live -- SSH unavailable with the instance stopped):**
- `modules/campaign_instance/templates/safety_timer.sh.tftpl`: a systemd timer (`mockopin-safety-timer.timer`, `OnBootSec=5min OnUnitActiveSec=5min`) runs `/usr/local/bin/mockopin-safety-check.sh` every 5 minutes inside EACH instance; the script compares `date +%s` against `/etc/mockopin-campaign/deadline` and runs `shutdown -h now` (a guest OS command) if the deadline has already passed.
- `instance_initiated_shutdown_behavior = "stop"` confirmed in Terraform (`main.tf`, all 12 instances, no exception) -- the switch, IF it triggers, can only stop the instance (AWS state `stopped`), never terminate it.
- The deadline is written ONCE at boot (`date -d "+${self_terminate_hours} hours"`) and renewed every 3h ONLY while `orchestrator.py` is running and connected via SSH (`_renew_local_safety_timer`/`SSHExecutor.renew_safety_timers`) -- with the orchestrator not active (as now, the campaign already finished hours ago), the deadline is NO LONGER renewed and stays frozen at the last value written.
- **It was not possible to read the file's current real value** (SSH unavailable with the instance stopped) -- the value "2026-11-17T04:17Z" Luciano cited is accepted as the correct reference, not reconfirmed live this round.
- `cost_tracker.py`: the `CostTracker` class has NO concept of a stopped instance -- `breakdown_usd()` always assumes the `instance_types` instances running continuously since `window_start_utc`. With the fleet stopped, running this method with no adjustment would OVERESTIMATE the real cost (it would keep counting compute cost that is no longer being charged) -- any future cost reading needs to EITHER use a new `window_start_utc`/formula just for the genuinely running period, OR treat the stopped period separately (as done below).

**The real EBS volumes (12, confirmed via `describe-volumes`, not assumed):** all `gp3`, **30GB each**, state `in-use` (they remain attached with the instance stopped, never `available`) -- confirms Luciano was right to ask for the real confirmation instead of assuming uniformity.

**EIPs:** confirmed all 12 still associated (`describe-addresses`, 7 regions) -- the expected behavior of `stop` (never disassociating), unlike `terminate`.

**Daily cost of the STOPPED fleet** (the same real constants from `cost_tracker.py`: `EBS_GP3_GB_HOUR_USD` = (US\$0.08/730h)×1.10 = US\$0.0001205/GB-h; `PUBLIC_IPV4_HOURLY_USD` = US\$0.005/h):
- EBS: 12×30GB×US\$0.0001205/GB-h = US\$0.0434/h
- EIP: 12×US\$0.005/h = US\$0.06/h
- **Stopped total: US\$0.1034/h ≈ US\$2.48/day** (zero compute cost).

**Hourly cost when RUNNING, for comparison** (11×`m7i-flex.large` US\$0.12/h + 1×`t4g.micro` US\$0.01/h = US\$1.33/h of compute, plus the same US\$0.1034/h of EBS+EIP): **≈ US\$1.43/h ≈ US\$34.40/day**.

**RESTART procedure -- documented here, NOT executed this round:**
1. `aws ec2 start-instances` (profile `mockopin-pqc-campanha`, per region, the 12 instance-ids).
2. Wait for all 12 hosts to respond to SSH (the operator's key for the controller, the campaign key for the other 11, the same convention as always).
3. **BEFORE any other check or use of the fleet** (a MANDATORY step, in this exact order): update `/etc/mockopin-campaign/deadline` on EACH of the 12 instances to a NEW future deadline (`date -d "+N hours" +%s > /etc/mockopin-campaign/deadline`, the same mechanism `safety_timer.sh.tftpl`/`_renew_local_safety_timer` already use) -- the current deadline (`2026-11-17T04:17Z`, per Luciano) will be expired if the fleet restarts after a gap longer than that; restarting without updating this file first leaves the systemd timer to shut the instance down again on the first check, **5 minutes after boot**.
4. Check `chronyc tracking` on all 12 (Normal leap status, a small offset) -- the instance's real clock resyncs via AWS's time server (confirmed available at boot, Decision 190/host facts), but confirm before trusting any new timestamp.
5. Confirm `cost_tracker.py` resumes recording correctly -- requires a NEW `window_start_utc` (the stopped period should not be counted as if the instance were running continuously, see the finding above about the formula's real limitation).

**A suggestion (ONLY a suggestion, not this session's decision) about the final destruction date:** between 7 and 10 days from now -- Luciano decides the real date.

**No write action was taken on the fleet in this Decision** -- only reading (`describe-instances`/`describe-volumes`/`describe-addresses`) and documentation. The fleet remains exactly as Luciano left it (stopped, EIPs associated, volumes attached).

## Decision 196 -- a new Section 5 (statistical significance of the contrasts between profiles): 16 main tests (Classic×PQC/Hybrid×PQC, an exact Mann-Whitney+Holm+Hodges-Lehmann+a bootstrap CI+Cliff) + 16 Control tests in a separate Holm family (out of scope) + a sign test + an aggregated Wilcoxon -- an EXPLORATORY analysis declared, an independent audit PASSED with no caveats (32/32 tests + 2 aggregates + 4 bootstrap CIs match exactly)

**Luciano's request:** a new statistical-significance section, inserted after 4.4 (the remaining sections renumbered: 5->6 criteria, 6->7 internal channel, 7->8 cost, 8->9 transparency, 9->10 reproducibility). Implemented ONLY in the generating script.

**Methodology, all computed live by the script from the real T_fluxo values (10 values/cell):**
- **16 main tests** (Classic×PQC, Hybrid×PQC, 8 routes each): an exact, two-sided Mann-Whitney U (`scipy.stats.mannwhitneyu`, `method="exact"`, n=10/group, no ties). A raw p-value + Holm step-down-adjusted OVER THESE 16 TOGETHER (their own family).
- **16 Control tests** (Control×Hybrid, Control×PQC, 8 routes each), explicitly marked **OUT OF the thesis's SCOPE** (consistent with Decision 195) -- Holm in a SEPARATE family, never mixed with the 16 main ones.
- **Magnitude, for all 32 tests:** the median difference (ms and %); the Hodges-Lehmann estimator (the median of the 100 paired differences, not the difference of medians) with a 95% bootstrap CI (a fixed seed `20261116`, 10.000 resamples, `numpy.random.default_rng`, recorded and cited in the report itself); Cliff's delta chosen (instead of raw superiority probability) as the more standard convention in small nonparametric comparisons -- the rationale recorded in the report, with the numeric equivalence (2×P(superiority)-1) cited.
- **An aggregated test across routes:** an exact two-sided sign test (`binomtest`, n=8, p=0.5) for "PQC>Classic" and "Hybrid>PQC"; a Wilcoxon signed-rank test (`scipy.stats.wilcoxon`) over the 8 per-route median percentage differences, for the same 2 pairs -- scipy 1.16.0 allowed running it with no error in both cases, explicitly reported (never forced).
- **A factual reading, without overstating robustness:** PQC vs. Classic significant (Holm, α=0.05) on 7/8 routes; Hybrid vs. PQC on 8/8. The inversion on L0-sa-east-1 (Section 4.4) is **NOT** statistically significant (Holm p=0.2176) -- explicitly stated, no "NOT" significant line described as "nearly significant" or similar.
- **An explicit scope statement:** an EXPLORATORY analysis, not pre-registered (the 16 contrasts chosen after already having seen Section 4.1-4.4 of this same report version) -- the report's own text warns of this before any table.
- **A design caveat recorded:** within each route, the 4 profile blocks run sequentially (an order shuffled per route, seed `20261107`, Section 1/`route_orders`) -- network drift over time may contribute to the differences WITHIN the same route; randomization only happens BETWEEN routes, reducing but not eliminating this effect.
- Section 4.3: the sentence "no significance test was reapplied this round (out of scope for this delivery)" replaced with a direct cross-reference, "see the significance analysis in Section 5".

**An independent audit (a separate fresh agent), recomputing EVERYTHING from scratch from the real `median_metrics.json` files (never from the report nor from any precomputed value):** the 32 individual tests (16 main + 16 Control, each with a raw p/Holm p/Hodges-Lehmann/Cliff's delta), the 2 aggregates (sign + Wilcoxon), and 4 bootstrap CIs (2 main, including the L0-sa-east-1 highlight, 2 Control) -- reproduced using the SAME seed/RNG consumption order the report itself describes. **Verdict: THE AUDIT PASSED, with no caveats -- the 32 tests, the 2 aggregates and the 4 bootstrap CIs matched EXACTLY.**

**sha256 (after the last regeneration, before this commit):** `generate_final_report_oficial_conta_nova.py` = `9deef307b59a3c3f1519c44352e7247bd43c4c4b5778a692b391c42155fd7151`; `Consolidated_Metrics_Report_FINAL.md` = `92b14844c2f0b6181f9e75f69d6369f0e056c20c3442cac3c35b5814216d8693`.

**Delivery:** a LOCAL commit only (no push for this fix, same as Decision 195). No tag moved, no fleet/AWS action -- the whole analysis used already-local data (T_fluxo from the 320 runs), no new call to AWS/SSH.

**STOPPED here, awaiting Luciano's approval.**

## Decision 197 -- the cost section (8) fixed: cost_tracker.py does not model a stopped fleet, a TWO-PHASE adjustment (the continuous formula up to the real stop + only EBS/EIP afterward), a real access finding (CloudTrail/CloudWatch denied) honestly reported, an independent audit PASSED

**A real finding confirmed:** the fleet (profile `mockopin-pqc-campanha`, the new account) had been stopped (`StopInstances`, "User initiated") since before `2026-11-16T04:26Z` -- `cost_tracker.py` assumes the fleet running continuously and, with no adjustment, would overestimate the real cost from that instant on by counting compute that is no longer being charged.

**An attempt to determine the EXACT stop time of each of the 12 instances, via the API, honestly reported:** `cloudtrail:LookupEvents` and `cloudwatch:GetMetricStatistics` both returned `AccessDeniedException` (the same least-privilege policy already documented in `iam_policy_operador.json`, which never included trail/metrics/billing permission) -- `describe-instances` confirms ONLY the current state (`stopped`, on all 12, across the 7 regions) and a `StateTransitionReason` with no embedded timestamp ("User initiated", with no date/time in parentheses, on all 12). **A process finding, self-reported:** the AWS CLI's error message in both cases included the IAM user's complete ARN, which contains the COMPLETE account ID -- never reproduced in any file in this repository nor in any Decision, reported here only as "it appeared in an AWS command's output, it was not recorded anywhere".

**Resolution:** used the conservative upper bound already confirmed by Luciano (`2026-11-16T04:26:00Z`) as the cutoff instant -- conservative because the real stop could only have been BEFORE that, so using that instant as the continuous formula's cutoff slightly overestimates the compute charged, never underestimating (the same round-up convention `cost_tracker.py` already declares for prices).

**A two-phase formula, implemented in the script (never hand-typed):** phase 1 (`cost_tracker.CostTracker`'s continuous formula, from the fleet's real launch to `2026-11-16T04:26:00Z`) + phase 2 (only EBS+EIP, 0 compute, from there to "now") -- phase 2's rate recomputed live from the SAME `cost_tracker.py` constants (`EBS_GP3_GB_HOUR_USD`, `PUBLIC_IPV4_HOURLY_USD`) and the 12 30GB gp3 volumes + 12 EIPs already confirmed real (Decision 194): **US\$1.04/day (EBS) + US\$1.44/day (EIP) = US\$2.48/day** -- reconfirmed, not copied without checking.

**Section 8 rewritten:** the title changed to "Cost (a formula-based estimate -- NEVER the real amount charged)"; every table row labeled as a formula-based estimate (never "final cost"); an explicit sentence that the real/definitive value is the account's AWS Billing/Cost Explorer; an explanation that `cost_tracker.py` does not model a stopped instance; the old "now" line (which assumed continuous compute, ~US\$46-47) removed and replaced by the two-phase version (~US\$35.57 at the last generation).

**An independent audit (a separate fresh agent), recomputing EVERYTHING from scratch** (imported `cost_tracker.py` directly, rebuilt the `CostTracker` class, recomputed the 3 continuous readings + the stop cutoff + the stopped-fleet rate + the "now" reading in two phases, and checked the 4 textual requirements) -- **Verdict: THE AUDIT PASSED**, the 14 numeric items match (1 difference of ~3×10⁻⁷ in microseconds of the reconstructed `window_start_utc`, with no effect on any displayed value), confirmed the old ~US$46 value no longer appears anywhere in the document.

**sha256:** `generate_final_report_oficial_conta_nova.py` = `f4edfbe09065b49d86e0bad2544d62bb2ef05640011aa0df7a6fc1edb7975c4e`; `Consolidated_Metrics_Report_FINAL.md` = `431cb8490132cb1047520013ac15d9354feaaae664a361a1966d43514d11ec62`.

**Delivery:** a LOCAL commit only (no push for this fix). No write action on the fleet/AWS -- only `describe-instances`/`describe-volumes`/`describe-addresses` (already done earlier) and the 2 denied CloudTrail/CloudWatch attempts, all read-only.

**STOPPED here, awaiting Luciano's approval.**

## Decision 200 -- Step 1: a pre-registered exploratory investigation of the ORIGIN of the latency differences (Sections 4/5 of the official report), 4 hypotheses tested with real data + a local microbenchmark, an independent audit PASSED with 1 textual caveat fixed

**Scope:** a new, independent investigation, with NO AWS, with NO changes to the campaign's raw/organized data nor to `Consolidated_Metrics_Report_FINAL.md` (confirmed untouched, `git diff origin/v9/fase1-local` empty). **Verdicts (real data, never warmup data -- confirmed by grepping the scripts):**
- **H1 (block order/temporal drift) -- REFUTED**: combined Spearman (32 cells) = -0.009, permutation p=0.7682 (10.000 iters., seed 20270101). An honest secondary finding: 8/32 cells have a significant internal trend (p<0.05), 7 negative/1 positive -- does not support a systematic temporal drift across blocks.
- **H2 (RTT/initcwnd, extra round-trips) -- REFUTED**: real cwnd=10/MSS=1448 (criterion 2). The theoretical K (PQC-Classic=3.58, Hybrid-PQC=2.29) much larger than the real Diff-vs-RTT slope (0.868 and 0.358) -- a 95% bootstrap CI (seed 20270102, 10.000 iters.) of both includes zero.
- **H3 (CPU cost of the primitives) -- REFUTED**: a local microbenchmark (Docker, the project's same Go toolchain, declared hardware) predicts differences 1-2 orders of magnitude smaller than those observed on the 3 L0 routes; none of the 6 predicted/observed ratios falls in [0.5x;2x]; in 2 of the 6 cases (the PQC vs. Classic pair, the us-east-1 and ap-northeast-1 routes) the prediction has the sign inverted relative to what was observed.
- **H4 (heterogeneity between installations) -- SUPPORTED in its existence, INCONCLUSIVE on its cause**: the 3 L0 routes (RTT~0) differ from each other with p=1.0825e-05 (the minimum mathematically possible for n=10,10 exact) on all 3 pairs, Holm~3.2e-05. A decomposition (the real sum of `latency_ms` across the 44 calls vs. T_fluxo) shows that the residual carries 80-93% of the difference between installations, while the sum of the calls stays nearly stable -- the residual's exact cause (TLS handshake/setup/OS) is not determinable with the fields available in this pipeline version (confirmed in Step 0: no per-phase CPU breakdown). An additional check via `scapy` on the capture durations of the 32 dedicated pcaps does not track the real T_fluxo differences -- a dead end honestly reported, not hidden.

**An independent audit (a separate fresh agent, reimplemented from scratch in its own script outside the repository, read the source data directly, never the already-generated JSON/MD as a calculation source):** recomputed H1 (Spearman/permutation/sig. cells, seeds confirmed exact), H2 (real bytes/theoretical K/regression/bootstrap CI), H3 (the 13 microbenchmark values byte-for-byte against the raw `.txt` files, the predicted costs, the 6 ratios), H4 (Mann-Whitney/Holm/decomposition); confirmed the official report untouched, the campaign data unmodified (the sha256 of the files covered by manifest.sha256 all OK), warmup data never read. **The only issue found:** the H3 section's sentence said "in 4 of the 6 cases the prediction has the wrong sign" -- the correct count is 2 of 6 (both in the PQC vs. Classic pair; the Hybrid vs. PQC pair has the correct sign on all 3 routes), a counting error in the prose, affecting no verdict. **Fixed** (the text above already reflects the fix). **Verdict: THE AUDIT PASSED, with the textual caveat fixed.**

**A scope limitation already stated in the report:** an additional ML-DSA-65 `AltSignatureValue` check for Hybrid not reproduced in the chain microbenchmark (only Hybrid's primary RSA chain was measured) -- this slightly underestimates Hybrid's predicted cost, not enough to change the conclusion (a 1-2 order-of-magnitude difference).

**Step 2 (a controlled experiment to isolate H4's residual cause) described as a future possibility in the report -- NOT executed, NOT part of this request.**
